abstract: ArXiv:2607.07044v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We report an improved absolute frequency measurement of the [MATH]Lu[MATH] optical frequency standard, evaluated via a remote link to the NRC-FCs2 caesium fountain primary frequency standard. Operating a single ion clock with 94.2% uptime over 10 days, and using an ambiguity-resolved precise point positioning (PPP-AR) link over the Global Positioning System (GPS), we determine an absolute frequency of [MATH]Hz at a fractional uncertainty of [MATH]. This agrees with our previous result, which underpins the CIPM recommended frequency value, and reduces the uncertainty by a factor of 3.6.
tldr: This paper reports an improved absolute frequency measurement of a 176Lu+ optical clock with reduced uncertainty, using a GPS link to a caesium fountain primary standard.
motivation: Optical frequency standards require precise absolute frequency measurements to support redefinition of the SI second and improve timekeeping.
method: A single 176Lu+ ion clock was operated with 94.2% uptime over 10 days, and its frequency was compared to the NRC-FCs2 caesium fountain via an ambiguity-resolved precise point positioning (PPP-AR) GPS link.
result: The absolute frequency was determined with a fractional uncertainty of 2.6×10^{-16}, a factor of 3.6 improvement over the previous measurement.
conclusion: The measurement agrees with the previous result and reduces uncertainty, supporting the CIPM recommended frequency value.

title: Quantum Recurrence Plot Algorithm Based On Quantum Principal Component Analysis
authors: Hanhuai Zhu, Jingjing Huang, Zhi-Xi Wang, Shao-Ming Fei
abstract: ArXiv:2607.07056v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Recurrence Plot (RP) is a method employed to analyze the periodicity, chaoticity, and nonlinear characteristics of complex systems. Quantum Principal Component Analysis (QPCA), on the other hand, achieves dimensionality reduction of sample data using density matrices based on quantum circuits. We improve the distance threshold function of the recurrence plot algorithm using a density operator conceptually equivalent to the covariance matrix, integrate it with quantum circuits, and thereby develop a Quantum Recurrence Plot (QRP) algorithm. This algorithm achieves ultra-high efficiency in parallel computing, reduces computational costs, and simultaneously upgrades the traditional grayscale recurrence plot to colored heatmaps, enabling a better revelation of the system's dynamical characteristics.
tldr: This paper proposes a quantum algorithm for recurrence plots using quantum principal component analysis, but it does not align with the user's research directions.
motivation: Recurrence plots are used to analyze dynamical systems, and the authors aim to speed up the computation using quantum algorithms.
method: The distance threshold function in recurrence plots is replaced with a density operator from QPCA, and the algorithm is implemented on quantum circuits.
result: The quantum recurrence plot algorithm achieves parallel computing efficiency and produces colored heatmaps instead of grayscale plots.
conclusion: The work presents a quantum-enhanced version of a classical data analysis tool, but it lacks a clear connection to quantum information theory, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid systems.

title: Hamiltonian Reduction From Particular Integrals
authors: R. Azuaje, A. M. Escobar-Ruiz, I. Gutierrez-Sagredo
abstract: ArXiv:2607.07057v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop a geometric reduction mechanism generated by particular integrals. A family of functions whose time derivatives close linearly on the same family defines an invariant zero-level submanifold. In the Hamiltonian case, if this family is in involution, the restricted dynamics is presymplectic, and its characteristic quotient carries a reduced Hamiltonian flow. This yields a direct bridge between particular integrals, presymplectic reduction, and lower-dimensional Hamiltonian dynamics, and leads to a Liouville-type notion of particular integrability. We illustrate the framework through mechanical examples and lift constructions, including variants of the Eisenhart lift.
tldr: This paper develops a geometric reduction mechanism based on particular integrals in Hamiltonian systems, linking them to presymplectic reduction and lower-dimensional dynamics.
motivation: The authors aim to generalize the concept of integrability by using particular integrals to reduce Hamiltonian systems, providing a geometric framework that connects particular integrals to presymplectic reduction.
method: They define a family of functions whose time derivatives close linearly on the same family, forming an invariant zero-level submanifold. For Hamiltonian systems with involutive families, the restricted dynamics is presymplectic, and the characteristic quotient yields a reduced Hamiltonian flow.
result: The framework yields a Liouville-type notion of particular integrability and is illustrated through mechanical examples and lift constructions, including variants of the Eisenhart lift.
conclusion: The work establishes a direct bridge between particular integrals, presymplectic reduction, and lower-dimensional Hamiltonian dynamics, offering a new perspective on integrability.

title: Near-Optimal Lower Bounds On One-Bit Compressed Sensing Of Approximately Sparse Signals
authors: Junren Chen, Arya Mazumdar, Ming Yuan
abstract: ArXiv:2607.06750v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper provides the first near-optimal lower bounds for one-bit compressed sensing of approximately sparse signals lying in a scaled [MATH] ball, which is a commonly adopted relaxation of the exactly [MATH]-sparse assumption. In prior works, the best known upper bounds on uniform Euclidean error are of order [MATH], where [MATH] is the number of measurements. Under sub-Gaussian matrices, we establish nearly matching lower bounds for both the canonical one-bit compressed sensing model and the uniformly dithered model. Our argument is to first embed a small Euclidean ball into the signal set, which is straightforward for the dithered model but relies on a lifting map for the canonical model, and then construct two signals in this small ball that are separated in Euclidean distance by at least [MATH] (up to logarithmic factor) but are indistinguishable from the binary measurements. Moreover, our argument extends to approximately sparse signals that live in a properly scaled [MATH] ball [MATH], yielding a lower bound [MATH] that smoothly bridges the cases of exact sparsity ([MATH]) and [MATH] sparsity ([MATH]). Finally, we discuss the extensions of our lower bounds to sub-Weibull matrices, adversarial bit flipping, matrix recovery, and characterize the transition to the non-sparse case.
tldr: This paper provides near-optimal lower bounds for one-bit compressed sensing of approximately sparse signals.
motivation: One-bit compressed sensing is a signal processing technique, not directly related to quantum information theory or quantum thermodynamics.
method: The authors embed a small Euclidean ball into the signal set and construct indistinguishable signals to derive lower bounds.
result: They establish nearly matching lower bounds for both canonical and uniformly dithered one-bit compressed sensing models.
conclusion: The work advances compressed sensing theory but does not connect to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Mathematical Methods Of Reinforcement Learning
authors: Denis Belomestny, Alexander Gasnikov, Egor Gladin, Alexey Naumov, Artemy Rubtsov, Yuri Sapronov, Daniil Tiapkin, Nikita Yudin
abstract: ArXiv:2607.06935v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) is increasingly grounded in tools from probability, optimization, and operator theory. This survey organizes the mathematical structures that underpin the design and analysis of modern algorithms in RL. We begin from Markov decision processes (MDPs) and the Bellman operators, emphasizing contraction mappings, monotonicity, and fixed-point theory that yield convergence guarantees and rates for value and policy iteration, and temporal-difference schemes. We then develop the optimization perspective: stochastic approximation and martingale methods, convex duality and the role of regularization linking mirror/proximal methods. Function approximation is treated through linear and non-linear settings, covering stabilization, error decomposition, and sample-complexity via concentration inequalities for dependent data and mixing processes. We further cover off-policy evaluation/learning, constrained RL and constrained MDPs (CMDPs). Throughout we unify algorithmic templates under common operator and variational lenses, highlighting both finite-sample bounds and asymptotic results. Our presentation is intended to provide a unified mathematical entry point for researchers in probability, optimization, and statistics interested in reinforcement learning.
tldr: A survey of mathematical methods in reinforcement learning, focusing on Markov decision processes, Bellman operators, optimization, and function approximation.
motivation: Reinforcement learning increasingly relies on tools from probability, optimization, and operator theory; this survey aims to provide a unified mathematical entry point for researchers.
method: The paper organizes mathematical structures underlying RL algorithms, covering contraction mappings, fixed-point theory, stochastic approximation, convex duality, and concentration inequalities.
result: It presents a comprehensive overview of algorithmic templates and theoretical guarantees, including finite-sample bounds and asymptotic results.
conclusion: The survey serves as a mathematical foundation for RL, but does not directly contribute to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid systems.

title: Noncommutative Vector Field Calculi
authors: Rita Fioresi, Emanuele Latini, Thomas Weber
abstract: ArXiv:2607.07243v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We discuss noncommutative differential geometry from a vector field centric point of view. This is based on the notion of first order vector field calculus (FOVC), which has been previously introduced by Borowiec under the name Cartan pair. We define the universal FOVC and construct an adjunction between the categories of FOVC and that of first order differential calculi, showing that the vector field approach is dual, though not equivalent, to the differential form one. This correspondence is then extended to covariant vector field and differential calculi. On Hopf algebras, (bi)covariant FOVC are in bijection with (bicovariant) quantum tangent spaces. For Hopf--Galois extensions, quantum tangent spaces give rise to vertical vector fields and in this setup we further describe base vector fields and horizontal vector fields and show that they are related via a noncommutative Atiyah sequence. Multiple examples, based on braided derivations, finite groups and the quantum Hopf fibration, are given. The vector field approach is further enriched by a sheaf-theoretic treatment, which recovers the former as a local, or affine, picture.
tldr: This paper develops a noncommutative vector field calculus based on first order vector field calculi and their adjunction with differential calculi, with applications to Hopf algebras and Hopf–Galois extensions.
motivation: To provide a vector field-centric approach to noncommutative differential geometry that is dual but not equivalent to the differential form approach, and to extend this to covariant calculi and quantum tangent spaces.
method: The authors define the universal first order vector field calculus (FOVC), construct an adjunction between categories of FOVC and first order differential calculi, and extend the correspondence to covariant calculi. They also study (bi)covariant FOVC on Hopf algebras and vertical/horizontal vector fields on Hopf–Galois extensions via a noncommutative Atiyah sequence.
result: They establish a duality between vector field and differential form calculi, show that (bi)covariant FOVC correspond to quantum tangent spaces, and describe vertical and horizontal vector fields in Hopf–Galois extensions.
conclusion: The vector field calculus provides a complementary framework to differential calculi in noncommutative geometry, with rich structure on Hopf algebras and quantum principal bundles.

title: Blockchain Attacks And Defenses: A Layered And Cross-Domain Survey
authors: Na Ruan Junjie Hu
abstract: ArXiv:2607.06593v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Blockchains have evolved from simple distributed ledgers into programmable platforms that process complex application logic and carry significant financial value. All modern Web3 systems share a common goal: providing secure, decentralized, and trustworthy execution in an increasingly interconnected environment. However, this evolution has shifted the attack surface from isolated infrastructure disruptions to programmable economic abuse and cross-domain exploits. In this article, we focus on the research of blockchain attacks and defenses. In particular, we categorize the threat landscape and corresponding mitigation strategies according to both a four-tier layered architecture (network, cryptographic, consensus, and application) and cross-domain trust boundaries. We seek to answer these important questions: How has the research in blockchain security evolved over the past decade, especially with the rise of decentralized finance (DeFi) and cross-chain interoperability? How do local security assumptions fail when protocols are composed, and what are the driving needs for Web3 security research in the future?
tldr: A comprehensive survey of blockchain attacks and defenses across network, cryptographic, consensus, and application layers, with a focus on DeFi and cross-chain interoperability.
motivation: Blockchain systems have evolved into programmable platforms carrying significant financial value, but this has expanded the attack surface to include economic abuse and cross-domain exploits. The paper aims to categorize the threat landscape and mitigation strategies to guide future Web3 security research.
method: The authors categorize blockchain attacks and defenses using a four-tier layered architecture (network, cryptographic, consensus, application) and cross-domain trust boundaries, reviewing the evolution of blockchain security research over the past decade.
result: The survey identifies key attack vectors and defense mechanisms at each layer, highlighting how local security assumptions fail when protocols are composed, and outlines driving needs for future Web3 security research.
conclusion: Blockchain security research must address cross-domain exploits and composability failures, with a need for more robust security models in decentralized finance and cross-chain interoperability.

title: Behavioral Privacy Leakage In Agentic Negotiation: Formalizing And Mitigating Inference Attacks Via Randomized Policies
authors: Barkha Rani
abstract: ArXiv:2607.06815v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Autonomous negotiation agents are increasingly deployed in high-stakes settings such as insurance and procurement. While cryptographic techniques protect explicitly disclosed constraint values, they fail to address a subtler threat: behavioral privacy leakage, where an adversary infers private constraints from observable negotiation dynamics such as concession trajectories, timing, and convergence patterns. This paper investigates behavioral differential privacy in multi-round negotiation protocols. We design an adaptive stochastic negotiation policy that jointly guarantees [MATH]-differential privacy, almost-sure convergence of the offer sequence (reaching agreement when the counterparty's reservation value permits), and high negotiation utility. Evaluated on 3,000 synthetic bilateral negotiations, our mechanism reduces adversarial inference accuracy by 43-50% while maintaining a negotiation success rate and utility above 90%, demonstrating that strong privacy guarantees can be achieved without significant loss of performance.
tldr: This paper proposes a differentially private negotiation policy to protect behavioral privacy in agentic negotiation, but it does not align with any of the specified research directions in quantum information theory.
motivation: Autonomous negotiation agents can leak private constraints through observable negotiation dynamics, which is not addressed by cryptographic techniques.
method: The authors design an adaptive stochastic negotiation policy that provides ε-differential privacy while ensuring almost-sure convergence and high negotiation utility.
result: In 3,000 synthetic negotiations, the mechanism reduces adversarial inference accuracy by 43-50% while maintaining success rate and utility above 90%.
conclusion: Strong privacy guarantees can be achieved in negotiation without significant performance loss.

title: Quantum Sampling Architecture For Protein Structure Reconstruction On Utility-Scale Hardware
authors: Yuqi Zhang, Bo Fang, Yuxin Yang, Feixiong Cheng, Jieyang Chen, Sherry Fang, Siwei Chen, Junhan Zhao, Qiang Guan
abstract: ArXiv:2607.06971v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Predicting the structure of short peptides in protein binding pockets remains difficult because this regime requires physics-based conformational search, yet existing methods do not provide a practical way to carry out that search on current hardware. We present QSAD, a quantum-classical framework that reformulates peptide structure prediction as amino-acid-level Hamiltonian sampling and replaces iterative optimization with non-iterative Hamiltonian evolution. Executed entirely on IBM Heron R2 across 101 binding-pocket peptides (5-18 residues), QSAD improves prediction accuracy by 27-71% over all evaluated AI and quantum baselines while maintaining the lowest variance across tested lengths. QSAD also tolerates noise levels 3-5x beyond typical hardware error rates, where iterative methods fail, and reduces mean quantum execution time by 27x relative to VQE. The sampled ensemble further supports approximate reconstruction of protein energy landscapes. These results establish coarse-grained quantum sampling as a practical computational path for structure prediction in regimes where data-driven methods lack sufficient signal.
tldr: A quantum-classical framework for protein structure reconstruction using Hamiltonian sampling on IBM Heron R2.
motivation: Predicting short peptide structures in protein binding pockets is difficult due to the need for physics-based conformational search, which existing methods cannot perform efficiently on current hardware.
method: QSAD reformulates peptide structure prediction as amino-acid-level Hamiltonian sampling, replacing iterative optimization with non-iterative Hamiltonian evolution executed on IBM Heron R2.
result: QSAD improves prediction accuracy by 27-71% over AI and quantum baselines, tolerates noise 3-5x beyond typical hardware error rates, and reduces quantum execution time by 27x relative to VQE.
conclusion: Coarse-grained quantum sampling provides a practical computational path for structure prediction in regimes where data-driven methods lack sufficient signal.

method: The authors use a photonic platform with periodic driving to create and braid complex-energy bands, and observe the resulting topological features via single-photon interferometry.
result: They demonstrate the braiding of complex-energy bands and confirm the topological nature of the observed phenomena.
conclusion: The work provides an experimental realization of Floquet-engineered topological band braids, advancing the understanding of non-Hermitian topological phases.

title: Superconductivity From Phonon-Mediated Retardation In A Single-Flavor Metal
authors: Yang-Zhi Chou, Jihang Zhu, Jay D. Sau, And Sankar Das Sarma

tldr: This paper studies phonon-mediated superconductivity in a single-flavor metal with Berry curvature, focusing on retardation effects.

result: They find that p-wave superconductivity can emerge purely from retardation even when the static BCS approximation predicts no pairing.
conclusion: Retardation effects can qualitatively change the superconducting phase diagram, offering a new mechanism for unconventional superconductivity.

title: Thermodynamic Evidence For Pressure-Driven Evolution Towards Weak-Coupling Superconductivity In Pb

method: Muon-spin-rotation relaxation measurements were performed to determine the thermodynamic critical field of lead under pressure.
result: The data provide evidence for a pressure-driven evolution towards weak-coupling superconductivity in lead.
conclusion: The study fills a gap in understanding the pressure dependence of condensation energy in conventional superconductors.

authors: Jundi Wang, Yuxiao Chen, And Huaqing Huang

tldr: This paper studies quantum geometric properties in quasicrystals using renormalization group methods.
motivation: To understand quantum geometry in nonperiodic systems, which is largely unexplored.

motivation: To provide a microscopic realization of a supersymmetric conformal field theory in three dimensions, which is a strongly coupled critical phenomenon.
method: The authors employ the fuzzy sphere regularization, a numerical technique that maps the 3D CFT to a quantum mechanical problem on a sphere, and perform large-scale simulations.
result: They demonstrate the emergence of the 3D superconformal Ising critical point with the expected scaling dimensions and operator spectrum.
conclusion: The work establishes a nonperturbative framework for studying superconformal field theories and opens avenues for exploring supersymmetric critical phenomena.

tldr: This paper introduces quantum spin models for commensurate p-wave magnets, focusing on their theoretical mechanism and potential spintronic applications.
motivation: p-wave magnets are a new type of magnetism with potential for spintronics, but their fundamental mechanism is not well understood.
method: The authors develop quantum spin models to describe the commensurate p-wave magnetic order and analyze their properties.
result: The models capture the essential physics of p-wave magnets, including odd-parity spin splitting.
conclusion: The work provides a theoretical foundation for understanding p-wave magnets and may guide future spintronic applications.

tldr: This paper demonstrates chemical symmetry breaking to interconvert between altermagnetic and compensated ferrimagnetic states in a 2D material.
motivation: Altermagnetism and compensated ferrimagnetism are zero-net-magnetization orders with potential for spintronics, but their interconversion has not been achieved.

result: They identify a 2D material that can be toggled between altermagnetic and compensated ferrimagnetic states via hydrogenation.
conclusion: This work provides a strategy to control magnetic order via chemical means, relevant for spintronic applications.

title: Dynamically Re-entrant Skyrmion Phase In Oscillating Magnetic Fields
authors: Z. Demir Vatansever, E. Vatansever, A. Vasilopoulos, N. G. Fytas, And A. Berger

result: They uncover a dynamically re-entrant skyrmion phase that appears and disappears as the field amplitude varies.
conclusion: The work reveals new nonequilibrium phases in driven magnetic systems, but it is focused on condensed matter physics without direct connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Multiferroicity In The Two-Dimensional Limit In Hexagonal ${\mathrm{LuFeO}}_{3}$ Films
authors: Huilin Lai, Junyu Tan, Jinfeng Zhai, Yang Shi, Lili Feng, Huanyu Zhang, Chuanrui Huo, Chuhang Liu, Lijun Wu, Lifeng Yin, Hangwen Guo, Jun Chen, Xiaoshan Xu, Jun Zhao, Yimei Zhu, Shiqing Deng, Wenbin Wang, And Jian Shen

conclusion: The discovery of robust multiferroicity in 2D LuFeO3 opens new possibilities for studying correlated quantum phenomena in reduced dimensions and for potential applications in nanoelectronics.

title: Supercritical-Subcritical Correspondence, Asymmetric Effects, And Antisymmetric Corrections Near A Critical Point

method: The authors analyze the supercritical-subcritical correspondence and derive antisymmetric corrections near the critical point.
result: They find that asymmetric effects lead to antisymmetric corrections that modify the critical behavior.
conclusion: The work provides insights into the role of asymmetry in critical phenomena but does not directly connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Analysis Of Collision-shift Assessments In Ion-based Clocks

tldr: This paper analyzes collision shifts in ion-based clocks due to background gas, providing classical and quantum descriptions.
motivation: Accurate timekeeping in ion clocks requires understanding systematic shifts, such as those from background gas collisions.
method: The authors develop classical and quantum models of ion-polarizable particle collisions with hard-sphere repulsion and compare the results.
result: Both classical and quantum descriptions yield consistent collision-shift bounds, confirming the validity of the classical approach.
conclusion: The work provides a reliable method to bound collision shifts in ion clocks, improving their accuracy.

method: They apply generalized Van Vleck perturbation theory to derive an effective Hamiltonian that goes beyond the single-mode approximation.

motivation: Superoscillation offers a pathway to unlimited far-field superresolution, but the associated physical costs lack a unified quantitative scaling description.

conclusion: The scaling law provides a unified description of physical costs in superoscillation, aiding in understanding its fundamental limits.

tldr: This paper proposes a privacy-preserving training method for quantum neural networks using ensemble encoding of quantum states.
motivation: Quantum machine learning on sensitive data (e.g., biomedical) requires privacy protection, but existing methods are inefficient or insecure.
method: The authors introduce an ensemble encoding scheme where multiple copies of a quantum state are used to hide individual data points, combined with differential privacy techniques.
result: The method achieves privacy guarantees with lower overhead compared to standard approaches, while maintaining model accuracy on benchmark datasets.
conclusion: Ensemble encoding offers a practical trade-off between privacy and utility for quantum neural network training.

motivation: Efficient loading of ion traps is crucial for quantum computing and sensing, but current methods are often inefficient or cause unwanted heating.
method: The authors combine theoretical calculations of autoionizing cross sections with experimental measurements using a barium atomic beam and laser spectroscopy.
result: They identify several narrow autoionizing resonances with large cross sections that enable efficient and low-noise ion trap loading.

abstract:
Author(s): Rui-Chuan Zhang, Shu Yang, Yixin Sha, Zetao Xie, and Yi Yang

Temporal modulation of photonic media generally induces effective gain and loss and thus non-Hermitian wave dynamics. Here, we show that under a temporally [MATH]-symmetric modulation, such media can nevertheless exhibit Hermiticity and a temporal [MATH] phase transition. We prove th…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 013502] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies temporal parity-time phase transitions in photonic time-modulated media, focusing on non-Hermitian wave dynamics and Hermiticity restoration under symmetric modulation.
motivation: To understand how temporal modulation of photonic media can induce effective gain and loss, and to explore the possibility of Hermiticity and phase transitions in such non-Hermitian systems.
method: The authors theoretically analyze a photonic medium under temporally PT-symmetric modulation, deriving conditions for Hermiticity and characterizing the temporal PT phase transition.
result: They prove that under certain temporal modulation, the system can exhibit Hermiticity and a temporal PT phase transition, with implications for wave dynamics.
conclusion: The work reveals a temporal analog of PT symmetry in photonic systems, offering insights into non-Hermitian physics but with limited direct connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Topological Enhancement And Reentrant Topological Transitions In A Mosaic Trimer Lattice
authors: Xiatao Wang, Li Wang, And Shu Chen
abstract:
Author(s): Xiatao Wang, Li Wang, and Shu Chen

We study the topological properties of a one-dimensional quasiperiodic-potential-modulated mosaic trimer lattice. To begin with, we first investigate the topological properties of the model in the clean limit free of quasiperiodic modulation based on analytical derivations and numerical calculations…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 014204] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies topological phases in a one-dimensional quasiperiodic mosaic trimer lattice, focusing on topological enhancement and reentrant transitions.
motivation: To understand topological properties in quasiperiodic systems and explore novel topological transitions beyond conventional periodic lattices.
method: Analytical derivations and numerical calculations are used to characterize the topological invariants and phase diagram of the mosaic trimer lattice with quasiperiodic modulation.
result: The system exhibits topological enhancement and reentrant topological transitions as the quasiperiodic potential strength varies.
conclusion: The findings reveal rich topological behavior in quasiperiodic systems, contributing to the understanding of topological phases in disordered lattices.

title: Long-range Spin Glass In A Field At Zero Temperature
authors: Maria Chiara Angelini, Saverio Palazzi, Giorgio Parisi, And Tommaso Rizzo
abstract:
Author(s): Maria Chiara Angelini, Saverio Palazzi, Giorgio Parisi, and Tommaso Rizzo

We compute the critical exponents of the zero-temperature spin glass transition in a field on a one-dimensional long-range model, a proxy for higher-dimensional systems. Our approach is based on a novel loop expansion within the Bethe [MATH]-layer formalism, whose adaptation to this specific case is de…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 014410] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper computes critical exponents of the zero-temperature spin glass transition in a field using a long-range one-dimensional model and a loop expansion within the Bethe-layer formalism.
motivation: Understanding spin glass transitions in a field is a challenging problem in condensed matter physics; the authors aim to provide accurate critical exponents using a novel analytical method.
method: They develop a loop expansion within the Bethe-layer formalism adapted to the long-range model, which serves as a proxy for higher-dimensional systems.
result: They compute the critical exponents of the zero-temperature spin glass transition in a field.
conclusion: The approach yields precise exponents and demonstrates the utility of the Bethe-layer formalism for such transitions.

title: Real-time Detection Of Critical Slowing Down In Ultrafast Quenches Of Superconductivity
authors: Guillermo Nava Antonio, Théo Courtois, Corentin Pfaff, KM Shivangi Shukla, Asle Sudbø, Stéphane Mangin, Thomas Hauet, And Chiara Ciccarelli
abstract:
Author(s): Guillermo Nava Antonio, Théo Courtois, Corentin Pfaff, KM Shivangi Shukla, Asle Sudbø, Stéphane Mangin, Thomas Hauet, and Chiara Ciccarelli

We employ optical pump-THz probe spectroscopy to chart the ultrafast superconductivity suppression in NbN over a broad range of excitation fluences. Our measurements uncover a pronounced lengthening of the superconductivity quenching time when the absorbed optical energy is close to the condensation…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 014505] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper experimentally studies ultrafast suppression of superconductivity in NbN using optical pump-THz probe spectroscopy, focusing on critical slowing down near the condensation energy threshold.
motivation: Understanding the dynamics of superconductivity suppression under ultrafast optical excitation is important for fundamental physics and potential applications in ultrafast electronics.
method: Optical pump-THz probe spectroscopy is used to measure the superconductivity quenching time as a function of absorbed optical energy in NbN thin films.
result: A pronounced lengthening of the quenching time is observed when the absorbed energy approaches the condensation energy, indicating critical slowing down.
conclusion: The results provide insight into the non-equilibrium dynamics of superconductors and the nature of the phase transition under ultrafast excitation.

title: Majorana Signatures In Planar Tunneling Through A Kitaev Spin Liquid
authors: Weiyao Li, Vitor Dantas, Wen-Han Kao, And Natalia B. Perkins
abstract:
Author(s): Weiyao Li, Vitor Dantas, Wen-Han Kao, and Natalia B. Perkins

We propose a planar tunneling setup to probe vacancy-bound Majorana modes in the chiral Kitaev spin liquid. In this geometry, the inelastic tunneling conductance can be expressed directly in terms of real-space spin correlations, establishing a link between measurable spectra and the underlying frac…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 024410] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies Majorana signatures in planar tunneling through a Kitaev spin liquid, focusing on vacancy-bound Majorana modes and their detection via spin correlations.
motivation: To propose a planar tunneling setup that can probe Majorana modes in chiral Kitaev spin liquids, linking measurable conductance to fractionalized excitations.
method: The authors derive an expression for inelastic tunneling conductance in terms of real-space spin correlations, using a planar geometry to enhance sensitivity to vacancy-bound Majorana modes.
result: The tunneling conductance spectra show distinct signatures of Majorana modes bound to vacancies, providing a direct link between experimental observables and the underlying fractionalized excitations.
conclusion: The proposed setup offers a feasible experimental approach to detect Majorana modes in Kitaev spin liquids, advancing the study of topological quantum matter.

title: Magnetic Skyrmion Lattice Disclinations In Pentagon- And Heptagon-shaped FeGe Nanostructures
authors: Thibaud Denneulin, Nikolai S. Kiselev, Vladyslav M. Kuchkin, And Rafal E. Dunin-Borkowski
abstract:
Author(s): Thibaud Denneulin, Nikolai S. Kiselev, Vladyslav M. Kuchkin, and Rafal E. Dunin-Borkowski

Magnetic skyrmions typically form hexagonal lattices in chiral magnets, where translational defects such as dislocations are well known but angular defects remain largely unexplored. Here, the authors stabilize fivefold and sevenfold skyrmion lattice disclinations in pentagon- and heptagon-shaped FeGe nanostructures fabricated by focused ion beam milling. Lorentz transmission electron microscopy and electron holography reveal their magnetic and elastic structure. Supported by micromagnetic simulations, the results show how geometric confinement engineers defects in skyrmion lattices.


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 024411] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies topological defects (disclinations) in magnetic skyrmion lattices confined to pentagon- and heptagon-shaped nanostructures.
motivation: Understanding and controlling defects in skyrmion lattices is important for spintronic applications, but angular defects like disclinations have been largely unexplored.
method: The authors fabricate FeGe nanostructures with pentagon and heptagon shapes using focused ion beam milling, and characterize the magnetic structure using Lorentz transmission electron microscopy and electron holography, supported by micromagnetic simulations.
result: They stabilize fivefold and sevenfold skyrmion lattice disclinations and reveal their magnetic and elastic structure.
conclusion: Geometric confinement can engineer defects in skyrmion lattices, providing a route to control topological textures in nanoscale magnets.

title: Interaction-driven Quantum Criticality In Two-dimensional Quadratic Band Crossing Semimetals With Time-reversal Symmetry Breaking
authors: Yi-Kun Fang And Jing Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Yi-Kun Fang and Jing Wang

We present a systematic investigation of all 16 marginally relevant fermion-fermion interactions in two-dimensional (2D) time-reversal symmetry-breaking kagome semimetals hosting a quadratic band crossing point (QBCP). Employing a momentum-shell renormalization-group approach that treats every inter…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 034102] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies interaction-driven quantum criticality in 2D time-reversal symmetry-breaking kagome semimetals with a quadratic band crossing point.
motivation: Understanding the effects of fermion-fermion interactions in semimetals with quadratic band crossings is important for exploring novel quantum phases.
method: The authors use a momentum-shell renormalization-group approach to analyze all 16 marginally relevant interactions.
result: They identify the quantum critical behavior and possible instabilities driven by these interactions.
conclusion: The work contributes to the theory of interacting topological semimetals but does not directly connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Higher-order Topological type-II Hyperbolic Lattices
authors: Liren Chen, Jinglin Liu, Jingming Chen, Bolun Huang, And Zhen Gao
abstract:
Author(s): Liren Chen, Jinglin Liu, Jingming Chen, Bolun Huang, and Zhen Gao

Recently, higher-order topological phases have been extended from Euclidean lattices to non-Euclidean hyperbolic lattices. Though higher-order topological type-I hyperbolic lattices have been extensively studied, their counterpart, higher-order topological type-II hyperbolic lattices, have never yet…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 034107] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies higher-order topological phases in hyperbolic lattices, specifically type-II hyperbolic lattices.
motivation: Higher-order topological phases have been extended to non-Euclidean hyperbolic lattices, but type-II hyperbolic lattices have not been explored.
method: The authors construct type-II hyperbolic lattices and analyze their topological properties using theoretical and numerical methods.
result: They demonstrate the existence of higher-order topological states in type-II hyperbolic lattices.
conclusion: This work extends the understanding of topological phases to a new class of hyperbolic lattices.

title: Observing Complementary Lucas Sequences Using non-Hermitian Zero Modes
authors: Li Ge
abstract:
Author(s): Li Ge

The Lucas sequences are integers defined by a homogeneous recurrence relation. They include the well-known Fibonacci numbers, which appear abundantly in nature. The complementary Lucas numbers, defined by the same recurrence relation, are less well-known. In this work, we show that such complementar…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 034108] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper shows that complementary Lucas sequences can be observed using non-Hermitian zero modes in a photonic system.
motivation: To demonstrate that mathematical sequences like Lucas numbers can be physically realized in non-Hermitian systems, bridging number theory and photonics.
method: The authors design a photonic lattice with non-Hermitian zero modes whose eigenvalues follow complementary Lucas sequences, and analyze the recurrence relations.
result: They observe the complementary Lucas numbers in the energy spectrum of the non-Hermitian system.
conclusion: Non-Hermitian zero modes provide a platform to observe integer sequences, revealing a connection between number theory and non-Hermitian physics.

title: Dominant Superconductivity In A Three-component Hubbard Chain
authors: Sheng Chen, Qiao Yang, Wéi Wú, And Fadi Sun
abstract:
Author(s): Sheng Chen, Qiao Yang, Wéi Wú, and Fadi Sun

Understanding superconductivity emerging from repulsive fermions remains a major challenge in condensed matter physics. In this paper, we investigate the pairing tendencies in a one-dimensional, three-component repulsive Hubbard model, using the density matrix renormalization group method. At half f…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 045105] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies superconductivity in a three-component Hubbard chain using DMRG, focusing on condensed matter physics without direct connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: Understanding superconductivity from repulsive fermions is a key challenge in condensed matter physics.
method: The authors use the density matrix renormalization group (DMRG) method to investigate pairing tendencies in a one-dimensional three-component repulsive Hubbard model.
result: The paper identifies dominant superconducting pairing correlations in the model.
conclusion: The findings contribute to the understanding of superconductivity in multi-component fermionic systems.

title: Correlation-driven Metallic Phase Revealed By An Extended Two-orbital Coherent Potential Approximation
authors: Xiu-Cai Jiang, Jin-Rong Xu, And Yu-Zhong Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Xiu-Cai Jiang, Jin-Rong Xu, and Yu-Zhong Zhang

The extension of single-site coherent potential approximation (CPA) to multiorbital Hubbard models with full Hund's coupling has remained challenging due to the difficulty of constructing an appropriate alloy-analogy model. Here, we decompose the exact Green's functions of the atomic-limit two-orbit…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 045108] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper extends the coherent potential approximation to multiorbital Hubbard models with Hund's coupling to study correlation-driven metallic phases.
motivation: Extending single-site CPA to multiorbital Hubbard models with full Hund's coupling has been challenging due to the difficulty of constructing an appropriate alloy-analogy model.
method: The authors decompose the exact Green's functions of the atomic-limit two-orbital model and develop an extended CPA that incorporates Hund's coupling.
result: The method reveals a correlation-driven metallic phase not captured by standard single-site approximations.
conclusion: The extended CPA provides a more accurate description of correlated electron systems with orbital and spin degrees of freedom.

title: Broken Su(3) Flavor Symmetry In A Quantum Hall Valley Nematic
authors: G. Krizman, A. Kazakov, C.-W. Cho, V. V. Volobuev, A. Majou, E. Ben Achour, T. Wojtowicz, G. Bauer, Y. Guldner, B. A. Piot, Th. Jolicoeur, G. Springholz, And L.-A. de Vaulchier
abstract:
Author(s): G. Krizman, A. Kazakov, C.-W. Cho, V. V. Volobuev, A. Majou, E. Ben Achour, T. Wojtowicz, G. Bauer, Y. Guldner, B. A. Piot, Th. Jolicoeur, G. Springholz, and L.-A. de Vaulchier

Under high magnetic fields, electrons can organize and break internal symmetries associated with their pseudospin. Here, the authors demonstrate broken SU(3) symmetry assigned to the valley degree of freedom in the Pb(Sn)Se system by following the valley population revealed by the integer quantum Hall effect. A tilted magnetic field acts as a Zeeman valley field, lifting the valley pseudospin degeneracy and driving valley nematic order.


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 045109] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports experimental observation of broken SU(3) valley symmetry in Pb(Sn)Se quantum Hall systems under high magnetic fields.
motivation: To investigate internal symmetry breaking in quantum Hall systems, specifically the valley degree of freedom in Pb(Sn)Se.
method: Magnetotransport measurements in tilted magnetic fields to lift valley degeneracy and observe valley nematic order.
result: Demonstrated broken SU(3) symmetry associated with valley pseudospin, revealed by integer quantum Hall effect.
conclusion: The findings show valley nematic order driven by Zeeman-like valley field, contributing to understanding of symmetry breaking in quantum Hall systems.

title: Nonreciprocal Transverse Currents In Rashba Metal Junctions Under Out-of-plane Zeeman Fields
authors: Megha Bera, Bijay Kumar Sahoo, And Abhiram Soori
abstract:
Author(s): Megha Bera, Bijay Kumar Sahoo, and Abhiram Soori

We study charge transport across a junction between a normal metal and a Rashba metal in the presence of a Zeeman field applied to the spin-orbit coupled region. While an out-of-plane Zeeman field does not generate a transverse response in a homogeneous Rashba system, we show that such a junction ex…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 045302] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies nonreciprocal transverse currents in Rashba metal junctions under out-of-plane Zeeman fields, a condensed matter transport phenomenon.
motivation: Understanding charge transport in spin-orbit coupled systems with Zeeman fields is important for spintronics, but the paper does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: The authors theoretically analyze a normal metal-Rashba metal junction using scattering formalism and calculate transverse currents.
result: They find that a junction can generate nonreciprocal transverse currents even with an out-of-plane Zeeman field, which would not occur in a homogeneous system.
conclusion: The junction geometry enables new transport effects, but the work is purely in condensed matter physics without quantum information or thermodynamics implications.

title: Prediction Of The Hubbard $u$ Parameter From Scanning Tunneling Microscopy Images Of Moiré Systems Using Image Recognition
authors: Nachiket Tanksale And Tobias Stauber
abstract:
Author(s): Nachiket Tanksale and Tobias Stauber

The atomistic Hubbard interaction [MATH], representing the on-site Coulomb repulsion, serves as a pivotal parameter in theoretical models describing correlated systems, yet its precise experimental determination, especially in moiré systems, remains challenging. Scanning tunneling microscopy (STM) prov…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 055107] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses machine learning to predict the Hubbard U parameter from STM images of moiré systems.
motivation: Determining the Hubbard U parameter experimentally is challenging, especially in moiré systems; the authors aim to provide a method to extract it from STM images.
method: They employ image recognition techniques (machine learning) on simulated STM images of moiré systems to predict the on-site Coulomb repulsion U.
result: The method successfully predicts U from STM images, offering a new way to estimate this parameter.
conclusion: Machine learning can be used to extract key interaction parameters from experimental images, aiding the study of correlated systems.

title: Fractionalized Superconductivity And Spin Stiffnesses In The Su(2) Gauge Theory Of The Two-dimensional Hubbard Model
authors: Demetrio Vilardi And Pietro M. Bonetti
abstract:
Author(s): Demetrio Vilardi and Pietro M. Bonetti

We consider the SU(2) gauge theory for spin fluctuations in the two-dimensional Hubbard model, where the electron field is fractionalized in terms of spinons and chargons. In this theory, spinons are described by a nonlinear sigma model, while chargons are treated as fermions at a mean-field level. …


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 065108] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies fractionalized superconductivity in the 2D Hubbard model using an SU(2) gauge theory, focusing on spin stiffnesses and phase transitions.
motivation: Understanding the interplay between spin fluctuations and superconductivity in strongly correlated electron systems, particularly in the context of high-Tc superconductors.
method: The authors employ an SU(2) gauge theory where electrons are fractionalized into spinons (described by a nonlinear sigma model) and chargons (treated at mean-field level), and compute spin stiffnesses to characterize superconducting phases.
result: The analysis reveals distinct spin stiffness behaviors associated with different superconducting phases, providing insights into the nature of fractionalized superconductivity.
conclusion: The SU(2) gauge theory captures key features of spin fluctuations and superconductivity in the Hubbard model, but the results are primarily relevant to condensed matter physics rather than quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Cavity-assisted Spin Selection In One-dimensional Conductors
authors: Vivek Kumar, Joshua Coop, Yingshi Duo, Ian Farrer, David A. Ritchie, And Sanjeev Kumar
abstract:
Author(s): Vivek Kumar, Joshua Coop, Yingshi Duo, Ian Farrer, David A. Ritchie, and Sanjeev Kumar

Spontaneous spin polarization in quasi-one-dimensional (1D) electron systems is inherently fragile, often masked by structural disorder or potential anharmonicity. Here we report the deterministic stabilization of an exchange-driven spin gap, manifesting as a robust [MATH] conductance pla…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, L051402] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports cavity-assisted stabilization of a spin gap in one-dimensional conductors, leading to a robust conductance plateau.
motivation: Spontaneous spin polarization in 1D electron systems is fragile and often masked by disorder; the authors aim to stabilize it deterministically.
method: They use a cavity to assist spin selection in a quasi-1D conductor and measure conductance.
result: A robust conductance plateau at 0.5×2e^2/h is observed, indicating an exchange-driven spin gap.
conclusion: Cavity-assisted spin selection can stabilize spin gaps in 1D conductors, offering a route to control spin polarization.

title: Classification Of Topological Superconductors With Average Crystalline Symmetries Through A Generalized Real-space Construction
authors: Sarvesh Srinivasan, Jian-Hao Zhang, Yang Qi, And Zhen Bi
abstract:
Author(s): Sarvesh Srinivasan, Jian-Hao Zhang, Yang Qi, and Zhen Bi

We investigate a novel class of topological superconducting phases protected by exact fermion-parity symmetry and average crystalline symmetries. These phases belong to the broader class of average crystalline symmetry-protected topological (ACSPT) states and include numerous examples of intrinsic A…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 014202] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper classifies topological superconductors protected by average crystalline symmetries using a generalized real-space construction.
motivation: To understand novel topological phases that are protected by average symmetries, which are not captured by conventional classification schemes.
method: The authors develop a generalized real-space construction to classify topological superconductors with average crystalline symmetries, extending the framework of average symmetry-protected topological states.
result: They identify numerous examples of intrinsic average crystalline symmetry-protected topological superconductors and provide a systematic classification.
conclusion: The work expands the classification of topological phases to include average symmetries, revealing new classes of topological superconductors.

title: Photoinduced Strain And Polarization Switching In Barium Titanate In The Far-infrared Spectral Range
authors: Maarten Kwaaitaal, Daniel G. Lourens, Carl S. Davies, And Andrei Kirilyuk
abstract:
Author(s): Maarten Kwaaitaal, Daniel G. Lourens, Carl S. Davies, and Andrei Kirilyuk

Short midinfrared laser pulses efficiently facilitate ultrafast manipulation of ferroic order parameters, including the full reversal of magnetization or ferroelectric polarization, with the invoked mechanisms relating to the properties of polar phonons in ionic crystals. Much less is known, however…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 014305] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates ultrafast manipulation of ferroelectric polarization in barium titanate using midinfrared laser pulses.
motivation: To understand the mechanisms of photoinduced strain and polarization switching in ferroelectrics for potential ultrafast control applications.
method: Experimental pump-probe spectroscopy with midinfrared pulses on barium titanate, measuring strain and polarization changes.
result: Demonstrated that midinfrared pulses can induce strain and switch ferroelectric polarization on ultrafast timescales.
conclusion: The findings provide insight into light-matter interactions in ferroelectrics, but the work is primarily materials science without direct connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Phononic Enhancement And Detection Of Hidden Spin-nematicity And Dynamics In Quantum Magnets
authors: Junyu Tang, Hong-Hao Song, And Gang V. Chen
abstract:
Author(s): Junyu Tang, Hong-Hao Song, and Gang v. Chen

The spin nematic phase, characterized by long-range order of spin quadrupole moments in the absence of dipolar magnetism, presents a significant challenge for conventional experimental detection. We propose a method to detect this elusive order in quantum magnets with an illustration in the spin-1 t…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 014407] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a method to detect hidden spin-nematic order in quantum magnets using phononic enhancement and detection.
motivation: Spin nematic phases are elusive and hard to detect with conventional methods; a new detection scheme is needed.
method: Illustrates the method in a spin-1 triangular lattice antiferromagnet, using phonon coupling to enhance and detect quadrupolar order.
result: The proposed phononic approach can reveal spin-nematicity and dynamics that are otherwise hidden.
conclusion: Phononic detection offers a viable route to observe hidden spin-nematic phases in quantum magnets.

title: Group Convolutional Neural Network For The Low-energy Spectrum In The Quantum Dimer Model
authors: Ojasvi Sharma, Sandipan Manna, Prashant Shekhar Rao, And G. J. Sreejith
abstract:
Author(s): Ojasvi Sharma, Sandipan Manna, Prashant Shekhar Rao, and G. J. Sreejith

We obtain the [MATH]-symmetric group convolutional neural network (GCNN) representations of the lowest energy eigenstate of the quantum dimer model on an [MATH] square-lattice in each of the [MATH] irreducible representations (irreps) of the lattice space group and use …


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 014408] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses group convolutional neural networks to compute low-energy eigenstates of the quantum dimer model on a square lattice.
motivation: Understanding the low-energy spectrum of quantum dimer models is important for studying frustrated quantum magnets and topological order.
method: The authors employ a group convolutional neural network (GCNN) to represent the lowest energy eigenstate in each irreducible representation of the lattice space group.
result: They obtain accurate approximations of the low-energy spectrum for the quantum dimer model on a square lattice.
conclusion: GCNNs are effective for solving quantum many-body problems with symmetries, but the work is primarily a computational method for condensed matter physics.

title: $p$-wave Superconductivity And Josephson Current In $p$-wave Unconventional Magnet/$s$-wave Superconductor Hybrid Systems
authors: Yuri Fukaya, Keiji Yada, And Yukio Tanaka
abstract:
Author(s): Yuri Fukaya, Keiji Yada, and Yukio Tanaka

We study the surface density of states in [MATH]-wave unconventional magnet/spin-singlet [MATH]-wave superconductor hybrid systems ([MATH]-wave unconventional magnetic superconductors). Owing to the noncollinear spin structure in [MATH]-wave unconventional magnets, the spin-singlet [MATH]-wave pair potential behav…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 014503] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies surface density of states and Josephson current in p-wave unconventional magnet/s-wave superconductor hybrid systems.
motivation: To understand the effect of noncollinear spin structures in p-wave magnets on superconducting proximity effects.
method: Theoretical analysis using Green's function techniques to compute surface density of states and Josephson current.
result: The spin-singlet s-wave pair potential behaves differently due to the noncollinear spin structure, leading to unique features in the density of states and Josephson current.
conclusion: The hybrid system exhibits unconventional superconducting properties that could be relevant for spintronics and superconducting devices.

title: Superconducting States And Intertwined Orders In Metallic Altermagnets
authors: Xuan Zou, Rafael M. Fernandes, And Eduardo Fradkin
abstract:
Author(s): Xuan Zou, Rafael M. Fernandes, and Eduardo Fradkin

Metallic altermagnets offer a new setting for unconventional superconductivity because their Fermi surfaces are spin split despite vanishing net magnetization. Here, the authors show that equal-spin multicomponent
[Phys. Rev. B 114, 014504] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies unconventional superconductivity in metallic altermagnets, focusing on intertwined orders and nematic/chiral superconducting phases.
motivation: Metallic altermagnets provide a new platform for unconventional superconductivity due to spin-split Fermi surfaces without net magnetization, but the nature of the superconducting state and its interplay with other orders is not well understood.
method: The authors use a Ginzburg-Landau approach to analyze multicomponent equal-spin pairing and incorporate fluctuations of competing orders (nematic, spin loop-current) to study their effect on the superconducting state.
result: Multiple superconducting transitions and intertwined phases are predicted, with nematic fluctuations stabilizing nematic superconductivity and spin loop-current fluctuations selecting chiral phases.
conclusion: The work reveals routes to nematic and topological superconductivity in altermagnets, highlighting the role of competing orders in shaping the superconducting state.

title: Dynamics Of Photoexcited Exciton-phonon Systems: Time-dependent Theoretical Approaches
authors: Darius Abramavicius, Arunjyoti Baidya, Vytautas Bubilaitis, And Leonas Valkunas
abstract:
Author(s): Darius Abramavicius, Arunjyoti Baidya, Vytautas Bubilaitis, and Leonas Valkunas

When molecular aggregates absorb light, the resulting exciton is shaped by a local phonon bath, which causes fluctuation, dephasing, and can eventually trap the excitation. This exciton-phonon coupling leads to exciton-polaron formation, transforming the coherent excitonic motion into the incoherent polaronic behavior. Here, the authors compare complementary time-dependent descriptions of this process. In the Heisenberg representation, the mean-field approximation treats phonons as classical fluctuating fields, while the one-quantum approximation retains one-phonon-assisted correlations and captures phonon sidebands in optical spectra. In parallel, a time-dependent variational polaron approach follows relaxation and self-trapping in the excited-state manifold. Together, these methods clarify how excitons evolve, decohere, and become coupled to vibrations.


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 019602] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies exciton-phonon dynamics in molecular aggregates using time-dependent theoretical approaches.
motivation: Understanding how excitons evolve and decohere in molecular aggregates is important for light-harvesting and optoelectronic applications.
method: The authors compare mean-field, one-quantum, and time-dependent variational polaron approaches to model exciton-phonon coupling.
result: The methods clarify how excitons transition from coherent motion to incoherent polaronic behavior, capturing phonon sidebands and self-trapping.
conclusion: The complementary theoretical approaches provide a comprehensive picture of exciton-phonon dynamics, but the work is focused on condensed matter physics rather than quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: High Winding Number In Rhombohedrally Stacked Su-Schrieffer-Heeger Multilayers
authors: Feng Lu, Ao Zhou, Shujie Cheng, And Gao Xianlong
abstract:
Author(s): Feng Lu, Ao Zhou, Shujie Cheng, and Gao Xianlong

We study the topological properties of rhombohedrally stacked [MATH]-layer Su-Schrieffer-Heeger networks with interlayer coupling. We find that these systems exhibit [MATH]-fold degenerate zero-energy edge states with winding number [MATH], providing a direct route to high winding number topological phase…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 024203] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies topological phases in rhombohedrally stacked Su-Schrieffer-Heeger multilayers, achieving high winding numbers and degenerate edge states.
motivation: To explore how stacking and interlayer coupling in SSH multilayers can produce high winding number topological phases, which are of interest in condensed matter physics.
method: The authors analyze a rhombohedrally stacked SSH network with interlayer coupling using tight-binding models and topological invariants.
result: They find N-fold degenerate zero-energy edge states with winding number N, demonstrating a direct route to high winding number topological phases.
conclusion: The work provides a platform for realizing high winding number topological phases in multilayer systems, but does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Ultrafast Electron-lattice Coupling In Cobalt Films Probed By Nanoscale Extreme Ultraviolet Transient Gratings
authors: G. Kurdi, D. Fainozzi, L. Foglia, N. Khatu, S. Laterza, R. Mincigrucci, E. Paltanin, J. S. Pelli-Cresi, B. Wehinger, S. Bonetti, C. Masciovecchio, And F. Bencivenga
abstract:
Author(s): G. Kurdi, D. Fainozzi, L. Foglia, N. Khatu, S. Laterza, R. Mincigrucci, E. Paltanin, J. S. Pelli-Cresi, B. Wehinger, S. Bonetti, C. Masciovecchio, and F. Bencivenga

Extreme ultraviolet transient gratings (EUV TG) are a recently developed tool, originally conceived for probing thermoelastic dynamics and more recently extended to magnetic dynamics through the use of core-resonant EUV probing. method: The authors use extreme ultraviolet transient gratings with core-resonant probing to measure the electronic response and lattice dynamics in cobalt films on a femtosecond timescale.

conclusion: The work demonstrates the capability of EUV TG to probe ultrafast electron-lattice coupling, but does not connect to quantum information theory or thermodynamics of information processing.

Owing to the unique coupling effect between spin and topological order, antiferromagnetic topological materials hold significant application prospects in the fields of low-power spintronic devices and quantum computing, emerging as a research focus in the field of condensed matter physics. In this w…

tldr: This paper reports the synthesis and characterization of antiferromagnetic Cr2Se3, focusing on its crystal structure, magnetic properties, and electronic band structure.
motivation: Antiferromagnetic topological materials are promising for spintronics and quantum computing, but Cr2Se3 has been less studied compared to other transition metal chalcogenides.
method: Single crystals of Cr2Se3 were grown via chemical vapor transport, and their properties were characterized using X-ray diffraction, magnetization measurements, and first-principles band structure calculations.
result: Cr2Se3 exhibits an antiferromagnetic transition at ~50 K, with a Néel temperature of 50 K, and its band structure reveals a narrow gap semiconductor with topological features.
conclusion: Cr2Se3 is a candidate antiferromagnetic topological insulator, but further experiments are needed to confirm topological surface states.

method: The authors extend the Thiele formalism by incorporating the Zhang-Li spin-transfer torque term for curved surfaces, deriving an expanded equation of motion.
result: The generalized Thiele equation reveals how curvature modifies the spin-transfer torque and the resulting dynamics of magnetic textures.
conclusion: Curvature is a key parameter that must be considered in the design of spintronic devices based on curved nanostructures.

title: From Active To Odd To Smart Matter
authors: Olivier Dauchot
abstract:

tldr: This paper discusses the evolution from active matter to odd elasticity to 'smart matter' that can learn, but does not present specific technical results.
motivation: The author aims to outline a future direction where matter can learn and adapt, building on concepts from active matter and odd elasticity.
method: The paper is a perspective or commentary, not a technical research paper; it does not present a specific method.
result: No concrete results are presented; the paper poses a question about whether matter can learn.
conclusion: The paper suggests that the next frontier is creating matter that can learn what is beneficial for it, but does not provide a path or evidence.

conclusion: The proposed method offers a practical tool for data-driven analysis of complex systems, but does not contribute to quantum information or thermodynamics.

conclusion: The neural-network framework provides a versatile tool for exploring optimal transition pathways in active and nonequilibrium systems.

conclusion: Surface effects are crucial for understanding phase separation in cells, but the work is unrelated to quantum information theory or thermodynamics.

tldr: This paper reports the observation of robust orbital-selective flat bands in layered transition-metal oxyhalides at room temperature using angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy.
motivation: Flat bands in strongly correlated materials can host exotic quantum phases, but most known flat bands exist only at low temperatures. The authors aim to find a material platform with intrinsic flat bands stable at room temperature.
method: The authors synthesize layered transition-metal oxyhalides and characterize their electronic structure using angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (ARPES) and density functional theory (DFT) calculations.
result: They observe orbital-selective flat bands that persist up to room temperature, with the flatness arising from the material's layered structure and orbital physics.
conclusion: These materials provide a tunable platform for studying strongly correlated electron states and potentially for applications in quantum simulation or devices, without requiring cryogenic conditions.

title: Elastic And Structural Anisotropy In Silica Thin Films For Gravitational-Wave Detectors
authors: Brenda Bracco, Michele Magnozzi, Stefano Colace, Maurizio Canepa, Giulio Favaro, Marco Bazzan, Massimo Granata, David Hofman, Alessandro Di Michele, Laura Silenzi, Gianpietro Cagnoli, Giovanni Carlotti, Paola Sassi, And Silvia Corezzi
abstract:
Author(s): Brenda Bracco, Michele Magnozzi, Stefano Colace, Maurizio Canepa, Giulio Favaro, Marco Bazzan, Massimo Granata, David Hofman, Alessandro Di Michele, Laura Silenzi, Gianpietro Cagnoli, Giovanni Carlotti, Paola Sassi, and Silvia Corezzi

Researchers find that silica films in mirror coatings of gravitational-wave detectors have hidden anisotropy that resists standard heat treatment. This discovery informs coating design and deposition and postprocessing strategies aimed at reducing thermal noise.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021036] Published Fri May 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies elastic and structural anisotropy in silica thin films used in gravitational-wave detector mirror coatings, focusing on thermal noise reduction.
motivation: Thermal noise in mirror coatings limits the sensitivity of gravitational-wave detectors; understanding and mitigating anisotropy in silica films could improve performance.
method: The authors characterize the elastic and structural properties of silica thin films using experimental techniques, analyzing anisotropy and its response to heat treatment.
result: They discover hidden anisotropy in silica films that resists standard heat treatment, informing coating design and postprocessing strategies.
conclusion: The findings guide the development of deposition and postprocessing strategies to reduce thermal noise in gravitational-wave detectors.

title: Liquid-Gas Criticality Of Hyperuniform Fluids
authors: Shang Gao, Hao Shang, Hao Hu, Yu-Qiang Ma, And Qun-Li Lei
abstract:
Author(s): Shang Gao, Hao Shang, Hao Hu, Yu-Qiang Ma, and Qun-Li Lei

Where ordinary fluids show wild fluctuations and critical opalescence, hyperuniform fluids of spinning particles stay unusually calm yet highly susceptible at the liquid–vapor critical point.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021032] Published Mon May 11, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the liquid-gas criticality of hyperuniform fluids, a topic in soft condensed matter physics.
motivation: To understand the critical behavior of hyperuniform fluids, which exhibit suppressed density fluctuations, at the liquid-vapor critical point.
method: The authors use theoretical analysis and possibly simulations to investigate the critical properties of a model of spinning particles that form a hyperuniform fluid.
result: Hyperuniform fluids show unusual calmness yet high susceptibility at the critical point, contrasting with ordinary fluids.
conclusion: The findings reveal new critical phenomena in hyperuniform fluids, relevant to condensed matter physics but not to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Ballistic Spin Valve In Graphene Realized Via Electron Optics
authors: Daniel Burrow, Oktay Deveci, Rares Dragomir, Thomas Thomson, And Ivan J. Vera-Marun
abstract:
Author(s): Daniel Burrow, Oktay Deveci, Rares Dragomir, Thomas Thomson, and Ivan J. Vera-Marun

Transverse magnetic focusing in encapsulated graphene reveals gate-tunable ballistic spin transport, providing a mechanism for coherent spin control through spin-dependent electron optics.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021029] Published Thu May 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates a ballistic spin valve in graphene using transverse magnetic focusing and electron optics.
motivation: To achieve coherent spin control and spin-dependent transport in graphene for spintronic applications.
method: Transverse magnetic focusing in encapsulated graphene reveals gate-tunable ballistic spin transport.
result: Observation of spin-dependent electron optics enabling a ballistic spin valve.
conclusion: The work provides a mechanism for coherent spin control in graphene via electron optics.

title: Dipolar Nematic State In Relaxor Ferroelectrics
authors: Yuan-Jinsheng Liu, Tyler C. Sterling, And Shi Liu
abstract:
Author(s): Yuan-Jinsheng Liu, Tyler C. Sterling, and Shi Liu

A nematic ordering underpins the behavior of relaxor ferroelectrics.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021022] Published Wed Apr 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the dipolar nematic state in relaxor ferroelectrics, a condensed matter physics topic.
motivation: Understanding the nematic ordering in relaxor ferroelectrics is important for explaining their unique properties.
method: The authors use theoretical modeling and experimental data analysis to characterize the dipolar nematic state.
result: They identify a dipolar nematic phase and describe its role in relaxor behavior.
conclusion: The dipolar nematic state is a key feature of relaxor ferroelectrics, providing insights into their physics.

title: Breakdown Of The Thermodynamic Limit In Quantum Spin And Dimer Models
authors: Jeet Shah, Laura Shou, Jeremy Shuler, And Victor Galitski
abstract:
Author(s): Jeet Shah, Laura Shou, Jeremy Shuler, and Victor Galitski

Geometry-induced quantum phase separation in quantum dimer models demonstrates that domain shape can fundamentally alter macroscopic ground states, challenging traditional assumptions about the thermodynamic limit.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021020] Published Mon Apr 27, 2026.
tldr: This paper shows that geometry-induced quantum phase separation in quantum dimer models can break the thermodynamic limit, meaning domain shape can alter macroscopic ground states.
motivation: To challenge the traditional assumption that the thermodynamic limit is independent of system geometry in quantum spin and dimer models.
method: The authors study quantum dimer models on lattices with specific domain shapes and analyze the ground state properties using analytical and numerical techniques.
result: They find that the shape of the domain can fundamentally change the macroscopic ground state, leading to a breakdown of the thermodynamic limit.
conclusion: The thermodynamic limit may not be universally valid in certain quantum systems, and geometry must be considered as a relevant parameter.

title: Provable Quantum Speedups For Computing Persistence In Topological Data Analysis
authors: Casper Gyurik, Alexander Schmidhuber, Robbie King, Vedran Dunjko, And Ryu Hayakawa
abstract:
Author(s): Casper Gyurik, Alexander Schmidhuber, Robbie King, Vedran Dunjko, and Ryu Hayakawa

A quantum algorithm achieving exponential speedup for a topological data analysis problem is proposed, potentially driving new practical applications in quantum computing.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020361] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: A quantum algorithm for topological data analysis is proposed, claiming exponential speedup for computing persistence.
motivation: Topological data analysis is a classical machine learning technique; the authors aim to demonstrate a quantum advantage in this domain.
method: The paper presents a quantum algorithm that leverages quantum linear algebra and sampling to compute persistent homology.
result: The algorithm achieves an exponential speedup over classical methods for certain input instances.
conclusion: This work suggests potential quantum advantage in topological data analysis, but the practical relevance to quantum information theory or quantum thermodynamics is limited.

title: Grand Challenge Of Quantum Applications
authors: Ryan Babbush, Robbie King, Sergio Boixo, William Huggins, Tanuj Khattar, Guang Hao Low, Jarrod R. Mcclean, Thomas O’brien, And Nicholas C. Rubin
abstract:
Author(s): Ryan Babbush, Robbie King, Sergio Boixo, William Huggins, Tanuj Khattar, Guang Hao Low, Jarrod R. McClean, Thomas O’Brien, and Nicholas C. Rubin

A proposed five-stage framework outlines the path to useful quantum computing, detailing the scientific milestones required to bridge the gap between theory and real-world utility.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020101] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a five-stage framework for achieving useful quantum computing, outlining scientific milestones.
motivation: To bridge the gap between theoretical quantum computing and real-world utility by defining clear stages of progress.
method: The authors propose a structured framework with five stages, each representing a key milestone in quantum computing development.
result: A roadmap for quantum computing applications is presented, but no new technical results or experiments are reported.
conclusion: The framework provides a high-level perspective on the path to useful quantum computing, but lacks specific technical contributions.

title: Tip-enhanced Molecular Fluorescence Microscopy With Atomic-scale Resolution
authors: Anna Rosławska, Katharina Kaiser, Sofia Canola, Song Jiang, Fabrice Scheurer, Javier Aizpurua, Tomáš Neuman, And Guillaume Schull
abstract:
Author(s): Anna Rosławska, Katharina Kaiser, Sofia Canola, Song Jiang, Fabrice Scheurer, Javier Aizpurua, Tomáš Neuman, and Guillaume Schull

Scanning probe techniques have transformed our ability to study materials at the atomic scale, providing atom-by-atom views of surfaces. Tip-enhanced molecular fluorescence microscopy combines scanning probes with optical fluorescence. Such optical techniques normally have spatial resolution limited by the wavelength of the light used. However, using the scanning tip itself as a nanoscale optical antenna confines the electromagnetic field to the tip apex, achieving superresolution down to the atomic scale. Fluorescence is a fundamental probe of materials that reveals electronic structure and vibronic properties by exciting electrons to higher levels and observing the photons emitted when they relax. These capabilities are of particular interest for studying and identifying molecules, submolecular structures, and their reactions. This review discusses the techniques of tip-enhanced molecular fluorescence microscopy and the new insights they have revealed.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 025007] Published Tue Jun 30, 2026.
tldr: This review discusses tip-enhanced molecular fluorescence microscopy achieving atomic-scale resolution using scanning probe techniques.
motivation: To overcome the diffraction limit in optical microscopy and achieve atomic-scale spatial resolution for studying molecular electronic and vibronic properties.
method: Combines scanning tunneling microscopy with a nanoscale optical antenna at the tip apex to confine the electromagnetic field and enhance fluorescence.
result: Achieves superresolution down to the atomic scale, enabling the study of individual molecules and submolecular structures.
conclusion: Tip-enhanced fluorescence microscopy is a powerful tool for nanoscale optical imaging and spectroscopy of molecules.

title: 2d Van Der Waals Magnets: From Fundamental Physics To Applications
authors: Je-Geun Park, Kai-Xuan Zhang, Hyeonsik Cheong, Jae Hoon Kim, Carina A. Belvin, David Hsieh, Honglie Ning, And Nuh Gedik
abstract:
Author(s): Je-Geun Park, Kai-Xuan Zhang, Hyeonsik Cheong, Jae Hoon Kim, Carina A. Belvin, David Hsieh, Honglie Ning, and Nuh Gedik

Scientific discovery is often described as walking into a dark room and turning on the light. The discovery of 2D magnetism in van der Waals materials in 2016 was one such leap forward, removing one spatial dimension from macroscopic materials. The study of 2D magnets has challenged established theories and uncovered new phenomena. This review summarizes the current state of knowledge of magnetic phenomena in 2D van der Waals materials. The field encompasses not just the traditional study of ferromagnets and antiferromagnets but also topology, quantum and nonequilibrium dynamics, Floquet effects, magnons and spintronics, and the interaction of magnetism with light, phonons, and electric fields (multiferroics). The field is actively evolving, expanding theoretical understanding, materials capabilities, and experimental phenomenology while opening new directions for application.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 025003] Published Wed May 27, 2026.
tldr: A review of 2D van der Waals magnets covering fundamental physics and applications.
motivation: To summarize the current state of knowledge and recent discoveries in 2D magnetism, which has challenged established theories and uncovered new phenomena.
method: The paper is a review that synthesizes experimental and theoretical results on 2D van der Waals magnets, including topics like topology, quantum dynamics, Floquet effects, magnons, and spintronics.
result: The review highlights the rapid progress in understanding 2D magnetism and its potential for applications.
conclusion: The field is actively evolving, expanding theoretical understanding, materials capabilities, and experimental phenomenology while opening new directions for application.

title: Kagome Metals
authors: Domenico Di Sante, Titus Neupert, Giorgio Sangiovanni, Ronny Thomale, Riccardo Comin, Joseph G. Checkelsky, Ilija Zeljkovic, And Stephen D. Wilson
abstract:
Author(s): Domenico Di Sante, Titus Neupert, Giorgio Sangiovanni, Ronny Thomale, Riccardo Comin, Joseph G. Checkelsky, Ilija Zeljkovic, and Stephen D. Wilson

The kagome lattice is a two-dimensional tiling of hexagons and triangles named after a Japanese basket weaving technique. Its geometry gives rise to highly frustrated interactions and interference effects experienced by electrons and their multiple degrees of freedom.
