In metals, the exploration of materials with kagome conduction networks is driven by predictions of realizing new electronic states where these interference effects are dominant, amplifying electronic interactions and many-body effects. In these kagome metals, these amplified correlation effects in combination with spin-orbit coupling and other forms of frustration have given rise to a wealth of phenomena beyond expectations. These include unusual states and responses born from topological flat bands, massive Dirac fermions, sublattice interference effects at saddle points such as unconventional superconductivity, orbital antiferromagnetism and flux phases, amplified anomalous Hall effects, and electronic nematic states. This review examines the theoretical and experimental work on kagome metals, with the aim of elucidating fundamental mechanisms underlying the observed exotic phenomena.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 015002] Published Thu Feb 12, 2026.
tldr: A review of kagome metals, focusing on exotic electronic states arising from the frustrated lattice geometry.
motivation: To understand the fundamental mechanisms behind unusual phenomena in kagome metals, such as unconventional superconductivity and topological flat bands.
method: The paper reviews theoretical and experimental work on kagome metals, synthesizing results from multiple studies.
result: Kagome metals exhibit a wealth of exotic states including topological flat bands, massive Dirac fermions, and unconventional superconductivity.
conclusion: The kagome lattice provides a rich platform for exploring strongly correlated and topological electronic phases.

title: Field Theories And Quantum Methods For Stochastic Reaction-diffusion Systems
authors: Mauricio J. Del Razo, Tommaso Lamma, And Wout Merbis
abstract:
Author(s): Mauricio J. del Razo, Tommaso Lamma, and Wout Merbis

The exchange of energy and molecules in a living cell, the spread of opinions through a society, and the flow of traffic in a crowded city are very different phenomena, yet they are all examples of complex systems composed of many agents that interact with each other and exchange energy or particles with the environment. These systems can be modeled as stochastic reaction-diffusion systems. In this pedagogical review, the authors apply powerful field-theoretic methods to these systems, unifying diverse approaches under a single framework. The methods are useful for handling chemical systems but also have applications in a wide range of areas such as ecology and epidemiology.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 015001] Published Thu Jan 22, 2026.
tldr: A pedagogical review applying field-theoretic methods to stochastic reaction-diffusion systems, with applications in chemistry, ecology, and epidemiology.
motivation: Stochastic reaction-diffusion systems model many complex systems, but a unified framework is lacking.
method: The authors review field-theoretic methods (e.g., Doi-Peliti formalism) to treat these systems.
result: They show how these methods unify diverse approaches and provide tools for analyzing such systems.
conclusion: Field-theoretic methods offer a powerful and unifying framework for stochastic reaction-diffusion systems.

title: Spin-glass Dynamics: Experiment, Theory, And Simulation
authors: E. D. Dahlberg, I. González-Adalid Pemartín, E. Marinari, G. Parisi, F. Ricci-Tersenghi, V. Martin-Mayor, J. Moreno-Gordo, R. L. Orbach, I. Paga, J. J. Ruiz-Lorenzo, And D. Yllanes
abstract:
Author(s): E. D. Dahlberg, I. González-Adalid Pemartín, E. Marinari, G. Parisi, F. Ricci-Tersenghi, V. Martin-Mayor, J. Moreno-Gordo, R. L. Orbach, I. Paga, J. J. Ruiz-Lorenzo, and D. Yllanes

This review updates the field of spin glasses with broad application to a large variety of physical systems. In particular, this review tracks the progress of experiment, theory, and large-scale simulations. It highlights the importance of their synergy, from the inception of the field to the present day, and includes future opportunities for research.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045005] Published Mon Dec 15, 2025.
tldr: A review of spin-glass dynamics covering experiment, theory, and simulation.
motivation: To provide an updated overview of spin-glass research and highlight the synergy between experiment, theory, and simulation.
method: Review of experimental, theoretical, and computational studies of spin glasses.
result: Summarizes key developments and future opportunities in spin-glass dynamics.
conclusion: Spin-glass dynamics remain a rich field with broad applications, and continued interdisciplinary collaboration is essential.

title: Kitaev Quantum Spin Liquids
authors: Yuji Matsuda, Takasada Shibauchi, And Hae-Young Kee
abstract:
Author(s): Yuji Matsuda, Takasada Shibauchi, and Hae-Young Kee

Frustration in spin systems can prevent ordering even at =0, creating quantum spin liquids that have been sought since Anderson’s pioneering work in 1973 and his influential 1987 paper connecting them to high-temperature superconductivity. Kitaev’s solvable spin-1/2 models on a honeycomb lattice brought renewed attention to this field, with Jackeli and Khaliullin later revealing how to engineer Kitaev interactions in real materials. This review highlights theoretical and experimental developments in Kitaev spin liquids, emphasizing leading candidate materials and their broad topological properties such as chiral edge modes. Consequently, it provides essential insights for both experimentalists and theorists working on quantum spin liquid problems.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045003] Published Wed Dec 03, 2025.
tldr: A review of Kitaev quantum spin liquids, focusing on candidate materials and topological properties.
motivation: To provide an overview of theoretical and experimental progress in Kitaev spin liquids, which are a type of quantum spin liquid with potential applications in topological quantum computing.
method: The paper reviews theoretical models (Kitaev honeycomb model) and experimental realizations in materials, highlighting chiral edge modes and other topological features.
result: The review summarizes key candidate materials and their properties, emphasizing the broad topological characteristics of Kitaev spin liquids.
conclusion: Kitaev spin liquids are a rich field with ongoing experimental and theoretical developments, offering insights into frustrated magnetism and topological phases.

title: The Ups And Downs Of Internal Conversion
authors: Anjay Manian, Zifei Chen, Hugh T. Sullivan, And Salvy P. Russo
abstract:
Author(s): Anjay Manian, Zifei Chen, Hugh T. Sullivan, and Salvy P. Russo

This review examines the theoretical methods used to describe the photophysical process of internal conversion in quantum systems. These models explore all facets of the nonradiative mechanism, and the review presents an outlook on how they can be incorporated in studies relevant to applications, for example, in photonics and energy harvesting.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 035003] Published Tue Sep 16, 2025.
tldr: A review of theoretical methods for internal conversion in quantum systems, with applications to photonics and energy harvesting.
motivation: Internal conversion is a key nonradiative process in quantum systems, and understanding its theoretical underpinnings is important for applications in photonics and energy harvesting.
method: The paper reviews various theoretical models describing internal conversion, covering different facets of the nonradiative mechanism.
result: The review provides an overview of existing theoretical methods and an outlook on their incorporation into application-relevant studies.
conclusion: Theoretical methods for internal conversion are mature but need to be better integrated into applied fields like photonics and energy harvesting.

title: Colloquium: Quantum Properties And Functionalities Of Magnetic Skyrmions
authors: Alexander P. Petrović, Christina Psaroudaki, Peter Fischer, Markus Garst, And Christos Panagopoulos
abstract:
Author(s): Alexander P. Petrović, Christina Psaroudaki, Peter Fischer, Markus Garst, and Christos Panagopoulos

Skyrmions are topological field configurations that were first discussed in the context of high-energy theory. In recent years, skyrmionic spin patterns in solid-state systems have received much attention, in part for their promising application potential. This Colloquium discusses quantum-mechanical aspects of such magnetic skyrmions, both for the interactions that underlie skyrmion formation and for quantum features of the skyrmions themselves.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 031001] Published Tue Jul 08, 2025.
tldr: This Colloquium reviews quantum properties and functionalities of magnetic skyrmions, focusing on their topological nature and potential applications.
motivation: Magnetic skyrmions are promising for future spintronic devices, and understanding their quantum aspects is crucial for advancing both fundamental physics and applications.
method: The paper surveys theoretical and experimental work on skyrmion formation, quantum features, and interactions, synthesizing results from condensed matter physics.
result: It highlights quantum-mechanical effects in skyrmion dynamics and interactions, and discusses their potential for quantum information processing.
conclusion: Magnetic skyrmions exhibit rich quantum behavior that could be harnessed for novel technologies, but the field is still developing.

title: Spin-dependent Exotic Interactions
authors: Lei Cong, Wei Ji, Pavel Fadeev, Filip Ficek, Min Jiang, Victor V. Flambaum, Haosen Guan, Derek F. Jackson Kimball, Mikhail G. Kozlov, Yevgeny V. Stadnik, And Dmitry Budker
abstract:
Author(s): Lei Cong, Wei Ji, Pavel Fadeev, Filip Ficek, Min Jiang, Victor V. Flambaum, Haosen Guan, Derek F. Jackson Kimball, Mikhail G. Kozlov, Yevgeny V. Stadnik, and Dmitry Budker

This review presents a comprehensive summary of theoretical investigations and experimental searches for spin-dependent interactions beyond the standard model. These interactions may be mediated by various types of exotic bosons, and their existence and properties may, in turn, explain the nature of dark matter and dark energy. The described experiments also probe the discrete fundamental symmetries of nature.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 025005] Published Tue Jun 24, 2025.
tldr: A comprehensive review of theoretical and experimental searches for spin-dependent exotic interactions beyond the standard model, including their potential connection to dark matter and dark energy.
motivation: To understand possible new physics beyond the standard model, particularly spin-dependent forces mediated by exotic bosons that could explain dark matter and dark energy.
method: The paper reviews a wide range of theoretical models and experimental techniques used to search for spin-dependent exotic interactions, including precision measurements and astrophysical observations.
result: The review summarizes current constraints on various exotic boson couplings and discusses the implications for fundamental symmetries and dark matter candidates.
conclusion: Spin-dependent exotic interactions remain an active area of research with many open questions; future experiments may further constrain or discover such interactions.

title: Colloquium: Materials That Exceed Classical Thermodynamic Bounds On Properties
authors: Roderic S. Lakes
abstract:
Author(s): Roderic S. Lakes

Classical thermodynamic bounds provide constraints on values that are expected in measurements of certain physical properties. In a variety of fields, some measurements exceed these bounds. This apparent violation of thermodynamics arises because the measurements are made in ways that violate the underlying assumptions made when deriving these bounds. This Colloquium describes a wide variety of circumstances where such violations occur and which of the underlying assumptions are violated in each case. It also describes how interesting material properties can be developed using materials designed to violate these assumptions.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 021002] Published Wed May 14, 2025.
tldr: This Colloquium reviews materials that appear to exceed classical thermodynamic bounds on properties, explaining the violations by examining underlying assumptions.
motivation: To clarify why certain measurements exceed classical thermodynamic bounds and how materials can be designed to exploit these violations.
method: The paper surveys a wide variety of examples from different fields, analyzing which assumptions of the classical bounds are violated in each case.
result: It identifies that violations occur because measurements are made in ways that violate assumptions such as equilibrium, linearity, or homogeneity.
conclusion: Understanding these violations allows the development of materials with properties that surpass conventional limits, but the findings are primarily in materials science and classical thermodynamics.

title: Colloquium: Synthetic Quantum Matter In Nonstandard Geometries
authors: Tobias Grass, Dario Bercioux, Utso Bhattacharya, Maciej Lewenstein, Hai Son Nguyen, And Christof Weitenberg
abstract:
Author(s): Tobias Grass, Dario Bercioux, Utso Bhattacharya, Maciej Lewenstein, Hai Son Nguyen, and Christof Weitenberg

This Colloquium presents ways to implement fractal lattices, curved spaces, and higher dimensions in atomic, photonic, and electronic systems. The study of quantum many-body physics in these exotic geometries permits simulation of phenomena from topology in condensed matter to models of gravity and cosmology.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 011001] Published Tue Mar 25, 2025.
tldr: A colloquium review on implementing fractal lattices, curved spaces, and higher dimensions in atomic, photonic, and electronic systems for quantum many-body physics.
motivation: To explore quantum many-body physics in nonstandard geometries, enabling simulation of phenomena from condensed matter topology to gravity and cosmology.
method: Reviews experimental and theoretical approaches for realizing fractal lattices, curved spaces, and higher dimensions in various quantum platforms.
result: Summarizes current capabilities and challenges in simulating exotic geometries with atomic, photonic, and electronic systems.
conclusion: Synthetic quantum matter in nonstandard geometries is a promising avenue for studying fundamental physics, but remains largely exploratory and not directly tied to the user's core interests.

title: Self-aligning Polar Active Matter
authors: Paul Baconnier, Olivier Dauchot, Vincent Démery, Gustavo Düring, Silke Henkes, Cristián Huepe, And Amir Shee
abstract:
Author(s): Paul Baconnier, Olivier Dauchot, Vincent Démery, Gustavo Düring, Silke Henkes, Cristián Huepe, and Amir Shee

What if active units could align–or even antialign–their orientation with their own velocity? This intriguing self-alignment property unlocks a spectrum of fascinating behaviors, from single self-propelled particles orbiting in harmonic traps to transformative collective phenomena like synchronized motion in dense or solid elastic assemblies. Unlike systems where units simply mimic their neighbors, self-alignment fundamentally reshapes how motion emerges, paving the way for groundbreaking discoveries in biology, smart materials, and robotics. This review uncovers the hidden power of self-alignment in active systems, introduces a unified mathematical and conceptual framework, explores existing models of self-alignment, and highlights its transformative impact on the study and real-world applications of active systems.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 015007] Published Thu Mar 20, 2025.
tldr: A review of self-alignment in polar active matter, covering single-particle and collective behaviors.
motivation: To unify and understand the role of self-alignment in active systems, which leads to novel phenomena.
method: Review of existing models and experiments, presenting a unified mathematical framework.
result: Self-alignment enables behaviors like orbiting and synchronized motion, with applications in biology and robotics.
conclusion: Self-alignment is a key mechanism in active matter, offering a new perspective for future research.

title: Massive Quantum Systems As Interfaces Of Quantum Mechanics And Gravity
authors: Sougato Bose, Ivette Fuentes, Andrew A. Geraci, Saba Mehsar Khan, Sofia Qvarfort, Markus Rademacher, Muddassar Rashid, Marko Toroš, Hendrik Ulbricht, And Clara C. Wanjura
abstract:
Author(s): Sougato Bose, Ivette Fuentes, Andrew A. Geraci, Saba Mehsar Khan, Sofia Qvarfort, Markus Rademacher, Muddassar Rashid, Marko Toroš, Hendrik Ulbricht, and Clara C. Wanjura

The authors review theories and experimental state-of-the-art efforts to study the effects of gravity on massive quantum systems. Classical gravity is the least precisely tested natural force and may be addressed via precision quantum probes. Experiments testing whether the quantum nature of gravity causes decoherence and collapse of matter-wave functions and whether it can mediate entanglement between separate massive particles are underway, and their results will guide the theoretical description of gravity effects on a laboratory scale.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 015003] Published Thu Feb 13, 2025.
tldr: A review of theoretical and experimental efforts to study gravity's effects on massive quantum systems, including tests of quantum gravity and entanglement mediated by gravity.
motivation: Classical gravity is the least precisely tested natural force, and massive quantum systems may serve as probes to study gravity at the quantum level.
method: The paper reviews theories of gravity-induced decoherence, collapse models, and entanglement generation, along with experimental platforms such as matter-wave interferometry and optomechanics.
result: Current experiments are testing whether gravity causes decoherence or can mediate entanglement between massive particles, with results guiding future theoretical descriptions.
conclusion: Massive quantum systems provide a promising avenue to explore the interface of quantum mechanics and gravity, but the field is still in early stages.

title: On The Significance Of Wigner’s Friend In Contexts Beyond Quantum Foundations
authors: Caroline L. Jones And Markus P. Mueller
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2147 (2026).

There has been a surge of recent interest in the Wigner's Friend paradox, sparking several novel thought experiments and no-go theorems. The main narrative has been that Wigner's Friend highlights a counterintuitive feature that is unique to quantum theory, and which is closely related to the quantum measurement problem. Here, we challenge this view. We argue that the gist of the Wigner's Friend paradox can be reproduced without assuming quantum physics, and that it underlies a much broader class of enigmas in the foundations of physics and philosophy. To show this, we first consider several recently proposed Extended Wigner's Friend scenarios, and demonstrate that some of their implications for the absoluteness of observations can be reproduced by classical thought experiments that involve the duplication of agents. Crucially, some of these classical scenarios are technologically much easier to implement than their quantum counterparts. Then, we argue that the essential structural ingredient of all these scenarios is a feature that we call "Restriction A": that a physical theory cannot give us a probabilistic description of the observations of all agents. Finally, we argue that this difficulty is at the core of other puzzles in the foundations of physics and philosophy, and demonstrate this explicitly for cosmology's Boltzmann brain problem. Our analysis suggests that Wigner's Friend should be studied in a larger context, addressing a frontier of human knowledge beyond quantum foundations: to obtain reliable predictions for experiments in which these predictions can be privately but not intersubjectively verified.

.
tldr: This paper argues that the Wigner's Friend paradox is not unique to quantum theory and can be reproduced classically, linking it to broader foundational puzzles.
motivation: To challenge the view that Wigner's Friend highlights a uniquely quantum feature and to show its relevance to other foundational problems.
method: The authors analyze extended Wigner's Friend scenarios, construct classical analogues with agent duplication, and identify a common structural feature called 'Restriction A'.
result: They demonstrate that some implications of Wigner's Friend can be reproduced classically, and that the core issue is a limitation of physical theories to describe all agents' observations probabilistically.
conclusion: Wigner's Friend should be studied in a broader context beyond quantum foundations, as it relates to obtaining reliable predictions in experiments with private verification.

title: Qubit Operations Using A Modular Optical System Engineered With PyOpticL: A code-to-CAD Optical Layout Tool
authors: Jacob Myers, Christopher Caron, Nishat Helaly, Zhenyu Wei, Justin Oh, Zack Gotobed, Kotaro Yabe, And Robert J. Niffenegger
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2135 (2026).

Complex optical design is hindered by conventional piecewise setup, which prevents modularization and therefore abstraction of subsystems at the circuit level. This limits multiple fields that require complex optics systems, including quantum computing with atoms and trapped ions, because their optical systems are not scalable. We present an open-source Python library for optical layout (PyOpticL) which uses beam-path simulation and dynamic beam-path routing for quick and easy optical layout by placing optical elements along the beam path without a priori specification, enabling adaptive, path-based layouts with automatic routing and connectivity. We use PyOpticL to create modular `drop-in' optical baseplates for common optical subsystems used in atomic and molecular optics (AMO) experiments including laser sources, frequency and intensity modulation, and locking to an atomic reference for stabilization. We demonstrate this minimal working example of a dynamic full laser system for strontium trapped ions by using it for laser cooling, qubit state detection, and over 99% fidelity single-qubit gates with 3D printed baseplates. This enables a new paradigm of design abstraction layers for engineering optical systems leveraging modular baseplates, as they can be used for any wavelength in the system and enables scaling up the underlying optical systems for quantum computers. This new open-source hardware and software code-to-CAD library seeks to foster open-source collaborative hardware and systems design across numerous fields of research including AMO physics and quantum computing with neutral atoms and trapped ions.

.
tldr: Presents an open-source Python library for optical layout and demonstrates its use for building modular optical systems for trapped-ion qubit operations.
motivation: Complex optical design in quantum computing with atoms and trapped ions is hindered by conventional piecewise setup, which prevents modularization and scalability.
method: Develops PyOpticL, a Python library that uses beam-path simulation and dynamic routing to enable adaptive, path-based layouts; creates modular drop-in optical baseplates for common subsystems.
result: Demonstrates a full laser system for strontium trapped ions achieving over 99% fidelity single-qubit gates with 3D printed baseplates.
conclusion: The approach enables a new paradigm of design abstraction layers for engineering optical systems, fostering open-source collaborative hardware design for AMO physics and quantum computing.

title: Sorting Prolate And Oblate Spheroids With A Diatomic Gas In A Magnetic Field
authors: Ruben Lier
abstract: For a gas of diatomic particles with a nonzero magnetic moment, the Senftleben–Beenakker effect implies that transport can be affected by a magnetic field even when the particles are charge neutral. In such a gas, two independent anisotropic odd viscosities are allowed by symmetry and can have opposite signs. We study the resulting odd-viscous Stokes flow around spheroids in the regime where the odd viscosities are small compared to the shear viscosity. Using a perturbative expansion around the spherical solution and the Lorentz reciprocal theorem, we compute the lift forces on oblate and prolate spheroids for general values of the two odd viscosity coefficients. We show that the resulting Hall angles can differ for oblate and prolate spheroids, implying that sedimentation in a diatomic gas subject to a background magnetic field can separate particles according to shape.
tldr: This paper studies odd-viscous Stokes flow around spheroids in a diatomic gas under a magnetic field, showing shape-based separation via Hall angles.
motivation: Understanding how magnetic fields affect transport in neutral diatomic gases (Senftleben–Beenakker effect) and exploiting odd viscosities for particle separation.
method: Perturbative expansion around spherical solution and Lorentz reciprocal theorem to compute lift forces on spheroids for general odd viscosity coefficients.
result: Hall angles differ for oblate and prolate spheroids, enabling shape-based separation during sedimentation in a magnetic field.
conclusion: Odd viscosities in diatomic gases can be used to separate particles by shape, with potential applications in particle sorting.

title: Gravitational And Other Shifts Of Whispering-gallery And Gravitational State Interference Patterns Of Light Neutral Particles
authors: V V Nesvizhevsky, J A Pioquinto, K Schreiner, S Baeßler, P Crivelli, F Nez, S Reynaud, P Yzombard, S A Vasiliev And E Widmann
abstract: We discuss the interference patterns of gravitational and whispering gallery quantum states that can be observed with neutrons, atoms, antiatoms, muonium (Mu), positronium (Ps), and other light neutral particles. A gravitational shift of interference patterns of neutron gravitational and whispering-gallery states can be easily observed with cold, very cold, or ultracold neutrons. The developed methods can be used for observing/searching for other shifts in fundamental neutron physics experiments, for instance, for measuring the gravitational constant or constraining the neutron electric charge. A series of such measurements will be made with neutrons at the PF1B, PF2, D17 facilities at the ILL. A peculiar feature of analogous atomic (anti-atomic) experiments is the much smaller effective critical energies of the materials of mirrors for (anti)atoms. We evaluated parameters that make a measurement of the hydrogen and antihydrogen whispering-gallery states and their gravitational shifts feasible. A series of such measurements will be made with hydrogen and deuterium atoms by the GRASIAN collaboration in Vienna and Turku. A similar measurement with antihydrogen atoms may be of interest for the GBAR experiment, the ASACUSA experiment, which is producing a beam of slow antihydrogen atoms, and other experiments at CERN that study the gravitational properties of antimatter. Quantum reflection (QR) of Mu and Ps from material surfaces opens the possibility of observing whispering-gallery states, although such measurements remain experimentally challenging. Because of the small masses of Mu and Ps, their effective critical energies of the mirror materials are much higher for them than the effective critical energies for hydrogen and other atoms. The observation of gravitational shifts of such states is particularly demanding because of the extremely short lifetimes of these systems. Measurements of whispering gallery states with all these atoms and particles yield precise and detailed information on the QR properties of materials, providing valuable input for both fundamental physics and surface physics studies.
tldr: This paper discusses gravitational and whispering-gallery state interference patterns for light neutral particles, focusing on experimental measurements of gravitational shifts.
motivation: To explore gravitational and other shifts in quantum states of neutrons, atoms, and antiatoms, which could test fundamental physics and constrain properties like the neutron electric charge.
method: The authors analyze interference patterns of gravitational and whispering-gallery states using quantum reflection from material surfaces, and evaluate experimental parameters for various particles.
result: They find that gravitational shifts can be observed with cold neutrons, and that hydrogen/antihydrogen whispering-gallery states are feasible, while muonium and positronium remain challenging due to short lifetimes.
conclusion: These measurements provide precise information on quantum reflection and can be used for fundamental physics tests, but the work is primarily experimental and phenomenological without strong connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Readjustment Of Intrinsic Activity Parameters Governs The Rectified Transport In Asymmetric Ratchets
authors: Yunyan Chen, Xiaoyuan Yu, Fengguo Li And Baoquan Ai
abstract: The rectified transport of active Brownian particles (ABPs) in asymmetric ratchets has been extensively studied. However, most existing literature regulates rectification by designing different structural boundaries. In this work, we shift the research perspective to the internal properties of ABPs and explore the influence of their internal physical parameters on the transport process. Using the vibration-driven vehicle (VDV) as a macroscopic experimental model for ABPs, we systematically adjust the overall mass and position of center of mass of the VDV to reveal its underlying dynamic mechanism. Through long-time dynamic tracking, we identify a ‘parameters readjustment effect’: an increase in mass weakens the particle’s average velocity and persistence length, ultimately driving the active system into a noise-dominated macroscopic localized state. More importantly, the shift of the center of mass induces persistent translational–rotational coupling in the VDV, leading to an anomalous non-monotonic reentrant phase transition in the rectification probability of the system. Our study reveals that this anomalous transport law is fundamentally governed by the dynamic spatial competition between the intrinsic chiral orbit radius of the VDV and the geometric characteristic scale of the channel. Coarse-grained ABP numerical simulations reproduce the overall experimental trends. This work indicates that load-induced parameters evolution is not merely a physical perturbation, but a core dimension that determines macroscopic transport behavior, providing physical insights and principles for going beyond purely geometric design constraints and designing efficient active rectification systems.
tldr: This paper studies the rectified transport of active Brownian particles in asymmetric ratchets by adjusting internal parameters like mass and center of mass, revealing a 'parameters readjustment effect' and anomalous reentrant phase transitions.
motivation: Most existing work on active ratchets focuses on structural boundaries; this work shifts to internal properties of active particles to understand their influence on transport.
method: Experiments using a vibration-driven vehicle as a macroscopic model for active Brownian particles, combined with coarse-grained numerical simulations, systematically varying mass and center of mass position.
result: Increasing mass reduces average velocity and persistence length, leading to a noise-dominated localized state; shifting center of mass induces translational-rotational coupling causing non-monotonic reentrant phase transitions in rectification probability.
conclusion: Load-induced parameter evolution is a core determinant of macroscopic transport behavior, offering principles for designing efficient active rectification systems beyond geometric constraints.

title: Vortex Solitons In Disclination Quasicrystals
authors: Hua Zhong, Yaroslav V Kartashov, Yongdong Li, Fangwei Ye And Yiqi Zhang
abstract: Quasicrystals are ubiquitous in nature. They represent unique aperiodic materials featuring long-range order that occupy an intermediate niche between exactly periodic and disordered materials. These properties are reflected in the unusual evolutionary dynamics of excitations and unique localization properties of linear eigenmodes supported by quasicrystals. In particular, being the structures characterized by discrete rotational symmetry of order , photonic quasicrystals can support the stable propagation of linear vortex-carrying light beams and vortex solitons. However, the impact of discrete rotational symmetry of quasicrystals on the properties of vortex light states has not been investigated so far, as only the systems constructed using the simplest Penrose tiling or corresponding optically induced Penrose lattices are considered in this context. Here, we propose a broad class of quasicrystals with global topological defects—disclinations—introduced into their structure that allows to produce novel quasicrystalline structures with any desired order of discrete rotational symmetry from the basic Penrose structure. Such global topological deformation substantially enriches the linear spectrum of quasicrystals, allowing them to support new types of linear vortex states and bifurcating from them families of stable thresholdless vortex solitons with unusual intensity and phase distributions. We find two different classes of stable vortex solitons comprising in-phase or out-of-phase pairs of closely located bright spots, with total intensity distribution reflecting a particular discrete rotational symmetry of the quasicrystal with disclination. Remarkably, even low-charge vortex solitons can be stable in quasicrystals with disclinations, whereas stability intervals for them broaden with the decrease of the discrete rotational symmetry of quasicrystals. Our results extend the theory of localization in quasicrystals to structures with global topological deformation, highlighting emerging prospects for the robust transmission of power or information arising in these systems.
tldr: This paper studies vortex solitons in photonic quasicrystals with disclinations, focusing on their stability and intensity distributions.
motivation: To understand how global topological defects (disclinations) in quasicrystals affect the properties of vortex light states, which have not been investigated before.
method: The authors propose a class of quasicrystals with disclinations, analyze their linear spectrum, and numerically find families of stable thresholdless vortex solitons.
result: Two classes of stable vortex solitons are found, with stability intervals broadening as discrete rotational symmetry decreases.
conclusion: The results extend localization theory to quasicrystals with topological deformations, offering potential for robust transmission of power or information.

title: Uniaxial-stress-induced Magnetic Transitions In The Triangular-lattice Antiferromagnet PdCrO2
authors: Nina Stilkerich, Tobias Ritschel, Hilary M L Noad, Richard Waite, Dmitry Khalyavin, Kousuke Ishida, Pascal Manuel, Fabio Orlandi, Seunghyun Khim, Elena Gati, Andrew P Mackenzie, Jochen Geck And Clifford W Hicks
abstract: Uniaxial stress is a promising method to tune magnetic frustration, allowing its effects to be studied in a precise way. In this work, uniaxial stress is applied to the triangular-lattice antiferromagnet PdCrO . The Cr–Cr magnetic interaction is very sensitive to interatomic separation, so laboratory-achievable stress can induce substantial changes in magnetic structure. Results from three types of measurement are presented: x-ray diffraction, the stress–strain relationship, and neutron diffraction. The combined data show that the elastic moduli of PdCrO are strongly affected by stress-induced changes in magnetic structure. A new, first-order stress-induced magnetic transition is observed, at which the lattice constant shrinks by 0.21%. The lattice stiffens dramatically across this transition: the Young’s modulus increases by GPa, and the Poisson ratio falls from to . This stiffening indicates that the magnetic order ‘locks,’ that is, becomes insensitive to lattice strain. This locking might occur because the new stress-induced magnetic order nests the Fermi surface of the Pd sheets. Other frustrated magnets, including candidate spin liquids, may show similarly strong coupling between magnetic and elastic degrees of freedom.
tldr: This paper studies uniaxial-stress-induced magnetic transitions in the triangular-lattice antiferromagnet PdCrO2, focusing on the coupling between magnetic and elastic degrees of freedom.
motivation: To understand how uniaxial stress can tune magnetic frustration and induce new magnetic phases in frustrated magnets.
method: Combined x-ray diffraction, stress-strain measurements, and neutron diffraction under uniaxial stress.
result: A first-order stress-induced magnetic transition is observed, accompanied by a 0.21% lattice shrinkage and dramatic stiffening of the lattice.
conclusion: The magnetic order becomes locked under stress, possibly due to Fermi surface nesting, suggesting strong magnetoelastic coupling in frustrated magnets.

title: Density Effects In Precision Laser Spectroscopy Of Exotic Helium Atoms
authors: Hubert J. J\'o\'zwiak, Dimitar Bakalov, Micha{\l} Przybytek, Michail Stoilov, Piotr Wcis{\l}o
abstract: ArXiv:2607.07125v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Exotic helium atoms act as unique atomic traps for heavy, negatively charged particles, protecting them from nuclear annihilation and nuclear capture on timescales long enough to enable high-precision laser spectroscopy. Such measurements serve as stringent tests of three-body quantum electrodynamics and offer a direct route to determining fundamental particle masses. Motivated by upcoming spectroscopic efforts targeting pionic ([MATH]) and kaonic ([MATH]) helium, we present a rigorous theoretical evaluation of the collisional and density effects governing these systems. Using an ab initio potential energy surface and coupled-channel quantum scattering calculations, we study the collisional stability of the candidate metastable states against inelastic quenching in a cryogenic helium buffer gas. Furthermore, we provide theoretical reference values for the pressure broadening and pressure shift coefficients of the targeted transitions. These results establish an essential benchmark for future experiments, paving the way for refined determinations of the pion and kaon masses.
tldr: The paper studies collisional and density effects in precision laser spectroscopy of exotic helium atoms, focusing on pionic and kaonic helium.
motivation: To enable high-precision laser spectroscopy of exotic helium atoms for testing three-body QED and determining fundamental particle masses.
method: Ab initio potential energy surface and coupled-channel quantum scattering calculations are used to evaluate collisional stability and pressure broadening/shift coefficients.
result: Theoretical reference values for pressure broadening and shift coefficients are provided, along with an assessment of collisional stability of metastable states.
conclusion: The results establish benchmarks for future experiments aiming to refine pion and kaon mass determinations.

title: Spectral Graph Uncertainty Principles Via The Graph Fractional Fourier Transform
authors: Bing-Zhao Li Yu Zhang
abstract: ArXiv:2607.06574v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper develops a graph fractional uncertainty principle in the graph fractional Fourier transform (GFRFT) domain. We introduce localization operators in the vertex domain and the graph fractional spectral domain, and build an operator framework to characterize the joint localization of graph signals. A sandwiched joint localization operator is first constructed, whose largest eigenvalue quantifies the attainable simultaneous concentration in the two domains. Then, rotated localization operators and the numerical range are used to provide a geometric description of the admissible uncertainty region, together with a polygonal approximation method for its computation. Numerical examples show that the fractional order reshapes the vertex-graph fractional spectral localization trade-off, and enlarge or shrink the uncertainty region relative to the graph Fourier transform based case. These results generalize classical graph uncertainty principles to the GFRFT domain and provide a flexible tool for graph fractional signal analysis and graph-adapted localized representations.
tldr: This paper develops uncertainty principles for graph signals in the graph fractional Fourier transform domain.
motivation: To generalize classical graph uncertainty principles to the graph fractional Fourier transform domain, providing a flexible tool for graph signal analysis.
method: Introduces localization operators in vertex and graph fractional spectral domains, constructs a sandwiched joint localization operator, and uses rotated localization operators and numerical range for geometric description.
result: The largest eigenvalue of the sandwiched operator quantifies simultaneous concentration; fractional order reshapes the localization trade-off and can enlarge or shrink the uncertainty region.
conclusion: The work generalizes graph uncertainty principles to the GFRFT domain and offers a flexible tool for graph-adapted localized representations.

title: Optimization Geometrodynamics: A Framework For Dynamic Geometric Optimization
authors: Zavier Li
abstract: ArXiv:2607.06723v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Most gradient-based optimization methods move parameters through a fixed background geometry, even when their internal states implicitly define changing notions of length, curvature, and preconditioning. We introduce optimization geometrodynamics, a benchmark language in which optimization is a coupled evolution of a parameter trajectory, a transported distribution of particles, and a controlled time-varying Riemannian metric. The language separates invariant obstructions from improvable geometric mismatch: positive metrics preserve critical points and Morse indices, and cannot remove global geodesic-convexity obstructions, but can alter conditioning, distributional transport, and flux away from exact critical points. We introduce dynamic geometric complexity, the minimum geometric cost required to reduce an optimization difficulty observable. In the oracle benchmark model of strongly convex quadratic objectives with full positive-definite metric control, this complexity is exactly the affine-invariant distance from the relative log-spectrum to a low-condition-number set. We also analyze Hessian-matching flows, spectral Onsager relaxation, discrete exponential projection updates, gauge-invariant observables, and fixed-time local Morse-saddle flux. The paper is theory-only: its claims are formal statements with proofs, intended to provide invariants and benchmark costs against which implementable adaptive optimizers can be compared once their admissible metric families, curvature estimates, and discretization errors are specified.
tldr: This paper introduces a theoretical framework for optimization as a geometric evolution, but does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: The author aims to formalize optimization as a coupled evolution of parameters, particle distributions, and a time-varying metric, separating invariant obstructions from improvable geometric mismatch.
method: The paper develops optimization geometrodynamics, a language using Riemannian geometry, and analyzes dynamic geometric complexity in strongly convex quadratic objectives.
result: It proves that positive metrics preserve critical points and Morse indices, and derives the exact geometric cost for reducing condition number in quadratic problems.
conclusion: The framework provides invariants and benchmark costs for adaptive optimizers, but remains purely theoretical without application to quantum systems.

title: Forgetting-Factor Regret For Online Zero-Sum Games
authors: Yuhang Liu, Zi'ang Yan, Wenjun Mei, Wenxiao Zhao
abstract: ArXiv:2607.07078v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper studies dynamic equilibrium tracking in online two-player zero-sum games with time-varying convex-concave payoff functions. Existing regret metrics for online saddle-point problems usually aggregate historical payoffs with uniform weights, and hence may fail to characterize the real-time tracking performance with respect to the current Nash equilibrium (NE). To address this issue, we introduce a zero-sum game regret function with a forgetting factor, which assigns exponentially decaying weights to past saddle gaps and emphasizes recent performance. This metric directly links regret minimization to the tracking of time-varying NEs. Within this framework, we investigate three online algorithms under different computational and information settings. For first-order feedback, we analyze projected gradient descent-ascent and design a projection-free online Frank-Wolfe method to reduce the computational cost of projections. For zeroth-order feedback, we develop a deterministic finite-difference method that only uses function-value queries. For all three algorithms, we establish forgetting-factor regret bounds that explicitly characterize the effects of NE variation, payoff variation, and gradient-estimation error. We further provide sufficient conditions under which the proposed regret converges to zero, thereby certifying asymptotic tracking of time-varying NEs. The numerical example validates the theoretical results and illustrates the tracking advantage of the proposed regret metric.
tldr: This paper studies dynamic equilibrium tracking in online two-player zero-sum games with time-varying convex-concave payoff functions using a forgetting-factor regret metric.
motivation: Existing regret metrics for online saddle-point problems use uniform weights and fail to track time-varying Nash equilibria effectively.
method: The authors introduce a forgetting-factor regret function with exponentially decaying weights, and analyze three online algorithms: projected gradient descent-ascent, online Frank-Wolfe, and a zeroth-order finite-difference method.
result: Forgetting-factor regret bounds are established that characterize the effects of NE variation, payoff variation, and gradient-estimation error; sufficient conditions for asymptotic tracking are provided.
conclusion: The proposed regret metric and algorithms enable effective tracking of time-varying Nash equilibria in online zero-sum games.

title: Auditable Machine Unlearning For Privacy-Compliant Ransomware Detection Using Multi-Shard Sisa And Deep Reinforcement Learning
authors: Jannatul Ferdous, Rafiqul Islam, Md Zahidul Islam
abstract: ArXiv:2607.06860v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Ransomware poses an escalating cybersecurity threat as attackers continuously modify behavioral patterns to evade static defenses. Although existing machine learning-based detectors often achieve strong predictive performance, they generally assume fixed training data and do not support the selective removal of previously learned samples. This limitation conflicts with privacy regulations such as the GDPR and CCPA, which require the removal of sensitive user data upon request. To address this challenge, we propose an auditable ransomware detection and unlearning framework that integrates deep reinforcement learning with multi-shard SISA retraining. In the proposed system, a Double Deep Q-Network (DDQN) learns a reward-guided detection policy from behavioral features under asymmetric security costs, while multi-shard SISA enables privacy-compliant selective sample removal through shard-level retraining. The framework was evaluated using four criteria: utility preservation, oracle-based forgetting validation, membership inference auditing, and computational efficiency. On a balanced Windows 11 behavioral dataset comprising 2,000 samples and 103 features, the baseline DDQN detector achieved an F1 score of 0.9925 and an AUC of 0.9983. The experimental results show that single-shard unlearning maintains minimal utility degradation and low oracle disagreement, whereas moderate shard counts (M = 5-10) provide the best efficiency-performance trade-off, reducing retraining time to 5-30 s compared with 80-330 s for full retraining. In addition, the membership inference scores remain close to 0.5 across most configurations, indicating limited privacy leakage after unlearning. These findings demonstrate that a privacy-compliant ransomware detection framework can jointly achieve high detection performance, auditable deletion verification, and efficient sample removal.
tldr: This paper proposes a ransomware detection framework that integrates deep reinforcement learning with multi-shard SISA for auditable machine unlearning to comply with privacy regulations.
motivation: Existing ML-based ransomware detectors cannot selectively remove training data, conflicting with privacy laws like GDPR and CCPA. The authors aim to provide a privacy-compliant detection system that supports data deletion requests.
method: A Double Deep Q-Network (DDQN) learns a detection policy from behavioral features, while multi-shard SISA enables efficient sample removal via shard-level retraining. The framework is evaluated on a Windows 11 dataset with 2000 samples and 103 features.
result: The baseline DDQN achieves F1=0.9925 and AUC=0.9983. Unlearning with moderate shard counts (M=5-10) reduces retraining time to 5-30 seconds vs 80-330 seconds for full retraining, with minimal utility loss and membership inference scores near 0.5.
conclusion: The framework demonstrates that privacy-compliant ransomware detection can achieve high performance and efficient, auditable unlearning.

title: Computing With Stochastic Oracles In AI-Augmented Computation
authors: Jie Wang
abstract: ArXiv:2607.06893v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Stochastic-Oracle Turing Machine (SOTM) framework models AI-augmented computation as the interaction of a probabilistic Turing machine with an oracle whose responses are drawn from context-dependent distributions. This paper studies what an SOTM can achieve under two oracle-response schemes: in a cached-response oracle, each distinct query receives one response that is reused on later calls to the same query, while in a fresh-response oracle, each call returns an independent response. In both schemes, the SOTM first computes from its input and internal random source to generate its first query, then proceeds adaptively, computing from its query-response transcript (the record of queries issued and responses received) to generate each subsequent query or produce a final output. Cached responses impose two transcript-based ceilings on achievable performance: a correct-identification ceiling governed by the total variation distance between the transcript distributions induced by the hidden states of the oracle, and an output quality ceiling equal to the expected score of the best output the SOTM can compute from the transcript. Fresh responses can raise these ceilings by allowing repeated calls to accumulate independent evidence toward correct or high-quality outputs. In the binary single-informative-query case, the error probability decreases exponentially in the number of calls to the same query at the Chernoff rate. For output quality, query-count bounds characterize threshold stopping when the score function is incorporated as part of the SOTM, and majority-based amplification bounds characterize the binary candidate-output model when it is not. Together, the results identify how response reuse, transcript information, and access to the score function determine what an SOTM can compute and at what token cost.
tldr: This paper studies the computational capabilities of stochastic-oracle Turing machines in AI-augmented computation, focusing on transcript-based ceilings and query strategies.
motivation: To understand the fundamental limits and capabilities of AI-augmented computation when oracles provide stochastic responses.
method: Formalizes two oracle-response schemes (cached and fresh) and analyzes transcript-based ceilings for correct identification and output quality, using total variation distance and Chernoff bounds.
result: Derives ceilings for cached responses and shows fresh responses can improve performance exponentially; provides query-count bounds for threshold stopping and majority-based amplification.
conclusion: The framework identifies how response reuse, transcript information, and access to score functions determine what an SOTM can compute and at what token cost.

title: Cyber Dynamics I: Finite Macrostates For Behavioral Anomaly Detection In Network Telemetry
authors: Abdul Rahman, Eranga Bandara, Sachin Shetty
abstract: ArXiv:2607.07075v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Entropy-based methods have long been used for network anomaly detection, but most existing approaches treat entropy as a scalar statistic on narrow observables rather than as part of a broader behavioral state-space for cyber systems. We propose a finite-dimensional macrostate framework for network telemetry, instantiated over the Canonical Security Telemetry Substrate (CSTS), so that coarse-graining is performed over persistent entities, typed relations, and temporal state rather than isolated event records. The resulting macrostate captures activity, distributional disorder, structural organization, temporal volatility, persistence, and deviation from benign baselines. Rather than scoring only unusual states, we model window-to-window macrostate transitions and define regime structure, stability, and anomalous change. This supports discrimination between benign workload drift and adversarial reorganization. We evaluate the framework on benchmark network telemetry datasets and compare it against Shannon-, R\'enyi-, and Tsallis-style entropy baselines, as well as standard anomaly detectors. The proposed representation improves anomaly discrimination and supports more interpretable behavioral analysis of cyber telemetry.
tldr: This paper proposes a finite-dimensional macrostate framework for network anomaly detection using entropy-based methods, applied to cybersecurity telemetry.
motivation: Existing entropy-based anomaly detection methods treat entropy as a scalar statistic on narrow observables, lacking a broader behavioral state-space model for cyber systems.
method: The authors define a macrostate over network telemetry using coarse-graining on persistent entities, typed relations, and temporal state, and model window-to-window macrostate transitions to discriminate benign drift from adversarial reorganization.
result: The proposed representation improves anomaly discrimination over Shannon, Rényi, and Tsallis entropy baselines and standard detectors on benchmark datasets.
conclusion: The macrostate framework enables more interpretable behavioral analysis of cyber telemetry for anomaly detection.

title: Simple Nash Equilibria For Qualitative Multiplayer Games
authors: Mona Alluwaym, James C. A. Main, Sven Schewe
abstract: ArXiv:2607.07151v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate memory requirements for Nash and subgame-perfect equilibria in turn-based deterministic games with [MATH]-regular objectives. We prove that memoryless randomised (i.e., stationary) subgame-perfect equilibria always exist in games with reachability, safety, and 0-2 Muller objectives (i.e., Muller objectives for which accepting sets are either up- or downward closed), and any combination of these objectives. We provide an algorithm to construct such an equilibrium. We also show that randomisation may be required to construct memoryless equilibria in games with reachability or B\"uchi as well as safety or CoB\"uchi objectives, and that memoryless equilibria need not exist for any other class of Muller objectives (with respect to the Mostowski hierarchy).
tldr: This paper studies memory requirements for Nash equilibria in multiplayer deterministic games with omega-regular objectives, focusing on reachability, safety, and Muller objectives.
motivation: Understanding the memory needed for equilibria in qualitative games is a fundamental question in game theory and computer science, but it is not directly connected to quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: The authors prove existence of memoryless subgame-perfect equilibria for certain classes of Muller objectives and provide an algorithm to construct them, using combinatorial and game-theoretic reasoning.
result: Memoryless randomised subgame-perfect equilibria exist for reachability, safety, and 0-2 Muller objectives, but not for other Muller classes; randomisation may be necessary.
conclusion: The results characterize when simple equilibria exist in qualitative games, but the work is purely classical and unrelated to the user's research interests.

title: Continual Learning With Participation Privacy: An Auditable Buffering-Aggregation Recipe
authors: T-H. Hubert Chan, Elaine Shi, Mengshi Zhao, Mingxun Zhou
abstract: ArXiv:2607.07209v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Modern federated and streaming learning systems often release intermediate models, so privacy must hold for the full trajectory under adaptive interaction. Motivated by participation privacy, we study single-edit neighboring user streams, where one insertion/deletion shifts all subsequent updates and defeats standard Hamming-neighbor continual-release analyses. We give an auditable modular recipe. A randomized buffering wrapper emits bins of size [MATH], reducing single-edit streams to a Hamming-style per-bin update stream with explicit backlog/delay guarantees, where [MATH] is calibrated by the privacy parameters [MATH]. We then prove a certification theorem identifying when a non-adaptive Hamming-neighbor DP proof for a continual primitive lifts to adaptive inputs: the primitive must use fresh per-round randomness and have a stable one-round privacy profile under common adaptive context. Together, these ingredients yield trajectory-level [MATH]-DP for single-edit streams using standard primitives (e.g., tree prefix sums), with an explicit privacy--latency link via [MATH].
tldr: This paper proposes a buffering-augmented recipe for continual learning with participation privacy, achieving trajectory-level differential privacy under single-edit streams.
motivation: Existing differential privacy analyses for continual release assume Hamming-neighbor streams, but single-edit user streams (insertion/deletion) shift all subsequent updates, breaking standard guarantees.
method: A randomized buffering wrapper emits bins of size M, reducing single-edit streams to Hamming-style per-bin updates; a certification theorem lifts non-adaptive Hamming-neighbor DP proofs to adaptive inputs using fresh per-round randomness and stable one-round privacy profiles.
result: The recipe yields trajectory-level (ε,δ)-DP for single-edit streams with explicit privacy-latency trade-off via M, using standard primitives like tree prefix sums.
conclusion: The work provides a modular, auditable framework for participation privacy in federated/streaming learning, with formal guarantees and tunable delay.

title: Narad: Non-colluding Aggregator-oblivious Record-And-Decrypt
authors: Akshit Vakati Venkata, Rajat Dugar, Ayush Adarsh
abstract: ArXiv:2607.07596v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Electronic voting must keep individual ballots private while letting anyone verify the final tally. This paper presents an architecture that meets both goals without a trusted key dealer: each voter encrypts a ballot in the browser with a self-generated secret key under the Paillier additive homomorphic cryptosystem, and no party ever holds every key. Two server roles divide the tally. A collector combines the voters' per-ballot auxiliary values into a single group element; an aggregator uses that element to cancel the voters' random masks inside the homomorphic product and recover the exact vote sum, learning the result but no individual ballot. The Solana blockchain records every ciphertext immutably and enforces the election lifecycle, while a native C library (libtommath) performs the heavy modular arithmetic. We state six assumptions under which the protocol is correct and prove product homomorphism, mask cancellation, and sum recovery; privacy rests on the Decisional Composite Residuosity (DCR) assumption for the additive layer together with a Diffie-Hellman-style assumption on the masking base. A bit-packing scheme places an entire multi-candidate ballot in one ciphertext, cutting client work, on-chain transactions, storage, and tally cost by a factor of k (the candidate count); the slot width b is free, with only k*b bounded by log_2(N). With b = 25 and a 255-bit modulus the scheme supports ten candidates and up to 2^25 - 1 = 33,554,431 votes per candidate, about 335 million ballots, and tallies 50,000 ballots in under one second. Finally, running the collector and aggregator inside attested secure enclaves makes the tally tamper-resistant and prevents cross-role collusion to deanonymize voters. The proof-of-concept implementation is open-source; a worked numerical example in the appendix reproduces the full pipeline.
tldr: A protocol for electronic voting using homomorphic encryption and blockchain, with security based on number-theoretic assumptions.
motivation: To enable verifiable electronic voting without a trusted key dealer, ensuring ballot privacy and tally correctness.
method: Voters encrypt ballots with Paillier encryption; a collector aggregates auxiliary values, and an aggregator cancels masks to recover the sum; Solana blockchain records ciphertexts; secure enclaves prevent collusion.
result: The protocol supports up to 335 million ballots with 10 candidates, tallies 50,000 ballots in under one second, and is proven secure under DCR and Diffie-Hellman assumptions.
conclusion: The architecture achieves privacy and verifiability without a trusted dealer, with efficient performance and open-source implementation.

title: Electro-optic Comb-empowered Measurement Of The Dynamic Frequency Of A Laser
authors: Weiwei Yang
Xingyu Jia
Jingyi Wang
Xinlun Cai
Yang Li
Guanhao Wu
abstract: Nature Photonics, Published online: 07 July 2026;
tldr: This paper demonstrates a method for measuring the dynamic frequency of a laser using electro-optic frequency combs on an integrated lithium niobate platform, enabling high-precision 3D ranging.
motivation: Accurate measurement of laser frequency dynamics is crucial for applications like LiDAR and spectroscopy, but existing methods are limited in speed or precision.
method: Two electro-optic frequency combs with slightly different repetition rates are generated on a lithium niobate chip; the beat note between them tracks the frequency variation of a frequency-modulated laser.
result: The technique achieves stable and high-precision 3D scene ranging, demonstrating the utility of integrated photonic combs for metrology.
conclusion: Integrated lithium niobate electro-optic combs provide a compact and effective solution for dynamic laser frequency measurement, with potential for practical ranging systems.

title: Unveiling Surface And Subsurface Atomic Vacancies In MoS<sub>2</sub> With Lateral Force Microscopy
authors: Oscar Gutiérrez-Varela
Aitor Zambudio
Pablo Ares
Julio Gómez-Herrero
Enrico Gnecco
Jaime Colchero
J. G. Vilhena
Cristina Gómez-Navarro
abstract: Nature Communications, Published online: 09 July 2026;
tldr: This paper uses lateral force microscopy to detect atomic vacancies in MoS2, including subsurface defects, via friction fingerprints.
motivation: Characterizing atomic defects in 2D materials like MoS2 is crucial for assessing material quality, but existing methods are often complex or limited to surface defects.
method: The authors employ lateral force microscopy (LFM) to image friction variations caused by atomic vacancies, and use simulations to correlate friction fingerprints with vacancy types and depths.
result: LFM can detect both surface and subsurface atomic vacancies in MoS2, and different vacancy configurations produce distinct friction signatures.
conclusion: LFM provides a simple, accessible technique for evaluating the quality of ultrathin materials by identifying atomic defects, including those hidden below the surface.

title: Tailoring Pure Valley-Zeeman Spin-Orbit Coupling In ${\mathrm{WSe}}_{2}$-Encapsulated Monolayer Graphene
authors: Yaqing Han, Siqi Jiang, Jingkuan Xiao, Jiawei Jiang, Yulu Liu, Jiabei Huang, Yu Du, Di Zhang, Fuzhuo Lian, Wanting Xu, Siqin Wang, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Xiaoxiang Xi, Alexander S. Mayorov, Renjun Du, Kai Chang, Hongxin Yang, Lei Wang, And Geliang Yu
abstract:
Author(s): Yaqing Han, Siqi Jiang, Jingkuan Xiao, Jiawei Jiang, Yulu Liu, Jiabei Huang, Yu Du, Di Zhang, Fuzhuo Lian, Wanting Xu, Siqin Wang, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Xiaoxiang Xi, Alexander S. Mayorov, Renjun Du, Kai Chang, Hongxin Yang, Lei Wang, and Geliang Yu

Clearly resolved Landau levels reveal a symmetry-enforced Landau-level reordering driven by competition between fixed valley–Zeeman splitting and magnetic-field-dependent cyclotron energy.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 027001] Published Wed Jul 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies valley-Zeeman spin-orbit coupling in WSe2-encapsulated monolayer graphene, focusing on Landau level reordering.
motivation: To understand the interplay between valley-Zeeman splitting and cyclotron energy in graphene heterostructures.
method: Magneto-transport measurements on WSe2-encapsulated monolayer graphene devices.
result: Observation of symmetry-enforced Landau-level reordering due to competition between fixed valley-Zeeman splitting and magnetic-field-dependent cyclotron energy.
conclusion: The results demonstrate tunable spin-orbit coupling in graphene, relevant for spintronics and valleytronics.

title: Microwave Vortex Beam Lasing Via Photonic Time Crystals
authors: Lei Huang, Weixuan Zhang, Deyuan Zou, Jiacheng Bao, Fengxiao Di, Haoyu Qin, Long Qian, Houjun Sun, And Xiangdong Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Lei Huang, Weixuan Zhang, Deyuan Zou, Jiacheng Bao, Fengxiao Di, Haoyu Qin, Long Qian, Houjun Sun, and Xiangdong Zhang

Microwave lasing carrying orbital angular momentum (OAM) holds significant potential for advanced applications in fields such as high-capacity communications, precision sensing, and radar imaging. However, conventional approaches to masers fail to produce emission with embedded OAM. The recent emerg…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 023801] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates microwave lasing with orbital angular momentum using photonic time crystals.
motivation: Conventional masers cannot produce emission with embedded OAM; photonic time crystals offer a new mechanism to generate vortex beams.
method: The authors propose and analyze a photonic time crystal structure that supports OAM-carrying modes and achieves lasing through temporal modulation.
result: They show that microwave vortex beams can be generated with controlled OAM states, enabling potential applications in communications and sensing.
conclusion: Photonic time crystals provide a viable platform for OAM lasing, expanding capabilities in microwave photonics.

title: Three-Dimensional Wide-Bandwidth Quantum Energy Truncation Terahertz Coherence Tomography
authors: Pengfei Zhu, Hai Zhang, Stefano Sfarra, Fabrizio Sarasini, Xavier Maldague, And Andreas Mandelis
abstract:
Author(s): Pengfei Zhu, Hai Zhang, Stefano Sfarra, Fabrizio Sarasini, Xavier Maldague, and Andreas Mandelis

We report a quantum energy truncation terahertz coherence tomography technique that enables highly localized extraction of molecular-species-specific THz responses. The method exploits resonant photon loss when the emitter THz energy matches molecular vibration quanta. Reflected THz radiation is rec…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 026901] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: A terahertz imaging technique using quantum energy truncation for molecular-specific tomography.
motivation: To achieve highly localized extraction of molecular-species-specific THz responses for imaging applications.
method: Exploits resonant photon loss when emitter THz energy matches molecular vibration quanta, and uses reflected THz radiation.
result: Demonstrates three-dimensional wide-bandwidth quantum energy truncation terahertz coherence tomography.
conclusion: The technique enables molecular-specific THz imaging with potential applications in materials characterization.

title: Revising The Superexchange Model For The Planar Iridate ${\mathrm{Ba}}_{2}{\mathrm{IrO}}_{4}$: From An Analytical Approach To $ab Initio$ Quantum-chemical Computations
authors: L. Siurakshina
abstract:
Author(s): L. Siurakshina

A modified spin-orbital superexchange theory is developed to derive the effective spin Hamiltonian [MATH] governing the exchange interactions between pseudospins-[MATH] on a square lattice, as occurs, for instance, in planar iridium oxide [MATH]. The proced…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 024412] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops a modified spin-orbital superexchange theory to derive an effective spin Hamiltonian for the planar iridate Ba2IrO4, using analytical methods and ab initio quantum-chemical computations.
motivation: To accurately model the magnetic interactions in Ba2IrO4, which is a candidate material for studying spin-orbit coupling effects and quantum magnetism.
method: The authors develop a modified superexchange theory that includes spin-orbit coupling and use ab initio quantum-chemical computations to parameterize the effective spin Hamiltonian.
result: They derive an effective pseudospin-1/2 Hamiltonian on a square lattice and compute exchange parameters that reproduce experimental observations.
conclusion: The modified superexchange model provides a more accurate description of the magnetic properties of Ba2IrO4, highlighting the importance of spin-orbit coupling in iridates.

title: Origin Of Muon Spin Relaxation And Frequency Shift In Frozen Water Explained By Spin-dipole Quantum Coherences
authors: Amba Datt Pant, Akihiro Koda, Burkhard Geil, Katsuhiko Ishida, Anjan Dahal, Anup Shrestha, Hari Shankar Mallik, Jumpei G. Nakamura, Shoichiro Nishimura, Masatoshi Hiraishi, And Koichiro Shimomura
abstract:
Author(s): Amba Datt Pant, Akihiro Koda, Burkhard Geil, Katsuhiko Ishida, Anjan Dahal, Anup Shrestha, Hari Shankar Mallik, Jumpei G. Nakamura, Shoichiro Nishimura, Masatoshi Hiraishi, and Koichiro Shimomura

To understand the origin of muon spin relaxation and frequency shift in water with temperature, we performed weak transverse-field muon spin rotation and relaxation ([MATH]) measurements over a temperature range of 220 K to 300 K. Using a conventional model with a phenomenological relaxation…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 034106] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper explains muon spin relaxation and frequency shift in water using spin-dipole quantum coherences, focusing on condensed matter physics rather than quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: To understand the origin of muon spin relaxation and frequency shift in water across temperatures, which is a problem in condensed matter physics.
method: Weak transverse-field muon spin rotation and relaxation measurements were performed over 220 K to 300 K, and a model incorporating spin-dipole quantum coherences was used to explain the data.
result: The model successfully reproduces the observed temperature dependence of muon spin relaxation and frequency shift.
conclusion: Spin-dipole quantum coherences are key to understanding muon behavior in water, but the work does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Robust Topological Surface States In Skyrmion-host Magnets Eu(Ga,Al)${}_{4}$: Evidence For Dual Topology
authors: Yuki Arai, Kosuke Nakayama, Takemi Kato, Tomonori Nakamura, Asuka Honma, Seigo Souma, Kenichi Ozawa, Kiyohisa Tanaka, Daisuke Shiga, Hiroshi Kumigashira, Yoshinori Okada, Kouji Segawa, And Takafumi Sato
abstract:
Author(s): Yuki Arai, Kosuke Nakayama, Takemi Kato, Tomonori Nakamura, Asuka Honma, Seigo Souma, Kenichi Ozawa, Kiyohisa Tanaka, Daisuke Shiga, Hiroshi Kumigashira, Yoshinori Okada, Kouji Segawa, and Takafumi Sato

The interplay between real-space topology such as magnetic skyrmions and momentum-space topology characterized by topological surface states (TSSs) is predicted to realize novel phenomena and functionalities, yet materials hosting both topologies are scarce. Skyrmion-hosting helimagnet family ${\mat…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, L020402] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports the observation of robust topological surface states in skyrmion-host magnets Eu(Ga,Al)4, providing evidence for dual topology.
motivation: The interplay between real-space topology (magnetic skyrmions) and momentum-space topology (topological surface states) is predicted to enable novel phenomena, but materials hosting both are rare.
method: Angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (ARPES) and first-principles calculations were used to investigate the electronic structure of Eu(Ga,Al)4.
result: Robust topological surface states were observed, confirming the coexistence of skyrmion and topological insulator phases.
conclusion: Eu(Ga,Al)4 is a promising platform for studying dual topology and related functionalities.

title: Tailoring Magnetocrystalline Anisotropy And Anisotropic Magnetocaloric Effect In Ni-doped ${\mathrm{Fe}}_{3}{\mathrm{GaTe}}_{2}$ Single Crystals
authors: Luozhao Zhang, Liqiang Zeng, Jinbo Yang, Yongfeng Mei, Zhongchong Lin, Zhigao Huang, And Jizhai Cui
abstract:
Author(s): Luozhao Zhang, Liqiang Zeng, Jinbo Yang, Yongfeng Mei, Zhongchong Lin, Zhigao Huang, and Jizhai Cui

The regulation of magnetic anisotropy in two-dimensional (2D) van der Waals (vdW) ferromagnets is critical for enabling spintronic and solid-state cooling applications, yet the microscopic doping mechanism remains poorly understood, as conventional ideal-lattice models fail to reconcile the moderate…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 014409] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the effect of Ni doping on magnetocrystalline anisotropy and the anisotropic magnetocaloric effect in Fe3GaTe2 single crystals.
motivation: Understanding and controlling magnetic anisotropy in 2D van der Waals ferromagnets is important for spintronic and solid-state cooling applications, but the microscopic doping mechanism is poorly understood.
method: The authors synthesize Ni-doped Fe3GaTe2 single crystals and characterize their magnetic properties using experimental measurements and theoretical modeling.
result: Ni doping tailors the magnetocrystalline anisotropy and enhances the anisotropic magnetocaloric effect.
conclusion: The findings provide insights into doping strategies for tuning magnetic properties in 2D ferromagnets for potential applications.

title: Intrinsic Structure Of Relaxor Ferroelectrics From First Principles
authors: Xinyu Xu, Kehan Cai, Yubai Shi, Peichen Zhong, And Pinchen Xie
abstract:
Author(s): Xinyu Xu, Kehan Cai, Yubai Shi, Peichen Zhong, and Pinchen Xie

We introduce FIRE-Swap, a first-principles-based framework for sampling representative compositional structures in complex perovskites using machine-learning interatomic potentials. By combining Monte Carlo chemical swaps with geometric relaxation, the method treats chemical and geometric degrees of…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 024204] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces a first-principles framework for sampling compositional structures in relaxor ferroelectrics using machine-learning interatomic potentials.
motivation: Relaxor ferroelectrics have complex compositional disorder that is difficult to model; the authors aim to efficiently sample representative structures for accurate property prediction.
method: They combine Monte Carlo chemical swaps with geometric relaxation, using a machine-learned interatomic potential to accelerate the sampling.
result: The framework successfully generates realistic structural models that capture the intrinsic disorder of relaxor ferroelectrics.
conclusion: The approach enables first-principles-level accuracy for studying relaxor ferroelectrics without exhaustive enumeration of configurations.

title: Coexistence Of Mixed-dimensional Fluctuations And Incommensurate Long-range Order In The Frustrated Antiferromagnet $\mathrm{C}{\mathrm{e}}_{5}\mathrm{Ag}{\mathrm{Pb}}_{3}$
authors: Zhijie Ma, Ying Sun, Jiechen Luo, Sihao Deng, Hongde Wang, Xiuliang Yuan, Kaiqi Zhang, Lunhua He, Cong Wang, And Youguo Shi
abstract:
Author(s): Zhijie Ma, Ying Sun, Jiechen Luo, Sihao Deng, Hongde Wang, Xiuliang Yuan, Kaiqi Zhang, Lunhua He, Cong Wang, and Youguo Shi

Low-dimensional systems host exotic quantum phenomena arising from dimensional confinement and strong electron correlations. Here, we report a prototypical case of site-specific mixed dimensionality in [MATH], which originates from inequivalent Ce1($…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 024406] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports the coexistence of mixed-dimensional fluctuations and incommensurate long-range order in a frustrated antiferromagnet Ce5AgPb3.
motivation: To understand exotic quantum phenomena arising from dimensional confinement and strong electron correlations in low-dimensional systems.
method: Neutron scattering and other experimental techniques were used to study the magnetic structure and fluctuations in Ce5AgPb3.
result: Site-specific mixed dimensionality was observed, with coexisting one-dimensional fluctuations and three-dimensional long-range order.
conclusion: The findings provide a prototypical case of mixed-dimensional magnetism in a frustrated antiferromagnet.

title: Hyperuniformity Near Jamming Transition Over A Wide Range Of Bidispersity
authors: Duc T. Dam, Takeshi Kawasaki, Atsushi Ikeda, And Kunimasa Miyazaki
abstract:
Author(s): Duc T. Dam, Takeshi Kawasaki, Atsushi Ikeda, and Kunimasa Miyazaki

Hyperuniformity, the anomalous suppression of density fluctuations in dense particle systems, has been reported in amorphous solids near the jamming transition. This manuscript shows that the value of the hyperuniformity scaling exponent in two dimensions differs from that in three dimensions, unlike previously thought.

#AdvancingField #UniversalBehavior


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 015407] Published Wed Jul 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies hyperuniformity scaling exponents near the jamming transition in bidisperse particle systems, finding a difference between 2D and 3D.
motivation: Hyperuniformity in amorphous solids near jamming is of interest, but the paper focuses on classical soft matter physics without quantum or information-theoretic aspects.
method: Simulations of bidisperse particle systems near jamming, measuring density fluctuations and scaling exponents.
result: The hyperuniformity scaling exponent differs between two and three dimensions, contrary to previous assumptions of universality.
conclusion: The dimensionality dependence of hyperuniformity near jamming is established, but the work is purely classical and unrelated to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Sufficient Statistics For Parameter Inference In The Stochastic Van Der Pol Oscillator Model For Thermoacoustic Instabilities
authors: Y. Sungtaek Ju
abstract:
Author(s): Y. Sungtaek Ju

Thermoacoustic instabilities pose a critical challenge in the design and operation of many combustion systems.
