We report a low-dimensional statistics approach for inferring the parameters of the stochastic Van der Pol oscillator from trajectory observations. From the exponential family structure of …


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014203] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops a low-dimensional statistics approach for parameter inference in the stochastic Van der Pol oscillator model applied to thermoacoustic instabilities.
motivation: Thermoacoustic instabilities are a critical challenge in combustion systems, and accurate parameter inference from trajectory observations is needed.
method: The authors exploit the exponential family structure of the stochastic Van der Pol oscillator to derive sufficient statistics for parameter estimation.
result: A low-dimensional statistics approach is reported that enables efficient parameter inference from trajectory data.
conclusion: The proposed method provides a practical tool for inferring parameters in thermoacoustic instability models, but it is not directly related to quantum information, thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Spatiotemporal Activity-driven Networks
authors: Zsófia Simon And Jari Saramäki
abstract:
Author(s): Zsófia Simon and Jari Saramäki

Temporal-network models have provided key insights into how time-varying connectivity shapes dynamical processes such as spreading. Among them, the activity-driven model is a widely used, analytically tractable benchmark. Yet many temporal networks, such as those of physical proximity, are also embe…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014306] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper extends the activity-driven temporal network model to incorporate spatiotemporal constraints, analyzing how spatial embedding affects spreading dynamics.
motivation: Many real temporal networks, such as physical proximity networks, are embedded in space, but existing activity-driven models ignore spatial aspects. The authors aim to understand how spatial constraints influence dynamical processes on temporal networks.
method: The authors introduce a spatiotemporal activity-driven model where nodes are placed in a metric space and connections depend on both activity and spatial distance. They derive analytical expressions for the temporal network's structural properties and simulate spreading processes.
result: The model reveals that spatial embedding can significantly slow down spreading and alter the epidemic threshold compared to the non-spatial activity-driven model. The analytical predictions match simulations well.
conclusion: Spatiotemporal constraints are crucial for accurately modeling spreading processes on real temporal networks, and the proposed model provides a tractable framework for further analysis.

title: Random Motility Regulation As A Generic Mechanism Of Community Formation
authors: Alberto Dinelli, Ada Altieri, And Julien Tailleur
abstract:
Author(s): Alberto Dinelli, Ada Altieri, and Julien Tailleur

The self-organization of microbial ecosystems involves a large variety of mechanisms, ranging from biochemical signaling to population dynamics. Among these, the role of motility regulation has been little studied, despite the importance of active migration processes. Here we show how weak, random m…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014404] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies how random motility regulation leads to community formation in microbial ecosystems, using active matter and population dynamics.
motivation: Understanding the self-organization of microbial ecosystems is important, but the role of motility regulation has been little studied.
method: The authors develop a theoretical model incorporating weak, random motility regulation and analyze its effects on community formation.
result: They show that random motility regulation can generically lead to the formation of stable communities.
conclusion: Motility regulation is a generic mechanism for community formation in microbial systems.

title: Locally Resonant Structure Optimal For Creation Of Nonlinear Schrödinger Solitons
authors: Xiezhi Mao And Xinlong Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Xiezhi Mao and Xinlong Wang

A more feasible and flexible approach is developed for emission of nonlinear Schrödinger solitons from an impurity-induced localized wave in the [MATH] model. The impurity structure used for inducing the localized wave is proposed to include an additional elasticity impurity [MATH], as…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014202] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a method to generate nonlinear Schrödinger solitons using a locally resonant impurity structure.
motivation: To develop a more feasible and flexible approach for soliton emission from impurity-induced localized waves.
method: The impurity structure includes an additional elasticity impurity to induce localized waves in the φ^4 model.
result: The approach enables controlled creation of nonlinear Schrödinger solitons.
conclusion: The proposed impurity structure offers a practical way to generate solitons, relevant to nonlinear wave physics.

title: Subexponential Growth Dynamics In Complex Systems: A Piecewise Power-law Model For The Diffusion Of New Words And Names
authors: Hayafumi Watanabe
abstract:
Author(s): Hayafumi Watanabe

A study of online language shows that niche terms—like the name of a narrowly popular music group—spread less quickly than mainstream words.


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014304] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper models the diffusion of new words and names in online language using a piecewise power-law model, finding that niche terms spread more slowly than mainstream ones.
motivation: Understanding how new words and names spread in complex systems like online language can reveal underlying dynamics of information diffusion.
method: The author proposes a piecewise power-law model to describe subexponential growth dynamics and fits it to empirical data on word and name usage from online sources.
result: The model shows that niche terms exhibit slower diffusion compared to mainstream terms, consistent with subexponential growth patterns.
conclusion: The piecewise power-law model effectively captures the diffusion dynamics of linguistic terms, highlighting differences between niche and mainstream spread.

title: Active Deformation Enhances Target Scanning In Crowded Two-dimensional Self-propelled Particle Simulations
authors: Lucas E. Wiebke And Daniel R. Parisi
abstract:
Author(s): Lucas E. Wiebke and Daniel R. Parisi

Self-propelled particles (SPPs) model diverse transport phenomena, including T-cell motility within crowded lymph nodes. Efficient scanning of antigen-presenting cells (APCs) by T cells remains poorly understood under dense conditions. Here we simulate a two-dimensional system of radius-oscillating …


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 015402] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies active deformation in self-propelled particle simulations to enhance target scanning in crowded environments, with applications to T-cell motility.
motivation: Efficient scanning of antigen-presenting cells by T cells in dense lymph nodes is poorly understood; active deformation may improve scanning efficiency.
method: Two-dimensional simulations of radius-oscillating self-propelled particles are used to model T-cell motility and target scanning.
result: Active deformation enhances target scanning efficiency in crowded conditions compared to non-deforming particles.
conclusion: Active deformation is a beneficial strategy for improving search and scanning in dense active matter systems.

title: Nonclassical Interfacial Response In Ionic Liquids At Blocking Electrodes
authors: Mahdi Yavarian And Roderick Melnik
abstract:
Author(s): Mahdi Yavarian and Roderick Melnik

The linear response of a symmetric binary ionic liquid confined between two parallel, blocking electrodes is analyzed under the influence of electrostatic correlations [MATH] while systematically comparing the effects of two distinct interfacial boundary conditions: the Bazant–Storey–Kornyshev (B…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 015502] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the linear response of ionic liquids between blocking electrodes, focusing on electrostatic correlations and boundary conditions.
motivation: Understanding the behavior of ionic liquids at interfaces is important for applications in energy storage and electrochemistry.
method: The authors analyze a symmetric binary ionic liquid model using linear response theory and compare two interfacial boundary conditions (Bazant–Storey–Kornyshev and another).
result: They find nonclassical interfacial responses due to electrostatic correlations, with significant differences depending on the boundary condition.
conclusion: The choice of boundary condition critically affects the predicted interfacial properties of ionic liquids, which has implications for modeling electrochemical systems.

title: Finite-size Scaling In Quasi-three-dimensional Stick Percolation
authors: Ryan K. Daniels
abstract:
Author(s): Ryan K. Daniels

This work extends the universal finite-size scaling framework for continuum percolation from two-dimensional (2D) to quasi-three-dimensional (Q3D) stick systems, in which sequentially deposited wires of finite diameter stack vertically on a flat substrate. Using Monte Carlo simulation, the percolati…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014102] Published Wed Jul 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies finite-size scaling in quasi-three-dimensional stick percolation using Monte Carlo simulations.
motivation: Understanding percolation in quasi-3D systems is important for applications like conductive nanowire networks, but the paper does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: Monte Carlo simulations are used to extend universal finite-size scaling from 2D to quasi-3D stick systems with sequential deposition of finite-diameter wires.
result: The paper presents scaling laws and critical exponents for percolation in quasi-3D stick systems.
conclusion: The work provides a framework for finite-size scaling in quasi-3D continuum percolation, but has no relevance to quantum information theory or thermodynamics.

title: Frustration-induced Collective Dynamical States In Pulse-coupled Adaptive Winfree Networks
authors: R. Anand, V. K. Chandrasekar, And R. Suresh
abstract:
Author(s): R. Anand, V. K. Chandrasekar, and R. Suresh

We investigate collective dynamics in a pulse-coupled adaptive Winfree network under the influence of a frustration (phase-lag) parameter. The coupling strengths coevolve according to a Hebbian adaptation rule and self-organize to support a wide variety of collective states. We observe frequency-clu…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014201] Published Wed Jul 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies collective dynamics in pulse-coupled adaptive Winfree networks with frustration, focusing on frequency clustering and synchronization.
motivation: To understand how frustration (phase-lag) and Hebbian adaptation affect collective states in oscillator networks.
method: Numerical simulations of a pulse-coupled Winfree network with adaptive coupling strengths following a Hebbian rule, varying the frustration parameter.
result: Observation of frequency-clustered states, chimera states, and other collective dynamical regimes depending on frustration strength.
conclusion: Frustration induces a rich variety of collective dynamical states in adaptive oscillator networks, relevant to neural and biological systems.

title: Physics-informed Neural Networks For Solving Saddle-point Equations In Strong-field Physics With Tailored Fields
authors: Jiakang Chen, Sufia Hashim, And Carla Figueira de Morisson Faria
abstract:
Author(s): Jiakang Chen, Sufia Hashim, and Carla Figueira de Morisson Faria

We develop an unsupervised physics-informed neural network (PINN) to solve the saddle-point equations (SPEs) governing direct above-threshold ionization (ATI) within the strong-field approximation. This setting provides a well-understood test bed in which the saddle-point structure is known for tail…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033029] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses physics-informed neural networks to solve saddle-point equations for above-threshold ionization in strong-field physics.
motivation: Solving saddle-point equations in strong-field physics is computationally challenging; the authors aim to develop a machine learning approach that is efficient and accurate.
method: An unsupervised physics-informed neural network (PINN) is designed to solve the saddle-point equations governing direct above-threshold ionization within the strong-field approximation.
result: The PINN successfully reproduces known saddle-point structures and provides accurate solutions for tailored fields.
conclusion: The PINN approach offers a promising alternative for solving saddle-point equations in strong-field physics, but the work is primarily computational physics without direct connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Structural And Thermal Confinement Of Schwarz Crystals
authors: Dan Huang, Huangliu Fu, Meng Lyu, Yuanwen Feng, Ryoichi Kajimoto, Mitsutaka Nakamura, Takashi Honda, Enke Liu, Bing Li, Xiuyan Li, And Ke Lu
abstract:
Author(s): Dan Huang, Huangliu Fu, Meng Lyu, Yuanwen Feng, Ryoichi Kajimoto, Mitsutaka Nakamura, Takashi Honda, Enke Liu, Bing Li, Xiuyan Li, and Ke Lu

As a nontrivial state of solid, Schwarz crystal manifests itself in extremely refined nanograins and triply periodic minimal surface (TPMS) grain boundaries, and therefore exceptional thermal and mechanical stability. However, it remains unexploited how the structural units interact and thermal tran…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033017] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the structural and thermal properties of Schwarz crystals, a type of nanostructured solid with triply periodic minimal surface grain boundaries.
motivation: Schwarz crystals exhibit exceptional thermal and mechanical stability, but the interaction of structural units and thermal transport mechanisms are not well understood.
method: The authors use neutron scattering and theoretical modeling to investigate the structural confinement and thermal transport in Schwarz crystals.
result: They find that the unique nanograin structure and TPMS boundaries lead to suppressed thermal conductivity and enhanced stability.
conclusion: The work provides insights into the design of thermally stable nanostructured materials, but does not directly relate to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Aging Of Ring Polymeric Topological Glass Formers Via Thermal Quench
authors: Arabinda Behera, Projesh Roy, Pinaki Chaudhuri, And Satyavani Vemparala
abstract:
Author(s): Arabinda Behera, Projesh Roy, Pinaki Chaudhuri, and Satyavani Vemparala

We investigate the nonequilibrium glassy dynamics of dense, topologically constrained ring-polymer systems subjected to instantaneous thermal quenches, using large-scale molecular dynamics simulations. We show that the onset of dynamical arrest is strongly controlled by polymer stiffness, with incre…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033019] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the nonequilibrium glassy dynamics of ring-polymer systems after thermal quench using molecular dynamics simulations.
motivation: Understanding the aging dynamics of topologically constrained ring polymers is important for polymer physics, but the paper does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: Large-scale molecular dynamics simulations are used to model dense ring-polymer systems subjected to instantaneous thermal quenches, varying polymer stiffness.
result: The onset of dynamical arrest is strongly controlled by polymer stiffness, with increasing stiffness leading to slower relaxation and more pronounced aging effects.
conclusion: The study provides insights into the glassy dynamics of ring polymers but remains within classical polymer physics, without relevance to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Multipoles As Quantitative Order Parameters For Altermagnetic Spin Splitting
authors: Francesco Martinelli, Anouk Droux, And Claude Ederer
abstract:
Author(s): Francesco Martinelli, Anouk Droux, and Claude Ederer

We establish a quantitative relation between the altermagnetic spin splitting and different higher-order multipoles of the charge and magnetization density around the magnetic atoms. title: Inferring The Underlying Higher-order Network Structure From Low-resolution Interaction State Data
authors: Chuang Ma, Xiao-Feng Luo, Rui-Hui He, Dao-Yu Li, Hai-Feng Zhang And Gui-Quan Sun
abstract: Network reconstruction aims to infer the underlying interactions between entities from observed data and serves as a cornerstone of network science. While most existing methods focus on dynamics-based data and primarily target binary interactions, real-world data often reflect coarse-grained interaction states of individuals over specific time intervals and may involve complex multi-body interactions beyond pairwise connections. Reconstructing the underlying higher-order network structure from such low-resolution interaction state data is therefore of critical importance. In this paper, we formulate an optimization model for inferring higher-order structures based on the minimum description length principle. To solve this problem, we propose a Bayesian network reconstruction method that integrates distribution estimation with Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) sampling. Our method begins by generating candidate configurations for each time interval via MCMC sampling, then constructs a Bayesian network—guided by minimum-entropy—to capture dependencies between configurations across different time intervals. Finally, an iterative update strategy based on distribution estimation is employed to approach the optimal solution. Extensive experiments on both synthetic and real-world datasets demonstrate the effectiveness and robustness of the proposed method.
tldr: This paper proposes a Bayesian method to infer higher-order network structures from low-resolution interaction state data using minimum description length and MCMC sampling.
motivation: Real-world data often provide coarse-grained interaction states over time intervals, and existing methods focus on binary interactions, neglecting higher-order structures. Reconstructing such structures is crucial for understanding complex systems.
method: The method uses MCMC sampling to generate candidate configurations per time interval, builds a Bayesian network guided by minimum-entropy to capture dependencies across intervals, and iteratively updates via distribution estimation to find the optimal solution.
result: Experiments on synthetic and real-world datasets demonstrate the method's effectiveness and robustness in inferring higher-order network structures from low-resolution data.
conclusion: The proposed approach successfully reconstructs higher-order network structures from coarse-grained interaction data, offering a new tool for network science.

title: Characterizing The Low Energy Breakdown In Interpreting Photoionization Delays
authors: Brock Grafstrom And Alexandra S Landsman
abstract: Typical attosecond pump–probe experiments utilize a combination of extreme ultraviolet and IR laser pulses to extract precise timing information of electron dynamics. For sufficiently high photoelectron energies it is typically assumed that Wigner and Coulomb–laser-coupling (CLC) delays are separable, adding up to the experimentally measured photoionization delay. However, no widespread consensus has been reached on how to best interpret time delays at low photoelectron energies or IR wavelengths shorter than 800 nm. These questions are becoming crucial for the interpretation of state of the art ultrafast experiments in atoms and molecules studying electronic motion in bound and quasi-resonant states, where the dynamics of interest are typically only present within the low-energy portion of time delay spectra. In this work we provide an analytical cut-off law which describes the minimum energy where it is valid to approximate the total delay as the sum of the Wigner and CLC components for a given probe laser frequency. In doing so, we discover that the breakdown between the short-range (Wigner) and long-range (CLC) delay components begins around 23 eV for IR wavelengths near 400 nm. This energy is markedly higher than what is traditionally assumed, and therefore has important implications for interpretation of photoionization delay experiments probed with visible light.
tldr: This paper studies photoionization delays in attosecond pump-probe experiments, focusing on the breakdown of the separability of Wigner and Coulomb-laser-coupling delays at low photoelectron energies.
motivation: Interpreting time delays at low photoelectron energies or with visible probe lasers is crucial for ultrafast experiments in atoms and molecules, but no consensus exists on how to separate delay components.
method: The authors derive an analytical cut-off law that gives the minimum energy for which the total delay can be approximated as the sum of Wigner and CLC components, and apply it to various probe laser frequencies.
result: The breakdown between short-range (Wigner) and long-range (CLC) delays begins around 23 eV for IR wavelengths near 400 nm, which is higher than traditionally assumed.
conclusion: The findings have important implications for interpreting photoionization delay experiments probed with visible light, especially in the low-energy regime.

title: Defect Approach To Giant Graviton Dynamics
authors: Yunfeng Jiang And Xinan Zhou Junding Chen
abstract: We develop a framework of zero dimensional defects for analyzing light–light–heavy–heavy (LLHH) correlators in conformal field theories. We specifically apply this formalism to correlators of giant gravitons in super Yang–Mills to probe the nontrivial physics beyond planarity. By combining this framework with bootstrap techniques, we compute all four-point functions at strong coupling involving two maximal giant gravitons and two supergravitons of arbitrary dimensions. We identify a partially broken, higher-dimensional hidden symmetry—a defect extension of 10d hidden conformal symmetry–present at both strong and weak coupling, which allows these correlators to be packaged into a single generating function. Furthermore, we perform a systematic OPE analysis of the strong-coupling correlators, extracting the complete spectrum of anomalous dimensions for the defect-channel double-particle operators. Finally, we argue that the defect perspective provides the natural nonperturbative description for any LLHH correlator by showing that four-point conformal blocks reduce to defect two-point blocks in the heavy limit.
tldr: This paper develops a defect framework for computing LLHH correlators in conformal field theories, applied to giant gravitons in super Yang-Mills theory.
motivation: To understand non-planar corrections in AdS/CFT by studying correlators involving heavy operators like giant gravitons.
method: Combines zero-dimensional defect formalism with bootstrap techniques to compute four-point functions at strong coupling.
result: Identifies a hidden 10d conformal symmetry and obtains the complete spectrum of anomalous dimensions for defect-channel double-particle operators.
conclusion: The defect perspective provides a natural nonperturbative description for LLHH correlators in the heavy limit.

title: Direct Visualization Of Field-driven Valence Band Modulation In Electrostatically Reconfigured Graphene Devices
authors: Umidakhon Rayimjonova, Chin-Yi Huang, Yi-Cheng Weng, Elin Cartwright, Fredrik O L Johansson, Noemi Vannucchi, Pavel Dudin, Avila Jose, Pei Ding, David Muradas-Belinchón, Henry Nameirakpam, Zhaojun Li, Andreas Lindblad And M Venkata Kamalakar
abstract: Graphene with ultrathin metal-oxide layers has emerged as a scalable platform for integrated electronic, spintronic, and neuromorphic devices. The in-plane electric fields in such devices are typically inferred indirectly from transport measurements, which do not provide microscopic details of the interface potential profile. Here, we use photoemission microscopy to uncover the precise electrostatic landscape of a complete device comprising diverse, heterogeneous ultrathin metal-oxide-covered graphene junctions. Using in operando x-ray photoelectron spectroscopy with submicron resolution, we directly image the real potential profile across an entire graphene device, including regions covered by AlOx and TiOx nanometer-thick overlayers. Tracking the valence band edge under current bias and gate voltage enables quantitative analysis of internal field evolution via a spectroscopic screening factor, revealing an up to more than 50% suppression of the electric field in graphene covered with oxides, in agreement with transport measurements. This demonstrates local reconfiguration of electric fields in graphene for advanced two-dimensional (2D) device engineering and circuitry, while our operando circuit spectroscopy measurements provide a generic means to uncover intricate potential landscapes and carrier redistribution in 2D electronic and spintronic circuits.
tldr: This paper uses photoemission microscopy to directly visualize the electrostatic potential profile in graphene devices with oxide overlayers, revealing field suppression.
motivation: Understanding the microscopic electrostatic landscape in graphene devices is crucial for optimizing electronic and spintronic performance, but indirect transport measurements lack spatial detail.
method: In operando x-ray photoelectron spectroscopy with submicron resolution was used to image the valence band edge across graphene junctions under bias and gate voltage.
result: The electric field in graphene covered with AlOx and TiOx is suppressed by up to 50% compared to bare graphene, consistent with transport measurements.
conclusion: Operando circuit spectroscopy provides a generic method to map potential landscapes in 2D devices, enabling advanced engineering of graphene circuits.

title: On The Geometrical And Kinematical Foundations Of The Symmetric Relativity Model: Lorentz Transformation And Time Dilation
authors: Miodrag Mateljevi\'c
abstract: ArXiv:2607.06800v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We examine the kinematic foundations of relativity by considering two inertial frames, [MATH] and [MATH], in a standard configuration, where [MATH] moves along the common spatial [MATH]-axis at a constant velocity [MATH]. By relaxing Einstein's second postulate regarding the universal invariance of the one-way speed of light, we adopt an operational framework grounded strictly on the directly observable two-way (round-trip) speed of light, evaluated alongside the principles of spacetime homogeneity, linearity, and reciprocity. Within this setting, we demonstrate that: (i) the classical Lorentz transformation is recovered exactly along the coordinate axes under a generalized two-way synchronization scheme without requiring Einstein's second postulate; (ii) Langevin's light-clock argument fundamentally implies that the longitudinal scale factor [MATH] matches the standard Lorentz factor [MATH]; and (iii) transverse lengths remain strictly invariant ([MATH]). Crucially, to resolve the ontic paradox of multiple co-existing wavefront centers, we introduce a kinematically symmetric model relative to an absolute cosmological rest frame (or geometric anchor) [MATH], wherein [MATH] and [MATH] move with equal and opposite velocities ([MATH] and [MATH], respectively). Within this generalized framework, allowing for anisotropic one-way light propagation via Reichenbach-type parameters ([MATH] or [MATH]) yields a consistent, linear velocity-addition law, a generalized Doppler effect, and a flat but oblique spacetime metric. Finally, we prove that all round-trip observables remain strictly invariant under synchronization gauge transformations (reflecting the Tangherlini-Edwards perspective) and demonstrate that the resulting non-diagonal metric structure is fully consistent withthe Sagnac effect over closed spatial loops.
tldr: The paper explores a symmetric relativity model by relaxing Einstein's second postulate and introducing an absolute rest frame, focusing on Lorentz transformation and time dilation.
motivation: To resolve the ontic paradox of multiple co-existing wavefront centers and to provide a kinematically symmetric model of relativity without assuming the universal invariance of the one-way speed of light.
method: The authors adopt an operational framework based on the two-way speed of light, spacetime homogeneity, linearity, and reciprocity, and introduce a symmetric model with an absolute cosmological rest frame using Reichenbach-type parameters.
result: They recover the classical Lorentz transformation without Einstein's second postulate, show that Langevin's light-clock argument yields the standard Lorentz factor, and prove invariance of round-trip observables under synchronization gauge transformations.
conclusion: The proposed symmetric model yields a consistent velocity-addition law, generalized Doppler effect, and a flat but oblique spacetime metric, consistent with the Sagnac effect.

title: Global Time-analytic Strong Solutions For A Class Of 3-wave Kinetic Equations
authors: Nguyen Gia Hien, Gigliola Staffilani, Minh-Binh Tran
abstract: ArXiv:2607.06836v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study a class of 3-wave kinetic equations arising in wave turbulence theory, with regularized kernels. For radial, nonnegative initial data, we construct an exact global-in-time strong solution which remains nonnegative and is analytic with respect to time. The proof combines a careful analysis of the resonant interaction surfaces with a time power-series construction and a continuation argument based on the conservation of the energy moment.
tldr: This paper constructs global-in-time analytic strong solutions for a class of 3-wave kinetic equations from wave turbulence theory.
motivation: Wave turbulence theory describes the statistical behavior of nonlinear wave interactions, and rigorous solutions to kinetic equations are needed to validate the theory.
method: The proof combines analysis of resonant interaction surfaces with a time power-series construction and a continuation argument based on conservation of energy.
result: Existence of a global-in-time strong solution that is nonnegative and analytic in time for radial, nonnegative initial data.
conclusion: The work provides a rigorous mathematical foundation for certain 3-wave kinetic equations, but has no direct connection to quantum information or quantum thermodynamics.

title: Inverse Low-Dimensional Manifold Reconstruction Framework For Spatiotemporal Reconstruction Of Compressible Physical Fields
authors: Qiang Liu, Feng Ma, Wei Zhu, Xiyu Jia, Jianmin Xue, Jun Wen, Gaojun Fu
abstract: ArXiv:2607.07084v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Compressible physical fields are widely present in the real physical world, but current artificial intelligence lacks an understanding mechanism for the non-differentiable features in compressible physical fields. Addressing the limitations of existing deep learning architectures in handling global non-differentiable features, we propose the Inverse Low-Dimensional Manifold reconstruction framework (ILDM). This framework couples the Non-differentiable Approximation Function (NAF) for capturing non-differentiable features in compressible flows with the Smooth Fluid Reconstruction (SFR) module tailored for smooth fluid regions. Extensive evaluations across 1D and 2D benchmarks, including Riemann problems and double Mach reflection, demonstrate that ILDM significantly outperforms cPINN and R-adaptive DeepONet. Specifically, ILDM achieves superior localization of non-differentiable interfaces and maintains robust super-resolution performance even with low-resolution inputs, establishing a physically consistent and scalable paradigm for data-driven fluid dynamics.
tldr: This paper proposes a deep learning framework for reconstructing compressible physical fields with non-differentiable features.
motivation: Current AI lacks understanding of non-differentiable features in compressible flows, limiting spatiotemporal reconstruction accuracy.
method: The Inverse Low-Dimensional Manifold (ILDM) framework couples a Non-differentiable Approximation Function (NAF) for capturing shocks and a Smooth Fluid Reconstruction (SFR) module for smooth regions.
result: ILDM outperforms cPINN and R-adaptive DeepONet on 1D and 2D benchmarks, achieving superior localization of interfaces and robust super-resolution.
conclusion: ILDM provides a physically consistent and scalable paradigm for data-driven fluid dynamics reconstruction.

title: Zeros Of Gkp Sequences Of Polynomials
authors: Antonio J. Dur\'an, Mario P\'erez, Juan L. Varona
abstract: ArXiv:2607.06578v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Given two sequences [MATH] and [MATH] and numbers [MATH], we introduce the GKP sequence of polynomials [MATH] using the following recurrence formula: [MATH] and for [MATH] \[ p_{n}(x) = (ax^2+bx+c) p_{n-1}'(x) + (\phi_{n} + \psi_{n} x)p_{n-1}(x), \] where we assume that [MATH] has two different real zeros. Tangent, Secant, Eulerian or Jacobi polynomials are examples of GKP sequences of polynomials. In this paper, under mild assumptions we prove that the zeros of the polynomials [MATH] are real, simple and live between the zeros of [MATH]. Moreover, the zeros of [MATH] interlace the zeros of [MATH]. We study in detail the cases when [MATH] is constant, and [MATH] is constant for [MATH] big enough, proving, among other results, asymptotics for the leftmost and rightmost zeros of [MATH].
tldr: This paper studies the zeros of GKP sequences of polynomials, a class of orthogonal polynomials defined by a specific recurrence relation.
motivation: To understand the properties of zeros of GKP polynomials, which generalize classical polynomial families like Tangent, Secant, Eulerian, and Jacobi polynomials.
method: The authors analyze the recurrence relation and use analytic techniques to prove that zeros are real, simple, and interlaced under mild assumptions.
result: They prove that zeros of GKP polynomials are real, simple, and lie between the zeros of the previous polynomial, with interlacing properties. Asymptotics for extreme zeros are also derived.
conclusion: The work provides a comprehensive characterization of zeros for a broad class of polynomials, contributing to the theory of orthogonal polynomials.

title: Picture Fuzzy Multigroups
authors: Taiwo O. Sangodapo
abstract: ArXiv:2607.06580v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, picture fuzzy multisets were studied together with their associated properties. We also introduced the concept of picture fuzzy multigroups and established some of their algebraic properties.
tldr: The paper introduces picture fuzzy multigroups, an algebraic structure combining picture fuzzy sets and multisets.
motivation: To extend the theory of fuzzy algebraic structures by incorporating picture fuzzy multisets.
method: Defines picture fuzzy multisets and their properties, then introduces picture fuzzy multigroups and studies their algebraic properties.
result: Establishes basic algebraic properties of picture fuzzy multigroups.
