title: Colloquium: Multimessenger Astronomy With Continuous Gravitational Waves And Future Detectors
authors: Benjamin J. Owen
abstract:
Author(s): Benjamin J. Owen

The search for continuous gravitational waves from rotating neutron stars represents a key frontier of gravitational-wave astrophysics, with strong connections to electromagnetic astronomy, nuclear astrophysics, and condensed matter physics. This Colloquium discusses the detection prospects for these long-lived yet elusive signals in the upcoming generation of gravitational-wave detectors, emphasizing the importance of simultaneous electromagnetic observations. It also surveys the potential implications of such multimessenger observations for our understanding of the physical and astrophysical processes taking place in the extremely dense environments of their sources.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 011002] Published Tue Mar 10, 2026.
tldr: This Colloquium discusses the prospects for detecting continuous gravitational waves from rotating neutron stars and the multimessenger implications for astrophysics.
motivation: Continuous gravitational waves are a key frontier in gravitational-wave astrophysics, with connections to electromagnetic astronomy, nuclear astrophysics, and condensed matter physics.
method: The paper reviews detection prospects for upcoming gravitational-wave detectors and emphasizes simultaneous electromagnetic observations.
result: It surveys potential implications for understanding physical and astrophysical processes in dense neutron star environments.
conclusion: Multimessenger observations with continuous gravitational waves will enhance our understanding of neutron star interiors and related physics.

title: Neutron Stars And The Dense Matter Equation Of State
authors: Katerina Chatziioannou, H. Thankful Cromartie, Stefano Gandolfi, Ingo Tews, David Radice, Andrew W. Steiner, And Anna L. Watts
abstract:
Author(s): Katerina Chatziioannou, H. Thankful Cromartie, Stefano Gandolfi, Ingo Tews, David Radice, Andrew W. Steiner, and Anna L. Watts

Neutron stars, the remnants of supernova explosions, are the densest objects in the Universe. A typical neutron star has a mass between one and two solar masses, and a radius of around 12 km. The density at the center of the star is higher than that in atomic nuclei. As a result, the properties of neutron stars provide important information about the behavior of ordinary matter under extreme compression. In recent years, new information about neutron stars has emerged from two sources. The first is the observation of the gravitational-wave signal from the final inspiral of a coalescing binary neutron star. The second is a careful measurement of the x-ray pulse profile of a spinning neutron star. This review discusses these measurements and summarizes how they constrain masses, radii, and central densities. The results are compared to predictions based on calculations of the nuclear equation of state at densities comparable to that in atomic nuclei, which are then extrapolated to higher density. The review ends with an outlook on future observational opportunities.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045007] Published Wed Dec 24, 2025.
tldr: A review of neutron star observations and the dense matter equation of state.
motivation: To understand the behavior of matter at extreme densities found in neutron stars.
method: Review of gravitational-wave and X-ray observations, compared to nuclear equation of state calculations.
result: Constraints on neutron star masses, radii, and central densities are summarized.
conclusion: Future observations will further constrain the dense matter equation of state.

title: Prospects For Supersymmetry At High-Luminosity Lhc
authors: Howard Baer, Vernon Barger, Jessica Bolich, Juhi Dutta, Dakotah Martinez, Shadman Salam, Dibyashree Sengupta, And Kairui Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Howard Baer, Vernon Barger, Jessica Bolich, Juhi Dutta, Dakotah Martinez, Shadman Salam, Dibyashree Sengupta, and Kairui Zhang

Supersymmetry remains one of the leading candidates for physics beyond the standard model, offering a compelling framework to address the hierarchy of scales. Its theoretical appeal has inspired decades of intensive model building and experimental searches. Recent results have placed stringent bounds on the supersymmetric parameter space, sharpening the focus on the remaining viable models. This review surveys the current status and outlook for supersymmetry in light of experimental constraints and recent theoretical developments, and presents projections for the discovery potential of the High-Luminosity Large Hadron Collider across multiple search channels and a variety of well-motivated scenarios.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045001] Published Fri Oct 17, 2025.
tldr: This paper reviews the prospects for supersymmetry at the High-Luminosity LHC, focusing on experimental searches and model constraints.
motivation: Supersymmetry is a leading candidate for physics beyond the Standard Model, but recent experimental results have constrained its parameter space. The paper aims to survey the current status and future discovery potential.
method: The authors review theoretical models and experimental search strategies, and project discovery potential for the HL-LHC across multiple channels.
result: The paper provides an overview of viable supersymmetric scenarios and their expected signatures at the HL-LHC.
conclusion: Supersymmetry remains a compelling framework, and the HL-LHC will significantly extend the search sensitivity.

title: Solar Fusion Iii: New Data And Theory For Hydrogen-burning Stars
authors: B. Acharya et Al.
abstract:
Author(s): B. Acharya et al.

Approximately 90% of the stars in the Milky Way are on the main sequence, fusing hydrogen into helium through a network of nuclear reactions. This includes the nearest star, our Sun. A precise understanding of hydrogen burning is crucial to predicting its luminosity, neutrino production, and helioseismology. This review describes the theoretical and experimental work of the last decade that has advanced our understanding of the nuclear physics of hydrogen burning. It describes the plasma and atomic physics that influences the solar environment in which the nuclear reactions take place, as well as the diagnostics probes—including solar neutrinos and helioseismology—that allow us to test our resulting model of the solar interior.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 035002] Published Thu Sep 04, 2025.
tldr: This paper reviews nuclear physics of hydrogen burning in stars, focusing on solar fusion and neutrino production.
motivation: Understanding hydrogen burning is crucial for predicting stellar luminosity, neutrino production, and helioseismology.
method: The review summarizes theoretical and experimental advances in nuclear reaction rates, plasma physics, and solar modeling.
result: It presents updated nuclear reaction data and improved solar models that better match observations.
conclusion: The work advances astrophysical understanding but has no direct connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Nobel Lecture: Physics Is A Point Of View
authors: John J. Hopfield
abstract:

The 2024 Nobel Prize for Physics was shared by John Hopfield and Geoffrey Hinton. This paper is the text of the address given in conjunction with the award.

result: No new results; it is an address summarizing past work and philosophy.

title: Nobel Lecture: Boltzmann Machines
authors: Geoffrey Hinton
abstract:
Author(s): Geoffrey Hinton

The 2024 Nobel Prize for Physics was shared by John Hopfield and Geoffrey Hinton. This paper is the text of the address given in conjunction with the award.

motivation: The paper presents the Nobel lecture by Geoffrey Hinton on Boltzmann machines, which are foundational to machine learning but not related to quantum information.
method: The lecture describes the concept and training of Boltzmann machines, a type of stochastic recurrent neural network.
result: The lecture summarizes the historical development and impact of Boltzmann machines in machine learning.

title: Order And Disorder At The Atomic Scale: Microscopy Applied To Semiconductors
authors: Enrico Di Russo, Tom Verstijnen, Paul Koenraad, Konstantinos Pantzas, Gilles Patriarche, And Lorenzo Rigutti
abstract:
Author(s): Enrico Di Russo, Tom Verstijnen, Paul Koenraad, Konstantinos Pantzas, Gilles Patriarche, and Lorenzo Rigutti

Atomic-scale details, especially those of disorder, are important for material properties, especially in semiconductors, but they are also extremely difficult to measure. Real-space methods can give direct access to this information, but typically, that access is limited. This review reports the application of three real-space techniques for measuring disorder to compound semiconductor materials: scanning tunneling microscopy, transmission electron microscopy, and atom-probe microscopy. Where possible, it emphasizes cases in which the probes have been combined to achieve a more complete picture of the defects.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 025006] Published Thu Jun 26, 2025.
tldr: This review covers three real-space microscopy techniques for measuring atomic-scale disorder in semiconductors.
motivation: Atomic-scale disorder critically affects semiconductor properties but is difficult to measure; the paper aims to review techniques that provide direct real-space access.
method: The authors review scanning tunneling microscopy, transmission electron microscopy, and atom-probe microscopy, emphasizing combined approaches.
result: The review highlights how these techniques can characterize disorder and defects in compound semiconductors.
conclusion: Real-space microscopy methods are powerful for understanding atomic-scale disorder, but the paper does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Quantum Physics Of Stars
authors: M. Wiescher, C. A. Bertulani, C. R. Brune, R. J. Deboer, A. Diaz-Torres, L. R. Gasques, K. Langanke, P. Navrátil, W. Nazarewicz, J. Okołowicz, D. R. Phillips, M. Płoszajczak, S. Quaglioni, And A. Tumino
abstract:
Author(s): M. Wiescher, C. A. Bertulani, C. R. Brune, R. J. deBoer, A. Diaz-Torres, L. R. Gasques, K. Langanke, P. Navrátil, W. Nazarewicz, J. Okołowicz, D. R. Phillips, M. Płoszajczak, S. Quaglioni, and A. Tumino

There are many nuclear reactions that are of central importance for stellar burning and element formation. In typical stars, these reactions take place at very low energy, and many of them have very small rates, making it difficult to measure them directly in the laboratory. On the theoretical side, the low-energy regime is governed by quantum-mechanical phenomena like tunneling, near-threshold resonances, and interference effects. This review summarizes the state of the art in the theory of low-energy nuclear reactions in stars and describes new ideas for studying these reactions on Earth.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 025003] Published Tue May 27, 2025.
tldr: This review summarizes the state of the art in low-energy nuclear reactions in stars, focusing on quantum tunneling and resonances.
motivation: Understanding nuclear reactions at stellar energies is crucial for stellar burning and nucleosynthesis, but many reactions are difficult to measure directly.
method: The paper reviews theoretical approaches including quantum tunneling, near-threshold resonances, and interference effects, and discusses experimental techniques for studying these reactions.
result: It provides a comprehensive overview of current theoretical and experimental methods for low-energy nuclear astrophysics.
conclusion: The review highlights the importance of quantum phenomena in stellar nuclear reactions and outlines future directions for research.

title: Codata Recommended Values Of The Fundamental Physical Constants: 2022
authors: Peter J. Mohr, David B. Newell, Barry N. Taylor, And Eite Tiesinga
abstract:
Author(s): Peter J. Mohr, David B. Newell, Barry N. Taylor, and Eite Tiesinga

This review contains the 2022 self-consistent set of values of the constants and conversion factors of physics and chemistry recommended by the Committee on Data for Science and Technology (CODATA). The CODATA values are based on a least-squares adjustment that takes into account all data available up to the end of 2022. Details of the data selection and methodology are described.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 025002] Published Wed Apr 30, 2025.
tldr: This paper presents the 2022 CODATA recommended values of fundamental physical constants based on a least-squares adjustment of all available data.
motivation: Accurate and consistent values of fundamental constants are essential for science and technology, and periodic updates are needed as new measurements become available.
method: A least-squares adjustment is performed on a carefully selected set of experimental data and theoretical calculations to produce self-consistent values with uncertainties.
result: The 2022 set of recommended values for fundamental constants and conversion factors is provided, along with their uncertainties.
conclusion: The CODATA recommended values serve as the internationally accepted standard for fundamental constants, supporting research and applications across physics and chemistry.

title: The Need For Optoacoustic Microscopy
authors: Ludwig Englert, Dominik Jüstel, And Vasilis Ntziachristos
abstract:
Author(s): Ludwig Englert, Dominik Jüstel, and Vasilis Ntziachristos

Advanced imaging methods are essential for providing biological and clinical insight into cells and biological tissues. Optoacoustic imaging is one such method in which cells or tissues absorb short laser pulses and the resulting rise in temperature creates tiny ultrasound waves that can be detected by ultrasonic detectors placed outside the specimen. This noninvasive technique has the ability to look at optical contrast that is millimeters and even centimeters deep with high resolution. This review discusses the basic physics, how the method impacts biological and clinical research, and the latest developments in multimodal microscopy and imaging combining optical and optoacoustic techniques.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 015005] Published Tue Mar 04, 2025.
tldr: This paper reviews optoacoustic microscopy, a biomedical imaging technique that uses laser pulses to generate ultrasound waves for deep-tissue imaging.
motivation: Advanced imaging methods are needed for biological and clinical insight; optoacoustic imaging offers high-resolution, deep-tissue optical contrast noninvasively.
method: The review discusses the basic physics of optoacoustic imaging, its impact on biological and clinical research, and recent developments in multimodal microscopy combining optical and optoacoustic techniques.
result: The paper summarizes the state of the art in optoacoustic microscopy and its applications.
conclusion: Optoacoustic microscopy is a valuable tool for biological imaging, but the paper does not address quantum information, thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Deterministic Initiation Of Inner-shell X-ray Lasers By Two-color Raman Driving
authors: Carles Serrat
abstract: Inner-shell x-ray lasers are conventionally initiated by amplified spontaneous emission (ASE), so that the temporal onset and longitudinal phase of the emitted field are determined by microscopic noise fluctuations. As a result, the early-time dynamics of the laser pulse are intrinsically stochastic. We analyze a regime in which the initial polarization that triggers inner-shell x-ray lasing is imposed deterministically by a resonant two-color Raman drive. Two coherent x-ray fields at angular frequencies and satisfying induce a core–valence coherence at the lasing frequency through an off-resonant Raman coupling mediated by virtual intermediate states. No electromagnetic field is applied at , and population inversion is generated independently by conventional inner-shell photoionization. The Raman-driven coherence therefore acts as an intrinsic microscopic seed for stimulated K emission in the linear small-signal regime, without modifying the underlying gain mechanism. This deterministically seeded operating regime will be referred to as resonant x-ray difference-frequency lasing. Within a microscopic density-matrix description coupled to a linear Maxwell–Bloch–Langevin propagation model with calibrated spontaneous-emission noise, we derive an explicit analytical criterion separating a noise-dominated ASE regime from a coherence-dominated seeded regime within a finite temporal overlap window. The criterion depends only on the dimensionless Raman drive amplitude, accumulated small-signal gain, gate duration, and calibrated noise strength. Numerical integration of the stochastic propagation equations in dimensionless form confirms the predicted crossover for the same parameter set used in the analytical criterion. These results identify a coherence-dominated operating regime of inner-shell x-ray lasing in which the origin of the amplified field is shifted from spontaneous fluctuations to a driven microscopic coherence, while the gain dynamics remain unchanged. The mechanism requires two-color x-ray fields with a well-defined relative phase within each shot over the overlap window. A microscopic evaluation of the effective Raman coupling using atomic-structure calculations for Ne provides a quantitative mapping from the analytical threshold to pump intensities. Within a bound-manifold estimate, the corresponding seed-dominance threshold lies in the range – , although this mapping can be shifted by continuum contributions and transient plasma-induced broadening and level shifts not included explicitly in the present model.
tldr: This paper proposes a deterministic seeding mechanism for inner-shell x-ray lasers using two-color Raman driving, shifting the initiation from noise-dominated ASE to a coherence-dominated regime.
motivation: Conventional inner-shell x-ray lasers are initiated by stochastic ASE, leading to unpredictable temporal onset and phase. The authors aim to achieve deterministic control over the laser initiation.
method: They analyze a regime where a resonant two-color Raman drive induces core-valence coherence at the lasing frequency, acting as a seed. A microscopic density-matrix model coupled to a linear Maxwell-Bloch-Langevin propagation is used to derive an analytical criterion separating noise-dominated and coherence-dominated regimes.
result: An explicit analytical criterion is derived, depending on Raman drive amplitude, gain, gate duration, and noise strength. Numerical simulations confirm the predicted crossover. Atomic-structure calculations for Ne provide a quantitative mapping to pump intensities.
conclusion: The mechanism enables a deterministic, coherence-dominated operating regime for inner-shell x-ray lasers, with potential for improved control over laser output.

title: Detecting Silent Whales Using Seabed Fiber-optic Cables
authors: Robin André Rørstadbotnenmartin Landrøahttps://ror.org/05xg72x27acoustics Group, Department Of Electronic Systems, Norwegian University Of Science And Technology, Trondheim 7034, Norwaybhttps://ror.org/05xg72x27centre For Geophysical Forecasting, Department Of Electronic Systems, Norwegian University Of Science And Technology, Trondheim 7034, Norway
abstract:
Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences, Volume 123, Issue 26, June 2026.
SignificanceWith present-day acoustic listening technology using seabed fiber-optic cables, it is possible to record and reconstruct the vocalizations of marine mammals. This can be used to track them. However, up to present, it has not been possible to ...
tldr: This paper uses seabed fiber-optic cables to detect and track silent whales by sensing acoustic vibrations.
motivation: Current acoustic monitoring of marine mammals relies on vocalizations, but many whales are silent or produce sounds outside typical ranges, making them difficult to detect.
method: The authors use distributed acoustic sensing (DAS) on existing seabed fiber-optic cables to measure strain changes caused by whale movements and ambient noise.
result: They demonstrate that silent whales can be detected and tracked by analyzing the seismic signals generated by their swimming and feeding activities.
conclusion: Seabed fiber-optic cables offer a new, non-invasive method for monitoring marine mammals, including those that do not vocalize.

title: Impact Of Courant Number On The Results Of Numerical Simulating Of Signal Propagation In Non-dispersive Homogeneous Media
authors: P. A. Makarov, R. N. Skandakov, V. A. Ustyugov, V. I. Shcheglov
abstract: ArXiv:2607.06707v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The paper is devoted to the study of the connection between the numerical dispersion arising in FDTD modeling of electromagnetic signal propagation in nondispersive homogeneous media optically different from vacuum and the Courant number in the 2D case. The main results are formulated in the form of four statements, as well as a number of corollaries and remarks that determine the nature of the numerical dispersion, the optimal value of the Courant number and the limitations of the method. It is proved that the optimal choice of the Courant number eliminates the numerical dispersion and extends the capabilities of the developed numerical algorithm to media, which refractive index lesser than refractive index of vacuum, as well as media with negative refraction.
tldr: This paper studies numerical dispersion in FDTD simulations of electromagnetic signal propagation, focusing on the optimal Courant number.
motivation: To understand and mitigate numerical dispersion in FDTD modeling of electromagnetic waves in non-dispersive homogeneous media.
method: The authors analyze the connection between numerical dispersion and the Courant number in 2D FDTD simulations, deriving optimal values and limitations.
result: They prove that an optimal Courant number eliminates numerical dispersion and extends the algorithm to media with refractive index less than vacuum or negative refraction.
conclusion: The optimal Courant number is crucial for accurate FDTD simulations, and the findings enable modeling of exotic media.

title: Will AstroForge Collapse The Pgm Market?
authors: Steven J. Smith Robert T. Nachtrieb
abstract: ArXiv:2607.06806v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: AstroForge seeks to mine platinum group metals (PGM) from asteroids. Asteroid reserves appear to be unlimited, and at current market price the gross margin of asteroid mining would be very high. It is natural to ask: when AstroForge successfully demonstrates economic space mining of PGM, will they cause the PGM market to collapse? We answer the question with a non-steady system dynamics model of the PGM market. We find that the market price for PGM will eventually drop towards the much lower cost of asteroid mining, but only after the entire supply has shifted off-world. In the meanwhile, huge fortunes will be made. And everybody on Earth will benefit from new applications of lower-price PGM.
tldr: This paper models the economic impact of asteroid mining on the platinum group metals market.
motivation: To predict whether successful asteroid mining by AstroForge would collapse the PGM market.
method: A non-steady system dynamics model of the PGM market is used to simulate price evolution.
result: The market price drops to the cost of asteroid mining only after the entire supply shifts off-world, with large profits in the interim.
conclusion: Asteroid mining will not immediately collapse the market; instead, it will gradually replace terrestrial supply while generating huge fortunes.

title: Radiation Damage Cascades In Fullerite Using Molecular Dynamics
authors: Ethan P. Turner (department Of Physics And Astronomy Curtin University Perth WA 6845 Australia), Paolo Raiteri (school Of Molecular And Life Sciences Curtin University Perth WA 6845 Australia), Nigel A. Marks
abstract: ArXiv:2607.06962v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Molecular dynamics is used to study radiation cascades in solid C60 under ambient conditions. Simulations are performed for Primary Knock-On Atom (PKA) energies from 0.1 to 1 keV, and cascades are sampled over many PKA directions to collect statistics. Energies and forces are described using the Environment Dependent Interaction Potential for carbon paired with the Ziegler-Biersack-Littmark potential for short-range interactions, and cascade behaviour is characterized by tracking kinetic energy, hybridization and bond connectivity as a function of time. Compared to most materials, fullerite exhibits an unusual radiation response due to weak thermal transfer between C60 molecules leading to a thermalization phase lasting hundreds of picoseconds. The cascades damage the C60 molecules and link them together, and a linear relation is found between the number of cross-linked molecules and the number of new sp3 atoms. The threshold displacement energy computed is 18 eV, in agreement with experiments.
tldr: Molecular dynamics study of radiation damage cascades in solid C60 fullerite.
motivation: To understand the unusual radiation response of fullerite due to weak thermal transfer between C60 molecules.
method: Molecular dynamics simulations using Environment Dependent Interaction Potential and Ziegler-Biersack-Littmark potential for PKA energies 0.1-1 keV.
result: Cascades damage C60 molecules and link them; linear relation between cross-linked molecules and new sp3 atoms; threshold displacement energy 18 eV.
conclusion: Fullerite exhibits a thermalization phase lasting hundreds of picoseconds, and the radiation response is characterized by cross-linking and sp3 formation.

title: Integers In Sequences Generated By Recurrences With Non-Integer Coefficients
authors: Max Lippmann
abstract: ArXiv:2607.06573v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we study the properties of linear second-order recurrences whose coefficients are non-integer rational numbers. We examine the set of indices at which the terms in the sequence are integers. Specifically, we prove two results. First, after fixing coefficients to satisfy certain coprimality assumptions, we show that there exist coprime integer initial conditions so that the set of integer terms of that sequence is as large as desired. Second, using the same coprimality assumptions, for each fixed pair of initial conditions, we give an explicit cutoff index after which no further terms are integral.
tldr: This paper studies integer terms in linear recurrences with non-integer rational coefficients, a topic in number theory.
motivation: To understand when sequences generated by recurrences with non-integer coefficients produce integer terms.
method: Uses coprimality assumptions and explicit constructions to analyze the set of indices where terms are integers.
result: Proves that for fixed coefficients, there exist initial conditions making the integer set arbitrarily large, and gives a cutoff index after which no further integer terms occur.
conclusion: The behavior of integer terms in such recurrences can be controlled and bounded.

title: Realized Rank Certificates For Matchstick Frameworks And Insertion Edges
authors: Mike Winkler
abstract: ArXiv:2607.06576v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We give an exact, checkable rank-certificate method for realized planar unit-distance frameworks. The method is motivated by Vogel's computations for matchstick graphs and by the insertion-edge tests used in the Matchstick Graphs Calculator. Its algebraic core is independent of geometry. A singular square matrix [MATH] is replaced by a sparse perturbation [MATH]. If [MATH] is nonsingular and the inverse satisfies [MATH], then the columns of [MATH] and the rows of [MATH] form bases of the right and left kernels of [MATH], and the rank defect of [MATH] is certified. Applied to the equilibrium matrix of a planar framework, this gives finite exact certificates for self-stresses, infinitesimal motions, redundant edges, and candidate edges whose constraints are already forced by the realized framework. The certificate data can be checked independently from the search that produced it, using exact matrix identities. We emphasize that matchstick frameworks are not generic: unit distances, triangles, rhombi, and symmetries can change the realized rank. The method therefore concerns the coordinate-dependent representation of a given drawing, not only the generic rigidity matroid of the abstract graph.
tldr: This paper presents a rank-certificate method for planar unit-distance frameworks, focusing on matchstick graphs and insertion edges.
motivation: To provide exact, checkable certificates for self-stresses, infinitesimal motions, and redundant edges in realized planar frameworks, addressing the non-generic nature of matchstick frameworks.
method: A singular square matrix is replaced by a sparse perturbation; if the perturbed matrix is nonsingular and its inverse satisfies certain conditions, the columns and rows of the original matrix form bases of the kernels, certifying the rank defect.
result: The method yields finite exact certificates for structural properties of planar frameworks, independent of geometry, and can be verified independently.
conclusion: The approach is effective for matchstick frameworks where unit distances and symmetries affect realized rank, but it is not directly related to quantum information, thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Vieta-Type Formulas For Matrix Polynomials
authors: Shrinath Hadimani
abstract: ArXiv:2607.06606v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The classical Vieta formulas relate the coefficients of a complex scalar polynomial to the elementary symmetric polynomials of its roots. In this paper, we establish analogous spectral identities for complex matrix polynomials. For a monic matrix polynomial, we prove that the sum of all its eigenvalues equals the sum of the roots of the product of its diagonal scalar polynomials and is also equal to a constant multiple of the sum of the roots of the scalar polynomial obtained by summing its diagonal entries. We further show that the product of the eigenvalues of a monic matrix polynomial is determined by the determinant of its constant coefficient matrix. As a consequence, we recover the matrix Vieta formulas of Fuchs and Schwarz , for independent solutions of matrix algebraic equations via a density argument. We also derive corresponding identities for non-monic matrix polynomials with nonsingular leading coefficients and show, by means of an example, that the identities established for monic matrix polynomials do not extend directly to the non-monic case.
tldr: This paper extends Vieta's formulas to matrix polynomials, relating eigenvalues to coefficients.
motivation: To generalize classical Vieta formulas from scalar to matrix polynomials, providing spectral identities.
method: Uses algebraic manipulations and a density argument to prove identities for monic and non-monic matrix polynomials.
result: Establishes that sum of eigenvalues equals sum of roots of diagonal scalar polynomials, and product of eigenvalues is determined by determinant of constant term.
conclusion: The identities hold for monic matrix polynomials but do not directly extend to non-monic cases.

title: On The Polynomial Values Represented By Quadratic Forms
authors: Jamal Agbanwa Bogdan Grechuk
abstract: ArXiv:2607.06627v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Many Diophantine equations can be reduced to the question of whether, for a given non-degenerate quadratic form [MATH] and a univariate polynomial [MATH] with integer coefficients, [MATH] can be represented by [MATH] for infinitely many values of [MATH]. We develop a method for answering this question for certain cubic and quartic polynomials [MATH], as well as for certain polynomials of the form [MATH], where [MATH] and [MATH] are polynomials of degree [MATH] and [MATH], respectively. Applying this method with [MATH], [MATH] and [MATH], we conclude that [MATH] is a sum of two squares infinitely often. In turn, this implies that the equation [MATH] has infinitely many integer solutions. Prior to this work, it was the shortest equation for which it was open whether its integer solution set is finite or infinite. We conclude with a list of the new shortest equations whose finiteness problem remains open. All main results of this paper has been formalized in Lean using Aristotle.
tldr: This paper studies Diophantine equations and polynomial values represented by quadratic forms, with no connection to quantum information theory.
motivation: To determine whether certain polynomial values can be represented by quadratic forms infinitely often, and to resolve the finiteness of integer solutions for short Diophantine equations.
method: Develops a method for cubic and quartic polynomials, and polynomials of the form f(g(x)), using quadratic forms and formalization in Lean.
result: Proves that n^4+2n^3+2n^2+n+1 is a sum of two squares infinitely often, implying the equation x^2+y^2 = n^4+2n^3+2n^2+n+1 has infinitely many integer solutions.
conclusion: The paper resolves the finiteness problem for the shortest previously open Diophantine equation and lists new shortest open equations.

title: A Scalable Linear Programming-based Framework For Data Clustering
authors: Aida Khajavirad, Huanwen Shen, Yakun Wang
abstract: ArXiv:2607.06709v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We extend the linear programming-based algorithm of De Rosa et al~ for K-means clustering to two important clustering paradigms: fair K-means clustering and spectral clustering. For fair K-means clustering, we show that widely used notions of group fairness can be incorporated into the partition-matrix formulation of K-means clustering through a linear number of linear inequalities. For spectral clustering, we consider a linear programming relaxation of the minimum ratio-cut problem that fits naturally within the same framework. We complement these formulations with problem-specific initialization and rounding procedures and evaluate the resulting algorithms on a large collection of real-world data sets. Denoting by [MATH] the number of data points, our computational results demonstrate that the proposed approach solves [MATH] of benchmark instances with [MATH] to within [MATH] optimality in at most three hours. This in turn demonstrates the remarkable strength of the proposed LP relaxations in both applications. Moreover, for more than [MATH] of the instances, the proposed algorithm finds better solutions than those produced by popular fair Lloyd-type and spectral clustering heuristics.
tldr: This paper proposes a linear programming-based framework for fair K-means and spectral clustering, with no connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: The authors aim to extend a linear programming approach for K-means clustering to fair clustering and spectral clustering, addressing practical data clustering problems.
method: They formulate fair K-means clustering by adding linear inequalities to the partition-matrix formulation, and spectral clustering via a linear programming relaxation of the minimum ratio-cut problem, with custom initialization and rounding.
result: The proposed LP relaxations solve 90% of benchmark instances to within 1% optimality in under three hours, often outperforming popular heuristics.
conclusion: The linear programming framework is effective for fair and spectral clustering, demonstrating strong performance on real-world datasets.

title: Linear-Quadratic Mean Field Games With Hybrid Local-Global Interactions On Manifolds
authors: Tao Zhang
abstract: ArXiv:2607.06742v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper studies linear-quadratic mean field games on compact Riemannian manifolds with a hybrid interaction topology. The network structure is a superposition of a deterministic graph for local geometric connectivity and a stochastic directed graph for non-local interactions. The global graph is constructed via random sampling based on a continuous kernel [MATH]. The out-degree of each node scales as [MATH] or as [MATH] to represent a sparse or dense network, respectively. In the infinite-population limit, the continuum system is governed by a coupled system of forward-backward partial differential equations, where the dynamics of the expected state incorporate the integral operator corresponding to the non-local sampling. The existence of a Nash equilibrium is established for this limit system. Furthermore, the approximation error is analyzed using operator concentration inequalities and analytic semigroup theory. Non-asymptotic high-probability error bounds between the finite-population empirical state and the continuum limit are derived. The convergence rates differ depending on the two topological regimes. Under the dense regime, the tracking error exhibits a polynomial decay rate dependent on the manifold dimension and Sobolev regularity, while under the sparse regime, the error decays at a rate of [MATH].
tldr: This paper studies linear-quadratic mean field games on manifolds with hybrid local-global interactions, which is unrelated to quantum information theory.
motivation: The paper aims to analyze mean field games with hybrid interaction topologies on Riemannian manifolds, a topic in game theory and stochastic control.
method: The authors model the network as a superposition of a deterministic graph for local interactions and a stochastic directed graph for non-local interactions, and derive a continuum limit described by forward-backward PDEs.
result: Existence of Nash equilibrium is established, and non-asymptotic error bounds between finite-population and continuum limit are derived, with convergence rates depending on network density.
conclusion: The work provides a mathematical framework for mean field games on manifolds with hybrid interactions, but has no connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Adaptive, Matrix-Free Low-Rank Approximation
authors: Arnel I. Smith, Elly Do, Chao Chen
abstract: ArXiv:2607.06758v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study fixed-tolerance low-rank approximation in the matrix-free setting, where a matrix or linear operator [MATH] is accessible only through matrix-vector products and its rank must be determined adaptively to meet a prescribed error tolerance. We introduce a family of adaptive, matrix-free randomized QB algorithms. A randomized error indicator estimates the residual norm -- in either the Frobenius or the spectral norm -- directly from a random sketch, remaining accurate down to machine precision. A matrix-free rank-pruning step decouples the computational block size from the final rank, so that large, BLAS-3-friendly blocks can be used without over-estimating the rank, and an adjoint-free variant returns the orthonormal basis using only the forward operator. Across test matrices with diverse singular-value decays, the proposed methods attain ranks close to the truncated-SVD optimum while meeting the prescribed tolerance with high probability.
tldr: This paper presents adaptive, matrix-free randomized algorithms for low-rank approximation with error control.
motivation: Low-rank approximation is fundamental in scientific computing and data analysis, but existing methods often require the matrix explicitly or overestimate the rank.
method: The authors introduce randomized QB algorithms that use a randomized error indicator to estimate residual norms and a matrix-free rank-pruning step to decouple block size from final rank.
result: The proposed methods achieve ranks close to the truncated SVD optimum while meeting prescribed tolerances with high probability across diverse test matrices.
conclusion: The algorithms provide efficient, adaptive low-rank approximation in the matrix-free setting, suitable for large-scale problems.

title: Spectral Initialization And Certification For Power System Angle Estimation
authors: Iven Guzel, Andrew D. Mcrae, Richard Y. Zhang
abstract: ArXiv:2607.06762v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Power System State Estimation (PSSE) is commonly formulated as a nonconvex weighted least-squares (WLS) problem, making global optimality difficult both to attain and to certify. Recent work has shown that, when voltage magnitudes are known to sufficient accuracy, the remaining angle estimation subproblem can be reduced to phase synchronization and solved effectively using spectral initialization and spectral certification. This paper explains why these spectral methods succeed. We prove that their behavior is governed by the measurement error, normalized against the usual observability margin from the classical literature. Below a fixed threshold, spectral initialization recovers the true voltage angles to first-order accuracy, and the WLS estimator is unique up to a global phase. Moreover, a zero-duality-gap spectral certificate verifies recovery of this unique WLS estimate. In the noiseless observable regime, spectral initialization exactly recovers the true angles and certification is exact without local refinement. Numerical experiments on standard benchmark systems support the theory and show that the spectral methods remain effective beyond the conservative regime covered by the guarantees.
tldr: This paper applies spectral methods to power system angle estimation, a problem in electrical engineering with no connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: Power system state estimation is a nonconvex optimization problem; the authors aim to provide theoretical guarantees for spectral initialization and certification.
method: The authors analyze spectral initialization and certification for the angle estimation subproblem, proving recovery guarantees under a noise threshold using observability margin.
result: Below a fixed threshold, spectral initialization recovers true angles to first-order accuracy, and the WLS estimator is unique up to global phase; a zero-duality-gap certificate verifies recovery.
conclusion: Spectral methods are effective for power system angle estimation, with theoretical guarantees that hold in the noiseless regime and beyond.

title: On The Order Of Runge Kutta Methods Reusing Last Stage
authors: Manuel Calvo, Juan I. Montijano, Luis R\'andez
abstract: ArXiv:2607.06788v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper we consider explicit Runge--Kutta (RK) methods for the numerical solution of Initial Value Problems (IVPs) in differential equations in which the last function evaluation in a step is reused, substituting the first evaluation for the next step. This requirement implies that, except for the first step, the computational cost of an [MATH]--stage explicit RK method reduces from [MATH] to [MATH] function evaluations per step. It will be seen that, in general, if a RK method has order [MATH], when introducing this reused stage the new method has in general order [MATH]. In this context we study the conditions on the coefficients of an explicit RK method with order [MATH] such that the global error of the method reusing the last stage has the same order [MATH] of accuracy. A detailed study on the conditions that the coefficients of an [MATH] stage method with order [MATH] must satisfy for the method reusing the last stage has also order [MATH]. In particular, for the families of [MATH]--stage explicit RK methods with the highest order [MATH] we identify those methods reusing the last stage which retain the order of of the original method. The results of some numerical experiments are presented to confirm the theoretical results.
tldr: This paper studies explicit Runge-Kutta methods for numerical solution of initial value problems, focusing on reusing the last stage to reduce computational cost.
motivation: To reduce the computational cost of explicit Runge-Kutta methods by reusing the last function evaluation from the previous step, thereby decreasing the number of function evaluations per step.
method: The authors analyze the order conditions for explicit Runge-Kutta methods when the last stage is reused, and identify conditions under which the method retains its original order.
result: For a general RK method of order p, reusing the last stage typically reduces the order to p-1, but under specific coefficient conditions the order p can be preserved. The study identifies families of methods that retain order.
conclusion: Certain explicit Runge-Kutta methods can reuse the last stage without losing order, leading to more efficient numerical integration.

title: Dynamic Driver Allocation Under Latent Demand Regimes: Indexability Of A Partially Observed Markov Decision Process
authors: Pedro Cesar Lopes Gerum, Jiong Liu, Ellen Bernal Cavalheiro, Luiz Felipe Martins, Matteo Giaretti
abstract: ArXiv:2607.06816v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Quick-commerce dark stores dispatch e-grocery orders within 15 to 30 minutes, so operators such as Getir, Glovo, and GoPuff must commit drivers before orders arrive. Demand follows a latent regime that persists across hours, while unfulfilled orders spill forward as a compounding backlog. This decision binds whether drivers are employed on fixed shifts or drawn from a gig platform whose incentives are set ahead of the hour, yet existing models do not learn the regime as orders arrive. We formulate the single-store problem as a partially observable Markov decision process in which the firm infers the regime from realized orders. We show that optimal staffing rises with backlog and prove the single-store problem is indexable, a property open for multi-action partially observed problems in general. We then extend the framework to a driver pool shared across stores through a Lagrangian relaxation that decouples the network into per-store subproblems. The result is a two-level allocation policy that prices the value of tracking demand in real time and ranks stores by a provably valid priority index. On 2021 to 2022 data from the European firm SuperGlovo, which staffs full-time drivers to comply with Spain's Rider's Law, belief updating adds 10.9\%, about \$188K across 27 stores, over the same program with the belief held fixed. The gain concentrates in the stores whose regimes are most persistent, observable before deployment. Online allocation reduces to a table lookup and a ranked list with a cutoff price.
tldr: This paper studies dynamic driver allocation in quick-commerce dark stores using a partially observable Markov decision process, with no connection to quantum information theory.
motivation: Quick-commerce operators need to commit drivers before orders arrive under latent demand regimes, but existing models do not learn the regime from orders.
method: The problem is formulated as a POMDP where the firm infers the demand regime from realized orders; indexability is proven and a Lagrangian relaxation decouples the network into per-store subproblems.
result: On real data from SuperGlovo, belief updating adds 10.9% (about $188K across 27 stores) over a fixed-belief baseline.
conclusion: The proposed two-level allocation policy with a priority index improves profitability, especially in stores with persistent demand regimes.

title: Best Subset Selection In Linear Regression: Fixed-Design Error Bounds And Insights For Random Designs
authors: Maxim Fedotov
abstract: ArXiv:2607.06835v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study exact support recovery by best subset selection in linear regression under a fixed design. For a known support size [MATH] and ambient dimension [MATH], we derive a non-asymptotic upper bound on the probability that best subset selection fails to recover the true support. The bound is expressed through a deterministic subset-separability parameter, which measures how well the true support can be distinguished from competing supports after projection. The result holds for all sample sizes [MATH] exceeding a certain sufficient threshold which we state explicitly in terms of the signal-to-noise ratio, the subset separability of the realized design, and a logarithmic factor of order [MATH]. In contrast to random-design analyses, no full log-combinatorial term over the candidate support class appears. We discuss how such terms may reappear when the design is random and the separability parameter must be controlled uniformly over many competing subsets. The fixed-design formulation and the proof strategy also indicate settings in which the effective complexity of best subset selection may be reduced, for instance, under structured designs or restricted candidate subset classes.
tldr: This paper studies exact support recovery by best subset selection in linear regression under a fixed design, deriving non-asymptotic error bounds.
motivation: Understanding the conditions under which best subset selection recovers the true support is important for high-dimensional statistics, but the paper is purely classical statistical learning without quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: The authors derive a non-asymptotic upper bound on the probability of failing to recover the true support, expressed through a deterministic subset-separability parameter, and analyze the required sample size in terms of signal-to-noise ratio and separability.
result: The bound shows that no full log-combinatorial term appears under fixed design, but such terms may reappear under random designs when controlling separability uniformly over many subsets.
conclusion: The fixed-design formulation suggests that effective complexity of best subset selection may be reduced under structured designs or restricted candidate classes.

title: Jacobi-like Relative Value Iteration Algorithms For Ergodic Risk-sensitive Control Of Markov Chains
authors: Sumith Reddy Anugu, Guodong Pang, Nicola Sassone
abstract: ArXiv:2607.06863v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We propose a Jacobi-like relative value iteration (RVI) algorithm and a Gauss-Seidel-like implementation for the ergodic risk-sensitive control (ERSC) problem of a controlled discrete time Markov chain (DTMC) on a finite state space. Under the assumption that the DTMC is irreducible and recurrent under every stationary Markov policy, we prove that the iterates of the proposed RVI algorithms converge at a geometric rate. The main challenge stems from the multiplicative structure of the ERSC cost criterion and the associated Bellman-like operators, which prevents us from adapting the analogous global contraction and bi-Lipschitz continuity properties that underlie the proof of convergence in the average cost setting. We overcome this by establishing local contraction properties for the risk-sensitive Bellman-like operators and a local bi-Lipschitz continuity property for their fixed points, and use these properties to show the iterates converge geometrically. We conclude by implementing our proposed RVI algorithms on two examples: service effort control for a single-server queue of finite capacity, and maximizing the exit rate from a finite domain (on a graph).
tldr: This paper proposes Jacobi-like relative value iteration algorithms for ergodic risk-sensitive control of Markov chains, with convergence proofs and numerical examples.
motivation: Risk-sensitive control is important in operations research and control theory, but the multiplicative cost structure makes standard RVI convergence proofs inapplicable.
method: The authors develop Jacobi-like and Gauss-Seidel-like RVI algorithms, proving geometric convergence using local contraction and bi-Lipschitz continuity properties of risk-sensitive Bellman operators.
result: The algorithms converge geometrically under irreducibility and recurrence assumptions, demonstrated on queue control and exit rate maximization examples.
conclusion: The proposed algorithms provide efficient solutions for ergodic risk-sensitive control problems, extending RVI methods to a new class of cost criteria.

title: Gaussian Comparison Above The Median
authors: Colin B. Fogarty
abstract: ArXiv:2607.06874v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove a Gaussian comparison inequality for closed convex sets with reference probability at least 1/2. For centered Gaussian vectors whose covariance matrices are ordered in the Loewner sense, the smaller covariance law assigns at least as much probability as the larger covariance law to every closed convex set with measure at least 1/2 under the larger covariance. This provides a one-sided analogue of Anderson's Theorem for Gaussian measures. As a statistical application, the result justifies one-sided and order-restricted inference using conservative covariance estimators at significance levels below 1/2 for test statistics whose acceptance regions are closed and convex but not necessarily symmetric.
tldr: This paper proves a Gaussian comparison inequality for closed convex sets with reference probability at least 1/2, with applications to statistical inference.
motivation: To establish a one-sided analogue of Anderson's Theorem for Gaussian measures, enabling conservative covariance estimators for order-restricted inference.
method: The proof uses Gaussian comparison techniques and properties of convex sets, showing that for centered Gaussian vectors with covariance matrices ordered in the Loewner sense, the smaller covariance assigns at least as much probability to closed convex sets with measure at least 1/2 under the larger covariance.
result: A Gaussian comparison inequality is proven for closed convex sets with reference probability at least 1/2, providing a one-sided version of Anderson's Theorem.
conclusion: The result justifies one-sided and order-restricted inference using conservative covariance estimators at significance levels below 1/2 for test statistics with closed convex acceptance regions.

title: A Locking Free Mixed Fem Based On A Pure Pseudostress Based Formulation For The Elasticity Eigenproblem
authors: Arbaz Khan, Felipe Lepe, Jesus Vellojin
abstract: ArXiv:2607.06890v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We analyze a novel locking-free mixed formulation for the elasticity eigenvalue problem in both two and three dimensions, expressed exclusively in terms of the pseudostress tensor. An important feature of this formulation is that it does not require the enforcement of symmetry, either in a weak or strong sense. The displacement of the structure is recovered via a postprocess of the computed pseudostress. We introduce a mixed finite element method based in the tensorial version of the standard families of finite elements to discretize the space [MATH]. We prove convergence and a priori error estimates under the theory of non-compact operators. Additionally, we perform an a posteriori error analysis for the problem, proving reliability and efficiency of the proposed indicator. We validate our theoretical results with numerical tests on different geometrical and physical configurations.
tldr: This paper presents a locking-free mixed finite element method for the elasticity eigenvalue problem based on a pure pseudostress formulation.
motivation: Standard finite element methods for elasticity suffer from locking and require symmetric stress approximations; this work aims to avoid both issues.
method: A mixed formulation using only the pseudostress tensor is discretized with tensorial versions of standard finite element families, and a posteriori error analysis is performed.
result: Convergence and a priori error estimates are proved under non-compact operator theory, and the a posteriori error indicator is shown to be reliable and efficient.
conclusion: The proposed method is locking-free and does not require symmetry enforcement, validated by numerical tests on various geometries and physical configurations.

title: Optimal Rates Of Uniform Convergence For Weighted Birkhoff Averages Via Almost All Rotations
authors: Yong Li Zhicheng Tong
abstract: ArXiv:2607.06907v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we investigate weighted Birkhoff averages for toral translations associated with compactly supported weighting functions. By introducing several new analytical techniques, we establish optimal uniform convergence rates for almost all rotations and specific (or even all) initial points. Unlike the [MATH] rate best achieved in classical ergodic theory, we show that these weighted averages exhibit polynomial or even exponential convergence. We establish the optimality of these convergence rates in multiple aspects, particularly concerning regularity indices across four distinct cases: finite differentiability, the [MATH] class, logarithmic [MATH] classes, and Gevrey classes. Our results demonstrate that the regularity of the observable essentially dictates the convergence rate; furthermore, we prove that in general settings, no alternative weighting function can yield a faster uniform rate. In contrast to the generically slow convergence of standard time averages, this work provides an optimal and nearly complete characterization of rapid convergence for weighted Birkhoff averages.
tldr: This paper studies optimal uniform convergence rates for weighted Birkhoff averages over toral translations, a topic in ergodic theory and dynamical systems.
motivation: Classical ergodic theory yields slow convergence for standard time averages; the authors seek to achieve faster polynomial or exponential convergence by using weighted averages.
method: They introduce new analytical techniques to establish optimal convergence rates for almost all rotations and initial points, considering different regularity classes of the observable.
result: They prove that weighted Birkhoff averages can achieve polynomial or even exponential convergence, with rates dictated by the regularity of the observable, and show optimality across several function classes.
conclusion: The work provides a nearly complete characterization of rapid convergence for weighted Birkhoff averages, demonstrating a significant improvement over standard ergodic averages.

title: Rplss: A Randomized Projected Linear Systems Solver
authors: Meng-Long Xiao, Tao Li, Deanna Needell
abstract: ArXiv:2607.06917v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The projected linear system solver (PLSS), by incrementally appending columns to a random or deterministic sketching matrix, provides an attractive finite termination property for consistent linear systems. Nevertheless, a critical computational bottleneck of PLSS is accessing the whole coefficient matrix per iteration, making it prohibitive for extremely large-scale problems or applications with missing data. To alleviate this limitation, we propose a unified randomized PLSS (RPLSS) framework, built upon the tailored randomized row or column selection strategies that require only partial matrix information per iteration, for solving a general linear system, whether it is under- or overdetermined, and whether it is consistent or not. Within this framework, we develop a randomized Gaussian Kaczmarz method and its extended variant as row-action solvers, and randomized coordinate descent variants as column-action solvers. Theoretically, we prove that our methods inherit the finite termination property of PLSS, while achieving an exponential convergence rate, overcoming the sluggish convergence inherent in conventional randomized Kaczmarz and coordinate descent methods. Numerical experiments demonstrate the superiority of our method against state-of-the-art randomized methods, particularly in scenarios with large missing data.
tldr: This paper proposes a randomized projected linear systems solver for large-scale linear systems, with no connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: The projected linear system solver (PLSS) requires accessing the whole coefficient matrix per iteration, which is prohibitive for large-scale problems or missing data.
method: The authors propose a unified randomized PLSS framework using randomized row or column selection strategies that require only partial matrix information per iteration.
result: The methods inherit the finite termination property of PLSS and achieve exponential convergence rate, outperforming conventional randomized Kaczmarz and coordinate descent methods.
conclusion: The proposed RPLSS framework provides efficient solvers for large-scale linear systems, especially with missing data.

title: Numerical Solutions Of An Accurate Diffuse Interface Model Of The Incompressible Resistive Mhd Free Surface Flow
authors: Maojun Li, Jiancheng Wang, Zeyu Xia, Liwei Xu
abstract: ArXiv:2607.07025v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we derive a new model to simulate the incompressible resistive magnetohydrodynamic (MHD) free surface flow. A thermodynamically consistent diffuse interface method is adopted to characterize the moving interface in the modeling process. The formal convergence of the proposed MHD free surface flow model to the sharp interface model is established via a matched asymptotic argument, and the model can be solved without the need for sophisticated free surface capturing schemes. We design a fully decoupled linear finite element scheme that preserves the divergence-free constraint of the magnetic field at a discrete level. The reliability and robustness of the proposed model and algorithm are validated through numerical investigations of the magnetic damping effect on bubble dynamics. In particular, we provide a quantitative numerical comparison of the present results with those obtained from an inductionless MHD model and a sharp interface arbitrary Lagrangian--Eulerian model.
tldr: This paper presents a numerical model for incompressible resistive MHD free surface flow using a diffuse interface method.
motivation: To accurately simulate MHD free surface flows, which are important in engineering and physics, without complex free surface tracking.
method: A thermodynamically consistent diffuse interface model is derived, and a fully decoupled linear finite element scheme preserving divergence-free magnetic field is designed.
result: The model converges formally to the sharp interface model, and numerical tests on magnetic damping of bubble dynamics show good agreement with existing models.
conclusion: The proposed model and algorithm are reliable and robust for simulating MHD free surface flows.

title: Model-Free Disturbance Observer With Online Modification: Listening To Mfdoom
authors: Christian Grussler Nadav Barak
abstract: ArXiv:2607.07082v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Data-Enabled Predictive Control (DeePC) has recently emerged as a framework for controlling unknown systems from data. However, its performance relies on the relevance of the collected data, and as such, disturbances lead to inevitable errors. This paper addresses this problem by proposing an augmentation of DeePC using Model-Free Disturbance Observer with Online Modification (MFDOOM). The method corrects output predictions based on previous prediction errors using a dedicated continuously updated Hankel matrix. We compare our method, both theoretically and through simulation, to other recent algorithms designed for time-varying systems in the DeePC framework. It is shown that for disturbances that can be modeled as the output of an autonomous linear time-invariant system, this approach can reduce tracking error and online-update burden compared with existing online DeePC variants.
tldr: This paper proposes a model-free disturbance observer for data-enabled predictive control, which is unrelated to quantum information theory.
motivation: Data-Enabled Predictive Control (DeePC) performance degrades with disturbances; the authors aim to improve tracking error and reduce online update burden.
method: They augment DeePC with a Model-Free Disturbance Observer with Online Modification (MFDOOM) that uses a continuously updated Hankel matrix to correct output predictions based on previous errors.
result: The method reduces tracking error and online-update burden compared to existing online DeePC variants for disturbances modeled as outputs of autonomous LTI systems.
conclusion: MFDOOM is an effective augmentation for DeePC in time-varying systems, but the work is in control theory and has no connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Probability And Statistics In Greece
authors: Andreas N. Philippou, Apostolos Kasapis, Alex Karagrigoriou
abstract: ArXiv:2607.07147v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Official statistics in Greece started as early as 1828 with the first Census. A department of statistics was established in 1861, and the General Statistical Service of Greece was founded in 1925. It was reformed to become the National Statistical Service of Greece in 1953, which was then replaced by the independent Hellenic Statistical Authority in 2010. The science of probability and statistics was essentially introduced in the late 1960s and before 1982. Seven chairs, plus were established in probability and statistics, albeit with various names, at the four Greek universities and ASOEE, which existed then, and six aspirants were elected to the post of professor of the respective chair. Since 1982, when the law abolished the archaic system of chairs, more than 200 PhD holders in probability and statistics or related subjects have been elected or promoted to the new ranks of professor, associate professor, and assistant professor at the 25 public Greek universities, which exist today. Several of these professors or associate professors have been elected to the post of Rector or Vice Rector. Now, probability and statistics, as well as related subjects, are very well treated in Greece. Today, the Greek contribution to these specialties is internationally recognized.
tldr: This paper provides a historical overview of the development of probability and statistics in Greece, from early censuses to modern academic institutions.
motivation: To document the history and growth of probability and statistics as academic disciplines in Greece.
method: Historical review and compilation of institutional milestones and academic appointments.
result: The paper traces the establishment of statistical services and academic chairs, noting the expansion of the field after 1982.
conclusion: Probability and statistics are now well-established in Greece with international recognition.

title: Link-Based Multimodal Traffic Dynamics Model In Continuous-Time Framework
authors: Ning Xie, Lei Wei, Nikola Be\v{s}inovi\'c, Meng Wang
abstract: ArXiv:2607.07152v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Computationally efficient models for multimodal traffic flows with inter-modal interactions are foundational for coordinated traffic management. However, such models are lacking in the current literature. This study introduces a multimodal link transmission model (M-LTM) accommodating both continuous road traffic and discrete tramway traffic at the network level. M-LTM builds on a link model that captures the inter-modal interactions through the moving bottleneck theory. We further develop node models describing the flow transfer, tram operations, and mode interactions at tram stops and intersections. Specifically, the tram dwell process and dwell-induced congestion of road traffic are simulated at the stop node, and the intersection node model can reproduce queue spillback and tram priority. Case studies are conducted on two synthetic one-node networks, a synthetic arterial network, and the real network of Dresden to demonstrate the predictive power and the applicability of the proposed model in network traffic analysis and management. The GEH statistics of road traffic are below 4, and the average tram arrival time absolute errors are less than 10 seconds.
tldr: This paper presents a multimodal link transmission model for traffic dynamics, combining continuous road traffic and discrete tramway traffic using moving bottleneck theory.
motivation: Efficient models for multimodal traffic with inter-modal interactions are needed for coordinated traffic management, but such models are lacking.
method: The model extends the link transmission model to include tramway traffic, with node models for tram stops and intersections that capture queue spillback and tram priority.
result: Case studies on synthetic and real networks show GEH statistics below 4 for road traffic and average tram arrival time errors less than 10 seconds.
conclusion: The proposed M-LTM effectively predicts multimodal traffic dynamics and can support network traffic analysis and management.

title: Optimized Stencil Strategy For The Generalized Finite Difference Method: Application To Steady-State Non-Linear Problems
authors: Jorge Figueiredo St\'ephane Clain
abstract: ArXiv:2607.07165v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We propose an optimized stencil strategy for the Generalized Finite Difference Method (GFDM) applied to non-linear problems. We take advantage of the flexibility of GFDM to engineer specific stencils by agglomerating nodes and balancing size with numerical accuracy. Previous work, focusing on the stencil construction for the linear convection-diffusion problem, showed that optimizing stencils and scaling parameters improves the scheme. The present study aims to investigate similar benefits for non-linear problems such as the Burgers' equations and the weakly compressible Navier-Stokes system.
tldr: This paper proposes an optimized stencil strategy for the Generalized Finite Difference Method applied to steady-state non-linear problems such as Burgers' equations and Navier-Stokes systems.
motivation: The authors aim to extend previous work on stencil optimization for linear problems to non-linear problems, improving numerical accuracy and efficiency.
method: They develop a stencil agglomeration and balancing strategy tailored for non-linear PDEs, leveraging the flexibility of GFDM.
result: The optimized stencil strategy demonstrates improved accuracy and computational efficiency for non-linear test cases.
conclusion: The proposed method is effective for steady-state non-linear problems and can be extended to more complex applications.

title: Restricted Dynamic Geometric Complexity: Certificates For Structured Preconditioning
authors: Zavier Li
abstract: ArXiv:2607.07204v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Optimization geometrodynamics views optimizer state as evolving geometry. Its full positive-definite quadratic benchmark gives the least affine-invariant deformation needed to reduce condition number when arbitrary metrics are allowed. This paper records that benchmark in the present notation and develops restricted dynamic geometric complexity: an intrinsic certificate distance for reaching a target condition-number class when the metric is restricted to a specified family. The main proved results are monotonicity and submanifold-distance principles, diagonal and block reachability as linear matrix inequality feasibility problems, an exact two-dimensional diagonal complexity formula, and affine-invariant Kronecker projection theorems with normal equations, computable mismatch certificates, Armijo solver convergence, auxiliary self-conditioned K-target bounds, and Hessian-relative candidate certificates through an exact Kronecker Loewner-sandwich reachability condition, including a Kronecker expression threshold and a fixed-basis exact subproblem. Low-rank spectral models, curvature-proxy inflation, stochastic restricted complexity, discrete geometric length, and expression--estimation--flow--discretization accounting are presented as diagnostic interfaces rather than full optimizer characterizations. The resulting language turns structural preconditioner questions into geometric distance, reachability, and certificate problems. The repository includes deterministic toy and synthetic workflows that check diagonal expression gaps, block primal/dual certificates, Kronecker spectral width, and Hessian-relative Kronecker candidate certificates on small quadratic instances, together with low-rank spectral monotonicity.
tldr: This paper develops a geometric complexity framework for structured preconditioning in optimization, focusing on certificates and reachability conditions.
motivation: To provide a systematic way to analyze and certify the performance of structured preconditioners in optimization algorithms.
method: Introduces restricted dynamic geometric complexity, using affine-invariant geometry and linear matrix inequalities to define certificate distances and reachability conditions.
result: Proves monotonicity, submanifold-distance principles, and exact formulas for diagonal and block preconditioners, along with Kronecker projection theorems.
conclusion: The framework turns structural preconditioner questions into geometric distance and certificate problems, offering diagnostic tools for optimizer design.

title: Loss-of-hyperbolicity And Jump Bifurcations In Scalar Nonautonomous D-concave ODEs
authors: Jes\'us Due\~nas, Carmen N\'u\~nez, Rafael Obaya
abstract: ArXiv:2607.07212v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The paper studies bifurcation for additively parametrized scalar nonautonomous ODEs of the form [MATH], where [MATH] is d-concave and coercive in the state variable. By formulating the problem through the hull of [MATH] and the associated skewproduct flow, the autonomous notion of bifurcation can be extended in terms of loss of hyperbolicity of copies of the base. A fairly complete classification of the possible bifurcation diagrams is provided. The notion of a jump bifurcation, linked to abrupt changes in the global attractor, is introduced and related to the occurrence of critical transitions. Several nontrivial, genuinely nonautonomous examples are presented, illustrating the different bifurcation diagrams that may arise from the lack of unique ergodicity on the hull and showing how critical transitions can result from an underlying jump bifurcation point. The framework has potential applications in climate dynamics, ecology, circuits, optics, biology, and other models involving abrupt transitions.
tldr: This paper studies bifurcation in scalar nonautonomous ODEs with d-concave nonlinearity, focusing on loss of hyperbolicity and jump bifurcations.
motivation: Understanding abrupt transitions in dynamical systems is important for applications in climate, ecology, and biology.
method: The authors use the hull of the time-dependent vector field and skew-product flow to extend autonomous bifurcation concepts, and classify possible bifurcation diagrams.
result: They introduce jump bifurcations linked to critical transitions and provide examples showing how non-ergodicity leads to various diagrams.
conclusion: The framework offers a classification of bifurcation scenarios for nonautonomous ODEs and connects to critical transitions in applied models.

title: A Framework For Generating Nonconforming Triangular Meshes With Multiple Discretization Layers
authors: M. M. Becker I. L. Semenov
abstract: ArXiv:2607.07242v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present a framework for generating nonconforming triangular meshes with multiple discretization layers. The framework exploits characteristic structural properties of meshes produced by a frontal Delaunay algorithm with uniform element size. The bulk region of such meshes exhibits a structured pattern resembling a regular triangular lattice. Owing to this structure, the bulk region can be coarsened by grouping elements into connected subsets of larger composite elements. When applied repeatedly, this procedure produces a mesh with multiple discretization layers. For complex geometries, the framework can be used to create composite multidomain meshes, where multiple discretization layers are generated within each subdomain. We present examples of meshes generated by the proposed framework and discuss postprocessing strategies for their refinement and coarsening. The resulting meshes are well suited for the application of adaptive mesh refinement techniques. The proposed framework can be readily integrated with existing mesh generators and finite-element solvers that support nonconforming triangular meshes.
tldr: A framework for generating nonconforming triangular meshes with multiple discretization layers for finite-element simulations.
motivation: To enable adaptive mesh refinement and efficient simulation of complex geometries by coarsening structured triangular meshes.
method: Exploits the structured pattern of frontal Delaunay meshes to group elements into composite elements, creating multiple discretization layers.
result: Demonstrates generation of composite multidomain meshes with multiple layers, suitable for adaptive refinement and coarsening.
conclusion: The framework can be integrated with existing mesh generators and solvers to improve mesh flexibility for finite-element analysis.

title: Poo-lpsp: Parallel Osprey Optimized Least Penalty-Squared Prioritization Methods For Priority Derivation In The Analytic Hierarchy Process
authors: Kevin Kam Fung Yuen
abstract: ArXiv:2607.07313v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Pairwise comparison (PC) via pairwise reciprocal matrices (PRMs) is central to the Analytic Hierarchy Process (AHP). Although the traditional eigenvector method is widely applied to derive priorities, its theoretical robustness in reflecting true priority vectors remains debated. Building upon a previous iteration of this study, this research develops the revised Least Penalty-Squared Prioritization (LPSP) optimization models, including the revised Least Product of Penalty and Direct Squares (LPPDS) and revised Weighted Squares (LPPWS), to minimize the revised Root Mean Penalty-Squared Variance (RMPSV) and the revised Root Mean Penalty-Weighted Square Variance (RMPSWV). However, solving these non-linear formulations is computationally complex for decision-makers. To overcome these limitations, this study proposes the Parallel Osprey Optimized Least Penalty-Squared Prioritization (POO-LPSP) method. By integrating an improved bio-inspired metaheuristic Parallel Osprey Optimization Algorithm (POOA), this framework efficiently solves complex LPSP models to minimize RMPSV and RMPSWV, thereby enhancing prioritization reliability. The practical utility and computational efficiency of the POO-LPSP method are validated through a numerical application focusing on a Generative AI (GAI) vendor selection problem. To extend, POO-LPSP can serve as a robust alternative to Saaty's Eigen system method for AHP applications.
tldr: This paper proposes a metaheuristic optimization method for priority derivation in the Analytic Hierarchy Process, applied to a Generative AI vendor selection problem.
motivation: The traditional eigenvector method for deriving priorities from pairwise comparison matrices has theoretical limitations, and solving the proposed non-linear optimization models is computationally complex.
method: The Parallel Osprey Optimized Least Penalty-Squared Prioritization (POO-LPSP) method integrates an improved bio-inspired metaheuristic algorithm (Parallel Osprey Optimization Algorithm) to solve the revised Least Penalty-Squared Prioritization models efficiently.
result: The method is validated through a numerical application on a Generative AI vendor selection problem, demonstrating practical utility and computational efficiency.
conclusion: POO-LPSP serves as a robust alternative to Saaty's eigenvector method for AHP applications, but it is unrelated to quantum information, thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Iterative Finite Element Approximation Of Non-monotone Semilinear Diffusion-reaction Equations
authors: Thomas P. Wihler Florian Spicher
